analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 91 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: One of, if not the best professor I've had in college. I learned a ton in this class and had fun doing so. This course was also not overly-demanding at all and I enjoyed it even though synthetic chemistry is not my field of interest within chemistry. Definitely take a class with Dr. Fostvedt if you can.

Best wet lab I've taken at UNC. To my knowledge, Dr. Fostvedt is the only lab instructor that actually releases the grading criteria used for evaluating each assignment. This course is 100x better than it used to be, and the pigment synthesis is actually pretty fun. Group research project at the end of the course with a poster presentation & paper.

Fostvedt is hands down the best chemistry professor at UNC. Shes so kind, good at teaching, and approachable. So reasonable with grades and classwork and takes feedback from students fullheartedly. An angel sent down to bring a little light to the hell that is the UNC chem department. If youre a chem major or need to take a chem class PLZ TAKE HER

Hands down my favorite chem professor so far (junior chem major). I love Dr Fostvedt so much. She cares about your learning, is kind, and is very accessible. She also wants you to succeed and do your best. Dr. Fostvedt will meet you where you are and try to help you every step of the way. Truly a wonderful human being--her kindness is contagious.

She is such a great person and great lecturer. She is open to feedback and is very passionate about her subject. By far the best chem prof I've had so far (chem major). She writes very fair exams and gives an extra credit question at the end of the midterms and final. There is also an opportunity to memorize the periodic table for a grade boost.

analysis.name: Prairie  Goodwin
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 119 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
Key takeaways so far:
1. answer keys frequently wrong
2. tests on content that is not taught during lecture
3. TA's are frequently incorrect during review sessions. Personally, I think its difficult to study when resources given are so obviously and drastically incorrect. Difficulty doesn't come from rigor of material, but rather these aspects.

The TAs don't know what they're doing but have large egos. Office hours are often a waste of time because most of the TAs are just as confused if not more confused than we are. The professor isn't receptive to feedback and lacks empathy. Tests are long and impossible to study for. Tests are also graded harshly. 

TLDR: Horrible in every aspect

This was the most discouraging class I've taken at Carolina. I felt completely unsupported and often left class feeling demoralized. The environment was unnecessarily harsh, and it seemed like the professor valued making things difficult over helping students learn. This experience made me seriously question pursuing this field.

The ratings speak for themselves. Don't come here rating her 5.0 just because you take 1-2 comp classes and a bunch of gen-eds, and have tons of time to go to office hours. The class isn't inclusive of people with really heavy schedules. Oh, and don't get confused by ratings from past semesters. Find a friend and compare how midterms have changed.

The professor doesn't teach how to write Java, making the class nearly impossible without prior experience, so you end up teaching it all to yourself. Exams are unlike reviews and worth 70% of the grade. Despite hours of studying, I feel set up to fail. I've always loved CS, but the lack of support and empathy makes this class deeply discouraging.

analysis.name: Govanni Granados
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great professor! He explained complex topics in understandable ways, which reflected in high class averages for all exams. For reference, my midterm scores were 102 and 96, with final exam 100. No access to lectures outside of class, so attendance is necessary for course content, but really you just have to show up. Would absolutely take again!

He's a great guy and teaches very well, with great tests. Easy to get an A in the class if you do all your homework and study well. Lectures were worthwhile to go to, and online resources also taught in similar ways to this professor. Everyone should try to get him for MATH 381.

Govanni is really understanding. If the class doesn't understand a certain topic, he is willing to walk us through step by step. HW and Exams aren't too difficult if you study, and exams are easier than the HWs. For the final he let us bring in one sheet of notes. Class is graded by two midterms, weekly hws, and a final.

He was my favorite professor last semester. He is a great option if you want to actually learn the material AND want to get a good grade. He is willing to help answer questions for anything and clearly wants his students to succeed. His tests were very fair and went over material we had learned.

Really great lecturer, goes at a good pace and explains everything really clearly. Only downside is that his final grading scale was not very clear, nor were our final grades released, only saw our grade in Connect Carolina at the end.

analysis.name: Gregory Kable
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 204 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I would die for this man. He is the nicest professor I have ever had. If you slightly pay attention in class and know the general plot of the plays and vocab you will get an A on the exams. Participants have many opportunities for extra credit through reading and answering mundane questions. Course journal is a free 100! He is very accommodating.

IF YOU ARE A FIRST YEAR HONORS STUDENT TAKE THIS CLASS!! super duper easy to get an A - literally just show up, submit the 3 assignments (only 3.), and give an ounce of effort when you do your scene panel. in class we just watched movies and read aloud scenes and chatted, but most ppl were just doing homework from other classes. highly recommend!

This class was probably the easiest I've ever taken, and Dr. Kable is so funny, caring, and supportive. Literally 75% of your grade comes from three journal entries that he grades super leniently on. The rest is participation and one "scene panel" that is a really simple acting project.

Professor Kable is genuinely interested in his students (he learned everyone's name in my 40-person class). I enjoyed his selection of plays, and most reading was done in class. He is funny, invested, and very professional.

Kable is such an amazing professor! You'll read a lot of plays, but as long as you show up to class, occasionally participate, and think about the material, it's an easy A. He's a generous grader and clearly knows a ton about the subject material. Take any and all of his classes!!

analysis.name: Gary Kayye
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 160 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Gary is an awesome professor! Most importantly, his class projects, whether on New Media and technologies or  Branding of Me, actually make an impact on the students life as well as the community around us.
This class requires you to blog a lot. A lot. Did I say a lot?  But he's clear about it upfront. And, it works.  It is a individual branding class so.

I took Gary because he was highest on Rate my Professor and it was the best decision ever. His lectures were very interesting and he was a very real person. He told lots of jokes and showed videos that made it interesting. There was only two assignments were we had ample amount of time. You work with a partner so its super easy.

prof kayye is an interesting guy. he seems very different than most others in the J school as he wants you to want to learn the material rather than force feed it. you can certainly get by with just sitting in his lectures and making a great grade in the class but, you get out of his projects what you put into them.

Great professor who clearly cares about what he's teaching. You don't have to take any notes or attend lectures to pass. The final for his portion of the class is super straightforward. There is one or two group projects for his part of the class which aren't bad at all but the rubric is a little vague and he barely gives out 100s for the projects.

analysis.name: Harry LLoyd
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Harry is new to the United States, but he is a kind, funny, and passionate instructor. He is understanding with his students, perhaps due to being a younger professor, and he tries hard to be friendly and engaging. There's a lot of reading, but you can get through it. Make sure to participate in class. He is a hard grader, but not unfair
He's a really great professor. He's pretty funny which makes the class enjoyable. He's obviously really knowledgeable and skilled at what he does, but still very modest and approachable.
Phenomenal professor, take his class if you get a chance

analysis.name: Jingfang Huang
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 86 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I dropped this class on the first day to switch to a different section. I had a very hard time understanding him. I was confused the entire class period. It took me an hour to realize he was trying to explain how to multiply vectors, a relatively easy concept. He also danced around questions when asked, instead of just giving a straight answer.

The syllabus of his 235 is unreasonable. Too many concepts he wants to cover, and there's even not one main textbook but only his OneNote, which is sometimes super confusing. He always wants to focus on something comprehensive, but it IS the instructor's job to lead students to dive into details all the time. Y'all should take 233 with another Prof

For M528. There are two sections for this course this semester. I was on the waitlist of another section for two months, from November until the waitlist was purged in January. So he was the only option left for me to take 528 with. He couldn't rephrase the concepts taught in 383 clearly. Thankfully this course has a tb, otherwise you'll get lost.

His class is super disorganized and boring. Though he makes the exams reasonable and easy, the contents of 235 are still heavy. He always emphasized on 'big picture', which sometimes confusing and useless. Overall, good teacher but not fitting to teach.

Prof. Huang is a very smart and nice man, but is a mediocre instructor. He constantly jumps around trying to cover multiple sections in a day, and gives very awkward answers to questions. However, he is VERY lenient. He let us redo our 2nd exam over fall break and dropped our 4 lowest hw grades which is nearly unheard of at UNC. Overall, he's ok.

analysis.name: Hill Taylor
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's nice and understanding when you have conflicts, the class itself is not difficult but he takes a long time to respond to emails and repeatedly shows up to class late. He would make updates an hour before class would start. Half of the assignments have yet to be graded this far into the semester.

Nice guy, the class is pretty easy and involves a lot of group work and class discussion. There's only three big projects and the rest is mostly discussions. The syllabus is a bit vague and he goes off topic a lot so if that bothers you should take this class with a different teacher

Dr. Taylor makes lots of jokes and is a very understanding guy. He teaches by digression but it is all relevant to the lesson. There are 3 projects that make up your grade along with two other minor components; participation (as long as you occasionally participate you get 100) and your journals which take 5ish minutes during class.

Dr. Taylor was an incredible teacher. He made english fun and enjoyable and understands that a lot of students already have a lot of work for their other classes. He is understanding if you have a conflict or issue come up during the semester. If you try your best, you will do great.

LOVEDDD Eng105 with Professor Taylor, as long as you do the work before hand, you will likely get a 100+ in the class. He's super chill and loves it when people participate and talk with him. He requires a lot of writing, but it's not difficult at all.

analysis.name: Herica Valladares
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: No required attendance in lecture unless you are worried about missing the notes. She is knowledgeable about her field and is an amazing class if you are interested in classics. As a non-history major got kinda boring. Easy grades, graded by a few in class writings, 2 papers, a midterm and a final. Midterm and final are nothing to stress over.

I loved this class. It was so incredibly chill; they just want you to learn. They send all test material out beforehand. Valladares was so kind. Her lectures could be a little boring, but it wasn't her fault; it's just that it was a Tu/Th class, and it loses your attention at some point. Overall, would definitely recommend for an easy gen ed.

She was very sweet and very passionate about Pompeii. Very easy tests and assignments, just make sure to put some effort into the 2 essays. Almost completely homework free, and prioritizes your learning over your grade. Unexpectedly interesting, easy, and professor Valladares is awesome. I would recommend this class to anyone

Had I known what this class would entail I never would have taken it. Your entire grade relies on two midterms and a final. Furthermore, Prof. V began to remove student's access to helpful study material (lecture videos) midway through the semester. Grading also takes a really long time, so I never really knew where I stood in the class.
Attendance isn't mandatory but such an easy class if you go. 6 participation in class writing assignments, a midterm, final, and a few essays. She's very understanding, highly recommend.

analysis.name: Hsun-ta Hsu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This professor was absolutely amazing. He has to be the best professor I have ever had. He had fun, engaging lectures and made occasional jokes that I enjoyed. Reading quizzes were all completion grades. No exams in the entire course. Final project was a group project that was very fair and they helped a lot with it. Please take this professor.

Nicest professor ever! He relates concepts to the current world and genuinely just wants you to learn. Very kind with grading and problem sets. Brought in some awesome guest speakers and is willing to help you. The best!

Outstanding professor with entertaining lectures! He did as much as he could to make every group's final project as fair as possible. I really enjoyed the class and made a lot of friends along the way!
this professor was genuinely the nicest person ever. the class itself was also pretty easy
He wants to give you an A, so let him

analysis.name: Sharon Holland
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Good professor. Graded on few assignments, which made the class feel low-stress. Mostly consisted of readings and lectures, and expectations were clear and manageable.

Professor Holland is a very engaging lecturer who does a good job of opening discussions to her students and challenging them to think critically. Her rubric is not always the most clear, and the class is a bit disorganized. Her TAs are very harsh graders, but Holland is the opposite. Little reading, non-mandatory classes, and a take-home final.

There were no traditional tests for this class; the two major grades for this class were the midterm and final, both of which were take home essays. The essays are based on readings that she assigns throughout the year, and the readings (if you choose to do them) are quite lengthy. That being said, I didn't read anything, but ended up with an A.

easy class but lectures were dull. graded on 3 essays and a final project. there was literally no rubric for anything which was kind of annoying but they graded easy so it turned out fine. easy focus capacity.

For 255. The class was super easy and as long as you put in a little bit of effort you'll get an A. The content and Dr. Holland's lectures were super interesting but because the class was so disinterested it felt hard to be engaged.

analysis.name: Harvey Seim
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Seim is SUPER kind and wants us to succeed. I am a biology major (took this as allied science) and HIGHLY recommend. Tests are straight from class and a study guide is provided. Homework is slightly difficult sometimes, but it's made by the TA. Content is interesting and I have learned a lot!

He is super nice and super invested in what he teaches. I learned a lot of interesting material. "Weekly" homework is easy, and tests are very straightforward. If you study the study guide and attend class the exams will be easy. The lectures sometimes felt like they were dragging or long, but overall easy class with a very nice professor.

Dr. Seim is SO sweet and his class was very interesting. I am an EMES major so that's why I found it fun, the lab is even better. Make a quizlet of the study guides and as long as you know the answers you will be fine. Take the homeworks seriously because they weigh a lot.

Prof. Seim is a good lecturer and he is really knowledgeable. The TA grades most of the work and helps make the homework and tests. Most of the testing material is pulled from the homework and the free textbook.

Nice guy but class was all auditorium lectures and graded nearly entirely by exams that were 100% fill-in-the-blank on very specific things. Very difficult tests for a 101 class. I did well bc I had prior knowledge but I certainly would not recommend this class to anyone looking for GenEds. If you're STEM take 401 instead and if not don't take this

analysis.name: Ivan Cherednik
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Math62H is ridiculously easy to get an A. Material is impossible to understand, but the final is take home and the projects are easy after help from the GRC. Homework is graded but not factored into final grade unless it helps your grade. Ivan is so smart it is mind boggling, however his accent and random trains of thought make it tough to learn in

He was a very tough grader. There was extra credit options on tests, but that was for a reason. Tests were so difficult that he had to give us the built in curve or else everyone in the class would have failed. The positive reviews are from the .1% of students who spend hours upon hours just studying for this one class. DO NOT TAKE!

Professor Cherednik was a nice and funny professor. He has an extremely thick Russian accent that can take a while to understand. He is too smart to teach a class such as MATH231. Had a weird grading scale that ended up making a lot of people have their final exam as 80% of the final grade. Overall, I would recommend with someone else if possible!

Cherednik was kind and good with email, but was difficult. His accent was thick and hard to understand since he didn't wear a mic. The homework was easy, had multiple attempts, but the exams did not reflect his lectures. If you take it, use CramBetter; it helped me out a ton! Overall, really really nice guy but really hard to keep-up-with :(

Do not take this course unless it is required. The professor has a very strong Russian accent, which makes lectures difficult to understand. On the first day, I was completely lost and could not follow what he said. However, he reviews material for the midterms except the first take-home exam. Later midterms usually have about four questions total.

analysis.name: irina kruchinina
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: If you are a stem major and don't have the mindset for creative thinking, unfortunately this is not the professor for you. Dr. I is very abstract and creative with her thought processes. To others, her guidelines appear to be vague and complex, but she wants to give you ideas and creative freedom. She is very caring and passionate.

her speech is very difficult to understand, and on top of the fact that the concepts are all very abstract makes her lectures very confusing. jumps between topics too quickly. the details of the performance requirements are usually incredibly vague and not fully explained until very close to the due date. take this class with literally anyone else.

Dr. I appears to be very caring and kind. However, I was very confused by her lectures. There are 3 major performances, but your TA gives good feedback on how to improve. This class was a nice brain break for me as a STEM major. I still didn't mind the class and would recommend it.

Gave multiple assignments over university mandated holidays, unclear assignment guidelines, excessive homework for a 100 level course. Currently have an A but not worth the effort. Professor is difficult to reach. TAs were the only saving grace for this course

Her lectures can be very boring and convoluted, and she also has a thick accent which can make understanding her a bit difficult, especially in the mornings. Otherwise, you can tell she's very into performance and analysis and if you are too she'd be a great professor.

analysis.name: Iris Fitzsimmons Christensen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Profe is amazing! Class is interesting, and she always engages with students. There is a LOT of homework and vocabulary in class, but the Spanish department assigns that, not her. Midterms and finals are difficult due to the amount of material covered, but profe always helped us with what to study. Go to her office hours as well!

Spanish at UNC is hard, but I would definitely recommend taking 105 with Iris! She's super accessible outside of class and genuinely wants her students to succeed! Be prepared to learn A LOT of content, but as long as you start studying for exams early, you can succeed in this class!
She's a very good teacher and explains tough spanish concepts very well. Her in class activities were always fun, and I've always felt prepared for the tests.

analysis.name: Isabella Hinks
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 80 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The lectures are very informative and she explains things very well especially if you are new to the topic. At first I did very poorly on the quizzes but after I went to tutoring with the TAs I did way better on the quizzes. I recommend going to tutoring right when you see yourself struggling and recommend it a bit more the office hours.

I came into this class with 0 coding experience and struggled to grasp the content often. However, the resources provided by the CS department are crazy. There is tutoring and office hours almost every single day (Sundays too!). 

Dr. Hinks is great, and she truly did everything (including omitting the late submission penalties) to help our grades.

she clearly wants everyone to do well in this class. turning EXs in before due date gets extra credit at the end of the semester, most missed quiz Qs often dropped, takes the time to explain things well. lectures can be a bit boring if you already know the content, but she is so nice and helpful! this class is so easy if you just put the time in

She is a wonderful professor and explains things very clearly. This class is hard so once you start to see yourself struggling on quizzes take advantage of the tutoring (this is what I did and it truly helped me). At first, I got 60s on the quizzes and after going to the tutoring with the TAs my scores went up to 80s/90s!

Class is well organized. But, if you've never coded, I think Dr Hinks is not the best teacher. Lecture slides are very high level w/ few examples covered in class. Quizzes are short so if you miss 1 section, its tough to do well. I found other resources to learn the content. She did adjust the final quiz/exam weights, which helped grades a lot.

analysis.name: Imran Rizvi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Rizvi is a very talented researcher and clearly has a lot of passion for the material he teaches. While his lectures sometimes seem a little out of order or repetitive, he covers most of the material he says he will at the start of the year, and his exams are very fair. One of the most passionate and easy to talk to professors.
Dr Rizvi is obviously very knowledgeable and incredibly passionate. He is my favorite BME professor I have had!

Dr. Rizvi is very knowledgeable about the subject. My main issue with the class is the lab reports, about half of them being full-length. I recommend going to office hours while doing them as the TA's will always find some points to deduct otherwise. Exams (including the final) are not bad, study diagrams and lecture slides and you're good.

I really enjoyed this class. He is very knowledgable and truly cares about the class's understanding. The only issue is that the class is somewhat disorganized with timing of assignments, and grading for labs doesn't seem standardized with TA's. If you don't pay attention, read the textbook instead. Tests are not impactful, and an A is 95+, not 93.
The best. He really organizes the class to ensure student's success. Truly passionate about the subject,  one of my favorite professors at UNC.

analysis.name: Inger Brodey
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I would rather retake Gen Chem, pull out my anterior cerebral artery, and lasso a bear with it than take this class again. Expected full-length novels in a week and acted like we only had her class. Gives zero feedback on assignments but continues to grade extremely harshly.

Dr. Brodey was very kind, and invited the class over to her house for dinner a couple times. She was nice to talk to, and I enjoyed the class a lot. She offered good feedback on essays when asked. However, the workload was definitely overwhelming at times. We consistently read 150 pages of dense reading for each class, or watched long movies.

professor brodey is knowlegeable, kind, and accessible. lots of reading, but to be expected for an english seminar, and definitely manageable. her grading criteria could be a bit unclear at times but she's always open to explaining! she even invited us over to her house for dinner, she's super sweet.

Professor Brodey is very kind and passionate, but the workload is overwhelming. Full novels in under a week and long films in one night made the class feel unrealistic with other commitments. Creative final project, but I wouldn't recommend unless you have lots of free time.

As a Jane Austen fanatic, I was very disappointed. I feel like we did 85% of the teaching. We had group presentations where we taught parts of adaptations or extra readings. Also, lots of group discussion. We read 8 books, so you had 150+ pages due every class, which was impossible. No rubrics for anything. Brodey was very sweet, though.

analysis.name: Isaac Unah
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Unah's a researcher, not a teacher. Late to every class, very unorganized, & falls way behind on schedule. He had an obsession with teaching us regression analysis (not in class description). The little amount he did teach, he was repetitive & didn't prepare us for the research paper or exam. We didn't learn for a month once. Wouldn't recommend.

You live by the test, you die by the test. I wish this class had more opportunities for students to demonstrate their knowledge on the law and court precedent. Instead 70% of the grade goes to two online tests with large multiple-choice sections. Unah is a very nice guy, but the laxity was too much. Class would begin far-later than scheduled.

Great professor, is engaging, and passionate about what he teaches.  He is a lenient grader, lets you know what is going to be on the quizzes, and he pushed the midterm back 3 times because the class begged him to.  He is a bit disorganized which makes it hard to prepare before the class. He did show up to the final late because of Canvas issues.

Dr Unah is a great professor. I think people need to give professors some grace. Unah is funny and caring. Definitely go to office hours and get to know him. He also has a lot of connections. If you're interested in law, take this. Easy A class - one midterm, 6 quizzes (drops lowest 2), a partner paper, and final. Exams are online which is nice

I love Dr. Unah! His style is not going to be for everyone, as you can tell from other reviews. However, if you can get past his high level of disorganization, his classes are really enjoyable. He has so much passion for his discipline, loves talking to students who are interested in law school, and is just a great guy overall. Would recommend!

analysis.name: Ian Williams
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Ian is one of the most friendly professors I've had. He engages students with class materials by asking relevant personal preference questions about pop culture. Plenty of opportunities to participate in class. 2 Essays, 1 group presentation, 1 exam. Essay and presentation topics were fairly open; he cares about what you're interested in and think.

He is a great man! In my opinion, the lectures are very irrelevant to the final. Our entire grade was based on 2 papers, a final, a group project, and participation, which scared me. However, he was a very fair grader and even curved the final, which I found to be difficult. Not an easy A class, but good. The final is over 700 pages of the textbook

very easy class and material. for all projects and papers the criteria is clear but the prompts are very open to your own imagination. he's very funny and engaging and you could just sit back and listen to his lectures and fully grasp the course content without taking notes

Ian is awesome - humble, hilarious, caring, and approachable. He deeply understands pop culture across generations and connects it to theories, inspiring us to think about the world through class concepts. He encourages discussion, grants lots of autonomy and extra credit opportunities. Genuinely cool prof who treats students as equal counterparts.
Enjoyed and learned a lot! Would recommend. Curved the final and graded fairly.

analysis.name: Ivonne Chirino-Klevans
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: literally 0 feedback on anything in a timely manner. also her quiz questions are very poorly framed and I don't even think she knows what she's asking on them. Ok professor and knows the material but is kind of just disconnected from the course and picks groups for you so your entire grade can literally hinge on a group at the beginning of the sem

If you read the textbook and study on your own, you should be fine. However, she told us just to study vocab and then only put 3 vocab questions out of 25 on the quiz. Her slides are also very unclear and she doesn't share them. Overall, not very clear or amenable.

Easy class, and is an approachable person in general. However don't even think about disagreeing with her views or questioning Academia even in a topic as unstructured as Organizational Leadership. 

Class is easy for sure. But the value is non-existent. She also struggles immensely with active listening in an online format.

Loved the fun interactive activities we did in class; however, she grades kinda harshly with vague instructions. Gave many groups mid 70s-80s on the final group project, which didn't have a rubric. Class quizzes seemed easy, but turned out difficult for no reason. The final was recycled from past quizzes, so that was nice. try to participate

Ivonne is a nice person, but I agree with the review that said you can't disagree with her or she may take it personally. The course doesn't encourage grasping content but more-so just memorizing vocab. Silly in-class activities. Final project instructions were vague and the rubric she used to grade it was never given out.

analysis.name: Joseph Telegen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is very passionate about teaching; however, his methods are not for everyone. He is very dramatic and at times a bit disorganized. He has a poor work-life balance, and talks a lot about it. While his train of thought is often heading to an insightful and interesting place, it sometimes gets lost on the way there.  Super easy grader.

Joe is really nice, and very accessible outside of class if you need help. This class is great if you want an easy A and enjoy talking about pop culture. He does go on a lot of tangents and I didn't really leave the class feeling like I'd learned much about writing though.

By far the easiest A I got all semester. He goes on a lot of tangents, but I tended to find them pretty interesting. If you're an English major or particularly care about learning about the field, maybe choose a different professor, since there were some days we straight up just watched TV shows in class that vaguely related to course content

Joe was an amazing professor and I would love to take his class again. You can tell he loves rhetorical analysis. He does bring up the TV show Succession quite a bit, as well as Kanye West, Taylor Swift, and Elon Musk. He is very accessible outside of class time, and he makes sure you know where and how to find him.

Joe is a nice guy, but rambles about unrelated stuff for most of class and frequently goes off track so I didn't get much out of his lectures. He is very friendly and tries to connect to students, but goes over the top sometimes. Almost all in-class work is group work, but rarely is it productive. He is a lenient grader and is very accessible.

analysis.name: Johannah Palomo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lots of reading and writing, and the class content is super boring. The workload seems endless and reading is very dense and confusing. Take this class if you truly love religion.

Professor Palomo was AMAZING! She is very kind and made the course engaging. The workload was manageable and assignments were graded fairly, but I still got a lot out of class. As someone who struggles with class participation, I always felt comfortable participating in class because she is so welcoming. I would take her class again in a heartbeat!

Johannah is an amazing professor! Attendance was mandatory, but you will enjoy her lectures. She is very funny and truly cares about her students and what she is teaching. I would take any class she taught! This was truly one of my favorite classes taken at UNC so far, and Johannah is one of the best professors I've had.

Johannah is amazing I would take any class with her. Exam and assignment expectations are clearly laid out, making it easy to do well. She also genuinely cares about her students and their success and well-being. Take a class with her!

analysis.name: Jason Roberts
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I honestly learned more in recitation than in lecture. He is not very engaging and can sometimes come off rude. First exam had a 63% average in the class and did not suggest any changes on his end to help our performance. There is definitely a way to do well in this class, but it requires a lot of effort outside of class.

For a first year seminar, class was difficult for no reason. Graded by a few things, so messing up on the exams doesn't help your grade. You never really know what to expect on the exams, so they were difficult. Not reading heavy but lectures are boring. Professor is nice but any other first year seminar would be easier.

would only really take this class if you are a political science major. i took this for the gen-ed credit and had a hard time. lectures are boring, Roberts moves through material super quick, and tests are relatively hard. you def can do well, but it requires A LOT of studying/work.

Class average on the first exam was a 63 and blamed it on us for not memorizing extremely obscure details. Class lectures are boring and unengaging and he often stops lectures to call people out for small talk.
2 papers and 2 exams. For a 100 level class you genuinely have to lock in, and the papers are graded strictly and if you do bad on one exam then your grade is predetermined.

analysis.name: Krysten Voelkner
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Krysten was awesome. Her class is environmentally focused, which is not usually something I would enjoy focusing on, but she ran it so well that I ended up liking it a lot. She encourages discussions/debate in class (especially materialism vs. idealism). If you are a reasonably strong writer, you will have zero issues and appreciate the discussions

Krysten is such a unique and interesting professor to have. She really just cares about you becoming a better writer, without making you jump through hoops. She is very clear on what she is looking for and will let you resubmit papers for a regrade if you are not happy. I think most people in this class will end with an A.

She was great, very approachable, an excellent choice for ENGL105. The class will be environmentally focused, even if you're taking a specific concentration of the class like humanities. I found her grading to be very lenient, everything I turned in was an easy A.

She is great. She's super down-to-earth, gives no tests, and pretty much grades all projections/essays on completion(I ended with a 100.0), as long as you put effort and follow her instructions. She focuses a lot on plants from various perspectives to teach class, so if you find that boring, she may not be for you, but definitely extremely easy A.
Her Engl105 is focused around environmental studies, which usually bores me to death, but she kept things interesting. If you're a competent writer you'll be absolutely find with her.

analysis.name: Kathryn Reissner
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took 418. She's super funny, lectures are engaging, exams are fair and not many other assignments. Her grading is good, nothing to complain, I would definitely take her again

Dr. Reissner was one of my favorite professors at UNC. You could tell how passionate she was about the content of the class and it made lectures so exciting. NSCI320 in general was such an interesting class, and she made accomodations for every student and truly cared about our well-being throughout the semester. She wants everyone to succeed!

Dr. Reissner is absolutely amazing! Her depth of knowledge in the subject makes her lectures very dense and informative. She is very good at explaining the material and always answers questions! Although the material is difficult, she really wants her students to do well! My favorite class ever at UNC- it inspired me to be pre-pharm! Amazing class!

Reissner is the sweetest person and amazing teacher. However, her tests are tricky because there is so much information and little guidance. Same goes with her papers-you never get a score back and have no idea how you did.

Professor Reissner is wonderful!! She cares deeply about her students success both in and outside of the classroom. Her lectures were very interesting. I would be excited going to her class. The quizzes and papers are not hard because she outlines the necessary information clearly. This is such an eye-opening first year seminar. I loved it!

analysis.name: Jodi Magness
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 98 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Definitely the worst class i've ever taken at UNC. Do not listen to anyone when they tell you to take this course for "easy" gen eds. Professor Magness has been incredibly inconsiderate given the COVID-19 pandemic. The TAs will literally perform surgery with your test responses to the broadest of questions. Also, the term paper was terribly graded.

Very well respected/famous in field, so that's neat. 3 midterms, 1 paper, 1 final. Attendance checks. Tests frustrating bc you are asked for 2-3 facts about each object, but TAs are only allowed to give you credit for facts Jodi has predetermined as the ones she's looking for. (My TA described guessing which facts Jodi's looking for as a crapshoot)

DO NOT take RELI 110 if you are just looking for your gen ed credits. PLEASE listen to me. I took this for the WB and BN credit. Whenever we thought we aced an exam, we got C's and D's because the TAs take off random, unnecessary points. The exams are very hard no matter how much you study. If you're only looking for gen eds, TAKE SOMETHING ELSE.

Magness is cool, but your grade depends on your TA, and if you need help, you go to them. Magness just lectures and makes the assignments. 3 midterms with 6 identifications and an essay. All given ahead of time. Term paper is tough because the lectures and tests cover different material. NOT AN EASY A. Lectures are mostly about history.

Prof. Magness is really engaging, and her lectures are very interesting for someone who didn't know alot about Jerusalem. She is knowledgeable, but she doesn't post her slides, so make sure to go to class. Also, the reading is ALOT for an IDST. Overall, this Triple I isn't that bad, but having interest in Jerusalem or history would be helpful.

analysis.name: Kristen Kucera
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Takes attendance randomly. 30% of your grade comes from the group research project, and groups are randomly assigned. Willing to help and gives extensions. The first exam was a little hard, but we were allowed a cheat sheet. The final was open note. She does grade the group project pretty strictly, so follow the rubric closely. Great prof!
I would take 273 with her if you can—great professor, clear expectations, and straightforward grading.

She is a good person but the class sucks. Its a lot of material that she does not really explain well. She will answer questions about it after though. She does allow extensions on a lot of the assignments. She is a tough grader especially on the one big project that is spread out over the semester. She is REALLY SPECIFIC about the grading for it

Dr. Kucera is an awesome professor who truly wants her students to succeed! She is very flexible with deadlines. Your experience in this class will HEAVILY depend on the group you are randomly assigned to work with for the semester (as this is a huge project worth a huge chunk of your grade). Ask questions when you're confused and you'll be fine.

Awesome, kind and very helpful professor. I met with her many times during office hours to get help with the group project. If you are assigned a good group then you'll be fine in this class. The first exam was a little difficult but we did get a cheat sheet. Second exam was take home. Took attendance one time the day before spring break.

analysis.name: Katherine Newhall
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Nice person, horrible professor. Can't lecture/teach for the life of her, tests have material that were never covered during lectures. Doesn't know what she's doing (didn't create class material, didn't create homework, lectures like she went over the slides the night before) and is only available two days of the week.

Honestly maybe not her fault since this is her first time teaching this course but awful. Did not teach half of exam 2 and has not curved it. Very disorganized, not responsive, overall just a difficult class. Self taught most of the material bc lectures were insufficient leading to poor grades. Avoid!!

This class feels hard if only listening to lecture, but if you keep track of the homework and try to really understand the material getting at least a B+ is def doable. Professor Newhall might not be the best lecturer but she's a really nice person, and she gave out curve at the end which makes 92.9 an A and 89 and A-.

DO NOT TAKE, never have I struggled in math as hard as in MATH-235. Never taught the class before so she could not do half of the problems in lectures. The tests are hard. They usually do not include the material given in the review sheets. The final had no review material, topic lists, etc. The labs aren't helpful.

Math 235 isn't an easy A and lectures can be hard to follow, but Professor Newhall is very responsive and gives a generous curve. The class is test-heavy, yet the exams are fair and one midterm can be replaced by the final. She also offers grade boosters like lab attendance and worksheets, though labs aren't very helpful, and grading varies by TA.

analysis.name: Karl Castillo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: GROUP PROJECTS (4). COIL makes class feel like 2 classes. Doesn't communicate well. Exams are niche and questions are worded poorly. Lectures are boring. Cold calls. Loved him for 490. Highly disappointed and frustrated with 441. Quizzes every class. Feels like he doesn't care about students and only wants to do his personal research.

Dr. Castillo is a passionate speaker. He is insightful and holds office hours and will work to make sure his class succeeds. I have taken 4 classes with him so far and plan to take more! There are also extra credit opportunities if you go to class.

Dr. Castillo really cares about his students' learning the material. There are quizzes in every class but they're open note. Even though there were weekly assignments, I didn't feel like they were busy work. He is very clear on grading and the class is well organized. I would recommend this class if you're interested in the material
This class was about corals and it was so interesting. There is a project, but the topic can be chosen for wahtever you want. As long as you try, you will succeed.

Professor Castillo is extremely intimidating and belittles students in class. He called out a girl for being on her phone in front of an entire class of at least 80 people. His lectures don't help at all and he pulls from a textbook that's simply too much to read for an entry level course. He is extremely unforgiving with grading/late work.

analysis.name: Kyle Cessna
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great professor who is passionate about material and intent on helping his students learn. Students could turn essays in again after reviewing feedback which was extremely helpful. Occasionally a little confusing with class schedule or due dates, but would always correct it and ensure everything was fair for students.

Mr. Cessna is very passionate about philosophy and managed to make a dry course relatively entertaining. You can tell he really cares about students and wants to see people succeed. His grading criteria is very clear and he provides constructive feedback on submissions.

I only took this course because of the major requirement but thought Kyle was a great teacher. I am not super into philosophy and wouldn't have taken this if it wasn't required, but Kyle had nothing to do with that. He is accessible and willing to work with you if you are with him. The grading system was slightly confusing but overall good prof.

analysis.name: Xinyun Liu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Liu is a very great lecturer who explains thing pretty well. His midterms and individual part for the final exam are easy. The common part of final exam is kinda challenging... but Dr. Liu's easy individual part really makes up for my bad grade in the common part. He is very accessible and really cares for the students. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!

Professor Liu was great. I loved watching him get progressively covered in chalk throughout the lectures. 

Seriously though, Professor Liu is a great guy and his lectures cover enough content so reading the textbook is unnecessary. My only note is that there can sometimes be a slight language barrier when asking questions.

Professor Liu is very caring and understanding. I struggled a bit for the exams but if you show up to class, pay attention, and start studying early you'll be fine. 
His lectures are great and really clear, and you can tell he cares about the subject and the class. Great professor, choose him!

Dr. Liu is a GREAT prof. He rescheduled two exams to fit classes needs, includes extra credit, and has great lectures. He is hilarious, and very good at explaining concepts. Highly recommend taking. If you pay attention, you will get an A.

Xinyun is a good time! Never read the textbook and was able to get all necessary content from lecture which typically ended early for time to ask questions about HW (or eat lunch early lol). He's funny in class and cares a lot. I can't recommend him more.

analysis.name: Saman Lagzi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Lagzi is awesome. Take him if you can. He is very passionate about what he teaches and truly wants to see the students succeed. Very clear slides and lectures. He answers his email in seconds and is very reasonable when it comes to giving you points back on exams. Great teacher but most importantly a great person.

Professor Lagzi is great. 403 is outside of my focus and Lagzi made it really straightforward and accessible. The exams are tough but if you build templates before you should be in a good spot. The group project is very important so make sure to spend real time on it. Homeworks were generally easy and Professor Lagzi cares about his students.

Professor Lagzi is incredibly caring. Many homework assignments that can take you hours to do, but it's pretty standardized across diff 403 classes. 2 midterms that were both hard and a time crunch, but the final is easier in comparison, all open note. Content gets easier later on. Group project takes a lot of time, but grading criteria is clear.

Saman is a great professor who cares about his students. I did not do as well in his class as I would have liked, but that's definitely on me. There's a big group project, homework might take a few hours, and exams are a little time-crunched. A lot of work is on Excel. Definitely pay attention during lecture and take good notes!

analysis.name: Lillian Zwemer
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 201 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr Z has some really hard exams and doesn't release them afterwards. She talks to you like a kindergartener and her slides are really convoluted. Good enough lecturer, but she doesn't annotate her slides much. The course is heavily credited on exams, and there are a lot of homework assignments that do not always feel relevant.
Zwemer is super nice, and 220 really isn't that bad of a class, ESPECIALLY if you take it after taking 103 with Ott.  Zwemer's exams are much more clear and about Biology than Ott's.

The content itself is easy, but her wording on exams is what will get you. Claims she has spent years studying people and knows what works best, but also constantly has errors in exams. INCREDIBLY passive aggressive and condescending when you ask questions. This class would've been so easy if I had taken it with someone else. Do not recommend.

She messes up at least one part of the lecture in every class, and she requires both in/outside participation. I also disliked how she does not release her actual exams, just scores. Instead, she schedules two sessions to 'view' your exam, which I have never been able to go to due to class/work conflicts. Avoid her class at all costs.

Several common phrases used in Lilian Zwemer's lecture:

"Let me see bababa...... So this uhhhh [insert structure here]'s function is uhhhh let me check my notes..... Oh yes! [Insert function here]"
"What a FUN question! I don't know the answer"
"Mea Culpa, andioop, I made a mistake in my lecture the correct [insert] should be[insert]"

analysis.name: Matthew Lockett
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 81 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He gives you all the tools you need to succeed, on top of some amazingly inspirational speeches at the beginning and throughout the course. Quite literally he has made me cry from how much he cares for his students. Absolute best chemistry teacher at UNC.

I waited a semester to take this course with Lockett because of his amazing reviews but I was incredibly disappointed. Expect to go over the easiest question in class 4 times only to open the HW to the most impossible unrelated questions. All the tests, including the final, are open note but he makes them very difficult.

Best professor I've ever had. His exams are hard, but he prepares you for them by giving you tons of practice exams. I could have failed every exam of his and would still rate him like this. Funny lecturer, understanding teacher, and overall great person. If you do bad on an exam DON'T PANIC because you always have the chance to replace it

Worst class ever!!! Everyone told me that he was a good professor, however he did not live up to my expectations. I genuinely don't understand how so many students like Lockett. Lectures were disorganized and didn't help with understanding the content. Half of his answer keys are incorrect. Tests are extremely difficult!!

Was so excited that I got into his class because of his 5.0 ratings but wish I took a different professor. Did not like this class, tests were hard and much different from the in class practice. He would say the test was going to be easier than practice exams and then it would be much harder.

analysis.name: Laura Ott
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 320 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Refuses to provide a copy of lecture slides, so half the class is scrambling to write down content instead of listening to what she's saying. Exam questions do not test on knowledge of content but instead are written to trick us. Median on the first midterm was a 74 AFTER 10 bonus points were added and 7 questions dropped (out of 27). Dr. Opp fr

Dr. Ott wants you to think she cares. However, that is only true for a select few. Very passive aggressive, not willing to answer questions, not widely accessible outside class, and relies heavily on peer mentors. Beware of "select all" questions with no partial credit and no low stakes practice for tests. Dr. Ott? More like "Dr. Opp."

Dr. Ott is one of the most condescending professors that I have had the unfortunate displeasure of taking a class with. The information of the class was bearable but whenever you need something from her, it always seems like she is talking down on you. If you have the chance to take a class with her, do yourself a favor and don't.

The course content itself is not hard to understand as a whole. However, Dr. Ott teaches the concepts in a nonlinear way that is hard to understand if you don't reorder it yourself. GRQs were a waste of time and lectures could be confusing at times. Pay attention to the lecture slides when studying. She is getting rid of cheat sheets soon - beware.

Does not seem to care about students. Extremely condescending, makes the class more difficult then it needs to be and also takes her bad mood out on students. Content is not difficult, exams are not necessarily hard but they are clearly meant to trick you rather than assess your actual understanding. Voice is really annoying.

analysis.name: Mariana Olvera-Cravioto
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It's undeniable she is a great person passionate about the subject and accessible outside the classroom. However I would not recommend taking this if you don't have background in stats or math. The lectures are extremely confusing and require you to know the material beforehand. Hardest tests ever. If you take 435 with her good luck you'll need it.

Lower averages than other sections. Failed several of her students. Insufficient prep materials for the exams. No recorded lectures. Exams were much more challenging than other sections. Homeworks take a ridiculous amount of time to complete. Professor has been falsely represented in her ratings. You've been warned. No curves when over half fail...

I had her for 435 and 445. I really struggled through 435 and her lectures started getting pretty confusing, but shes still an amazing prof and person. I'm half way through 445 right now and I do think it's a lot easier than 435 and I am enjoying my second class with her a lot more than my first.

To be honest I did not know what to expect with a 400 level class called Introduction to Probability but it was like two weeks of introduction. PSA that you need to do calculus in this course and I spent like 14 hours a week on this class. Go to class and do extra practice problems because honestly understanding the question is half the battle.

Professor Olvera is a genius and she is extremely well spoken when it comes to statistics; however, that does not take away from how difficult this material is. If you fall behind, it is almost impossible to catch up. I respect her so much as a professor and it is clear that she wants her students to learn, but be prepared to fight for your grade.

analysis.name: Maharshi Vyas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Vyas is a really cool guy overall. His lectures are interesting and it's clear that he is very knowledgable about the subjects. I took this class for an FC and it actually expanded my POV on a subject I wouldn't have otherwise studies. Prof. Vyas is great and this class is not stressful, a nice break from harder classes. 100% take again.

He is one of my favorite professors I've ever had! He's a super kind person and very clearly extremely knowledgeable on what he is teaching, and passionate about it. However, he still gives students ample time to discuss topics on their own, which is probably my favorite aspect of the class. His class Reli 388  isn't very work heavy either!

Honestly an amazing professor. One in class test that is graded well and showcases what one truly took from the class material. He is extremely accessible outside of class and so caring. Truly knows the content and welcomes differing ideas and opinions. I recommend taking his course(s) and if I can, I will again.

M. Vyas is a great professor! Super engaging during office hours and cares about his students ability to succeed. Had a small class cohort this semester but he's looking for new students to join and I would def encourage you to do so! His RELI 388 class has FC Global/Ethics and there's only one SHORT midterm exam. The rest is fun projects, etc.

If you are interested in learning more about Hinduism and Hindus as a diaspora I recommend RELI 281. We learned many interesting things about their history/religion/culture and how communities adapt to new settings. Prof. Maharshi is very nice, a fair grader, and all you need to do is read the material and participate to earn a good grade.

analysis.name: Miriam Watts
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Love Dr. Watts! She provides all her lectures on videos in case you ever missed information or want extra review. It is important to go to class due to graded participation assignments. She makes information really easy to understand though so just study hard for the tests because that is mainly what your overall grade is based off of.

The concepts are hard,but she teaches them in a way that make sense and her slides are very organized. I never read the textbook because she posts video lectures,and her tests are mainly on the stuff covered in class. There is only 1 assignment a week, 3 tests + final, and 4 group assignments. Dr. Watts is an amazing professor, take her if you can!

Awesome professor; really good at explaining complex topics and doesn't make her tests any harder than they needed to be. If you study the content, you'll do fine on the tests (which are all MCQ). The first unit is the easiest because it just focuses on neuroanatomy (the other units combine multiple body systems). Group project case studies are ok.

Without a doubt, Dr. Watts is the best STEM prof I've ever had. Her slides actually made sense (unlike so many other classes), she posts recorded lectures, and the exam questions are the fairest questions I've literally ever seen in my life. If you study for this class, you will do well on exams - the way God intended (even tho it's rare for UNC).

The content is moderately hard, and there is a lot of it, but she lectures very clearly and is engaging! The powerpoints and learning objectives have everything you need to know for exams, which are honestly very fair. Homework and other assignments aren't overly tedious. The only thing is that the polleverywheres are graded for accuracy.

analysis.name: Markus Nevil
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: In my opinion, this class needs to be entirely restructured. Very odd grading system, tons of group work, and zero real learning. Also, zero accountability for group members not helping. Basically, a high school science class. Despite Bio 101 being a pre-rec, we spend time in 105L learning 101L skills. Could be useful, just needs to be rethought.

Idk why Bio105L gets the bad rep. This class was super easy GPA booster. It's the easiest bio class I've ever took. The assignments didn't even take that long either. The only things that took time were the papers. But then again, they were group assignments and u r only responsible for one or two sections. Easy class. No final exam, just a paper.

Nevil seems great, but this class is the worst. Unsure if he set it up or was assigned to teach it, but it's the most nonsense class you'll ever take. Assignments take forever, are pointless, and have insanely confusing rubrics; it's a busy work highschool class. I don't get how this is considered a prereq because holy yap and time/energy wasted.

Dr. Nevil was great in 105. There was a lot of work to do every week but there were a lot of interesting topics. Due dates were clear and easy to keep track of. The rubrics for the projects were helpful and you can resubmit if you dont do well on the first try. Dr. Nevil was the the professor who did the lectures and I thought they were interesting

Dr. Nevil is kind, but the lectures are a waste of time. No exams, just a bunch of projects/assignments. Peer Reviews, discussion boards, and easy online video quizzes. Every week, there's a group lab report assignment. Annoying but easy once you get the hang of it. This class had so many assignments, but easy A. Good GPA boost

analysis.name: Zachary Nimchuk
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is super nice and so interested in CRISPR! There is 1 midterm and you get a cheat sheet. The average was a B+ and he gave us 2 questions back that people missed. Otherwise, the only other grades are a semester long group project and the "final exam" which is a prompt that you get ahead of time and can prepare. Definitely recommend this class.

Dr. Nimchuk has been by far the best biology professor I've ever had at UNC. This course was my absolute favorite this semester and I always looked forward to sitting in lecture. He is very knowledgable with the CRISPR-CAS9 system and has so much insight to provide. Everyone should take this class and witness how marvelous Dr. Nimchuk is!

The best professor I've had at UNC. Very clear on his expectations and willing to explain difficult concepts. The class material was interesting for people interested in genetics and molecular biology. If you read and understand the papers, you will do well.

Loved Dr. Z! His lectures were engaging and entertaining to learn from. He sent out a weekly email that outlined the class we had that week and showed how much he cared about us. This was a 1-credit seminar, but he's teaching a full course on CRISPR next semester which I would highly recommend!

Great professor and person. Very knowledgeable on the subject matter and cares about the students. Seems as though he wants students to succeed and learn from his class. I highly recommend his course on CRISPR if you're a science major and interested in genetics. Final project was a lot of fun.

analysis.name: Michal Osterweil
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 77 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. O is odd, but I do recommend her because she'll change the way you look at the world forever. This class can be frustrating at times in the way that's like those tiktoks where the girl is like "when a man has a thought I had when I was 7," but don't take it to heart if she comes off as patronizing because she really does just want you to learn.

Dr. O is a genuinely good person who cares about the class, her students, and the content. This being said, the class is semi-disorganized and can be redundant. Lots of reading, but you only really need to do it if you're doing the reading responses. Pretty liberal and not very open to other perspectives, so prepare accordingly. Go to office hours!

Dr. O is a great professor! The class itself was honestly not too bad, you just have to keep up with some readings (and you can honestly get away with not doing a lot of them). The tests were mostly short response with some multiple choice, but Dr. O and the TAs grade pretty leniently. Overall, fun and straightforward class!

We meditated before each class, which was kind of cool in my opinion. The course material is interesting and progressive, if you're into that stuff. The papers and exams were graded very leniently. If you can showcase within them that you did the readings / kept up with class, you will do very well. Attendance is not mandatory, but I recommend it.

Dr. Osterweil's class was definitely the most unique I've ever taken really - it is obvious she cares about the material very deeply and really gets you thinking. Even though the class could've been a bit more organized and straightforward, I really enjoyed the energy and knowledge she brought to the course. She's also very kind, open, and driven.

analysis.name: John Noonan
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Noonan is a truly a kind person, making an effort to remember your name and make 231 really entertaining than most sections. But most of us agree that he tends to ramble about things that aren't important to the curriculum at hand. the ULAs in recitation were def better at teaching than he was in general. also poll everywhere is used for attendance

Dr. Noonan is lots of fun! Teaching style could definitely be improved, but he's engaging and silly, and answers specific questions pretty well. I leaned HEAVILY on the ULAs in the class to actual learn material and prepare for tests... probably would've failed without them. Overall fun, but you're left to learn a lot of material on your own.

Professor Noonan is a great example of great person, somewhat lackluster teacher imo. He is lively and brings good energy to his classroom. However, his teaching is not my cup of tea. The material that is on exams is very different from what's practiced on homework/class. It was often "figure it out" with not much else for help. I felt unprepared.

Professor Noonan was such a great person and I enjoyed having him but the class itself was not the best. He was very all over the place and felt like we didn't have enough time to do anything. He is new though, so I think he's just getting the hang of thing and hopefully future classes will be more organized. I had to teach myself most material :(

I really like Noonan as a person and he wants the best for his students, his only down fall is the lectures. He gives a worksheet to work through and just gives the answers at the end of class. This was his first semester teaching here, so he was figuring out what worked along the way, so hopefully future classes will have more productive lectures.

analysis.name: Nora Hanagan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof Hanagan is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject matter, and she heavily encourages participation. She's a relatively tough grader as far as first year seminars go, but if you do the readings and put in some effort, you should be fine. The major grades are an in-class debate, short video, two reading analyses, and an oral exam.

Awesome professor, not too difficult. HEAVY readings and has textbooks, but can probably get PDFs. Main grade is a debate which needs a fair amount of effort but she gives class time, groups are random but worked out pretty well for our class. Fair grader, just put effort into your papers and reflections and in class writings and you'll do fine.

I liked this class. Lots of reading some required for in class assignments. She's a great lecturer so it made a class I was worried about more digestible. There's a debate at the end of the semester you might be worried about but it was pretty easy. Not a harsh grader either

I like her a lot, she is very sweet and caring. Flexible with attendance if you have a genuine reason you can't be there. her lectures are sometimes quite dry. Class involves a lot of group discussion so do the readings.

Dr. Hanagan is incredibly knowledgeable about American political theory and delivers lectures in a way that make the content digestible. There is a significant amount of content covered, so I would recommend doing all the readings if you want an A. She is accessible and helpful in office hours. Overall, I learned a lot and improved as a writer.

analysis.name: Ali Nezhad
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Currently taking for STOR415 (not listed on ratemyprofessor). Held class on Tuesday despite class being cancelled due to the winter storm (we were in condition 2 until 12pm, and he held class from 9:30-10:45AM). Holds quizzes throughout the semester, and makes you to stay in class 10 minutes late if you want a chance at completing the quizzes.

Took stor 415 with him, he made hardest exams and homework take forever to do. In class, he will give you the most basic examples, but then have the exceptional cases on the quiz and homework, where you have no idea how to even approach them. Lectures are super uninteresting.

Take discrete with him if you can! Great lecturer and tests were on homework problems or straightforward examples similar to those in class. He always wants you to participate and if you do sometimes he will give extra credit points on the midterms! Graded fairly and made discrete much easier to understand than most STOR professors do at Carolina
took stor 415 with him, this professor CANNOT teach

I liked him overall. A bit difficult but that's discrete, not him. Overall, he graded pretty leniently and I only got a B because I sold on the final (maybe not a good first semester class while taking 17 credits!) BUT that's more on me and I think if I had less credits and more college experience it wouldn't have been such a crunch at the end. W!

analysis.name: Natasha Parikh
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 128 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: super nice, class was rly easy, poll everywhere everyday, labs every week for completion, assignments every week for accuracy but super easy and using jamovi. take home quizzes, midterm and final. uses piazza for participation

She was wonderful. The course was structured where you watch lectures before class and do some compression questions (but that should take about an hour at most). In class we do review, poll everywhere, and work on assignments, which is really nice because you can get a lot of help from both Dr Parikh and the ULAs/IAs. Overall a great course!!!

Amazing Professor! She made retaking stats an enjoyable experience. The one downside I had with her is that she often would respond to emails very late, and many times she wouldn't even respond. But, it was not an issue as she was very welcoming and always had time before or after class to speak. I would recommend taking a class with her!

She is a great person! But on top of that this is the best class I have taken. The lectures are actually interesting and all test are take home and open note including the midterm and final. The only thing that you are not guaranteed to get an 100 on is the in class assignment but those don't really impact your grade. Take this easiest A.

Prof. Parikh is a great professor! 210 content was a bit dull just because it's statistics focused, but she made it as interesting as it can be. Easy A! Labs are automatic 100s as long as you try, and assignments are pretty easy. I liked how detailed instructions were provided. Overall, take it with Prof. Parikh.

analysis.name: Todd Ochoa
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 79 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Todd was a enthusiastic lecturer but sometimes did not explain the material in the readings well. There were lots of readings in this class - some of them were very dense. My TA broke down the material into manageable chunks that Todd lacked in lecture. Only 2 papers but weekly small writing assignments. Very low stress!

Passionate and caring professor. The small group oriented lessons implemented for this semester were a miss (especially if you're anxious speaking in a massive class hall). Class attendance is graded but may be *ahem* bypassed relatively easily with the check-in beacon system. Lots of homework is assigned, but was ungraded and therefore optional.

Awesome professor. Really knows what he's talking about is my favorite type of nerd/geek. He really does make the class engaging and provides nice discussions in class.
