There is a lot of material you need to read, however Ochoa does clarify ideas and concepts from them in his lectures. I would highly suggest taking this professor.
Lots of reading and writing and the contents feel super boring and dense. Plus, this class has high threshold (95%) for getting an A. Take this class if you truly enjoy religion.

Ochoa is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. Lectures were amazing and extremely interesting, class was fun and interactive. He makes very deep topics about religion and society very accessible to people of all backgrounds. I'm a CS major and Todd made me want to add a RELI minor. Not that hard if you just do the work and skim the readings.

analysis.name: Mike O’Sullivan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. O'Sullivan is my favorite lecturer at UNC. He is passionate and pretty funny, although self-deprecating at times. I liked learning how history is still very relevant today in stuff like politics. Few assignments, and most are completion/effort. There is a lot of reading, but take the time to go thru everything to ace the midterm and final.

Professor O'Sullivan gave detailed lectures and made sure to show every side of the various historical debates that we covered throughout the course. He provides good feedback on writing for history and is willing to talk and answer questions outside of class in general. He is very smart but also very down-to-earth, and kind to students.

Heavy on the reading, but very entertaining lectures, talks as if he is telling a story and is easy to learn from. Easily accessible outside class, very kind and very understanding. Encourages people with no outside knowledge to take the class. Highly recommend.

Hard to take notes on his lectures, it's a LOT in a short class period. Very story telling adjacent, so he's fun to listen to if you enjoy the topics. Amusing, very caring, chill professor. Very understanding. Graded on midterm paper and final paper, and a few reader response. Lots of reading and one group presentation.

Professor O'Sullivan is so nice! The course is easy overall: 3 reader responses, a map quiz, a mid-term, and a final exam. Don't stress if you are struggling, go to his office hours and he's always willing to help. This course is reading heavy and quite fast paced, so make sure you do your readings or else you'll feel lost in class

analysis.name: Timothy Ott
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Attendance played a big role in grading. Students were often asked to upload photos, which were then used to track attendance. The class felt quite boring, relied heavily on cold calling, and the slides were very amateur and could be much better. Overall, grades seemed to be based more on attendance than on actual learning or engagement.

Long cases and a quiz required for every lecture, were just a large amount of time and super exhausting. Ott is a good lecturer, however, the final project (which is a presentation) is a large amount of time and the average for the final project was a 75. I felt like it was hard to know what he was looking for since the TA graded our quizzes

I personally like Prof Ott, but know others who didn't. He's a tough grader, good lecturer and a nice guy. This course is based on 9 case studies with quizzes on each and a final group project. Grade-wise, it's 30% - Participation, 40% - Quizzes, 30% - Group Project. This class has a lot of reading, and if you do it, you'll do well.

analysis.name: Matthew Owain
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He sent me this email without knowing I am mentally ill and have been struggling with school. "I noticed that you were absent on the first day. Please drop as soon as you can. As policy, I do not over-enroll and the waitlist is 18 people deep and I am sure others would love to join this class." I dropped because of this. I found this to be rude.

I took this online/asynch over the summer and it was just okay for if you want to actually improve your writing. Not much work, easy for a quick credit or A. His videos were short, simple, & a bit awkward. He gave basically no feedback (it all came from our group mates) and the canvas was a mess. Decent bit of reading followed by peer discussions

Prof Owain is amazing, super enthusiastic and cares a lot about students. He fosters a safe environment in class and makes students feel comfortable sharing their thoughts. The assignments are really enjoyable and you edit them as a small group with peers. Pro Owain gives incredibly thoughtful feedback and is all around great, cannot recommend more

Very chill professor, highly recommend taking a class with him. Participation matters a lot, but it is easy to talk in class. Three papers and one final group project. He cares a lot and wants to see you succeed!

Take Professor O'wain! In ENGL 138, there were 3 easy papers, 1 final group project, and participation (30% of grade but just talk once or twice a class you will be fine). I enjoyed coming to class everyday and highly recommend taking any class you can with Professor O'wain!

analysis.name: Max Owre
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 63 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I am someone who loves all of my history classes. However, this was unlike any course I have taken prior (of which there are many). Grand total of 2 assignments graded by LDOC, insanely tough grader (free write exams - 45 min only), and unclear grading criteria. I literally had nightmares about these exams and almost didn't make it out alive.

Max gets so disorganized that it's hard to understand the point of the lectures. He gives no context for a lot of it, ultimately making it hard to understand for a beginning history class. All of the grades are based on the TA's, so you better hope you get a good one. I felt like getting an 'A' was practically impossible, even while going to hours.

I feel set up for failure in this class. I want to stay on top of the readings, but he doesn't post them for class ahead of time or even for weeks after the fact. Also, engaged activity reports  dumb. I go to every class and recitation, but still think the best possible grade I can get is a B. I feel like I work so hard but it doesn't even matter.

I wanted to like Max and this class but I just couldn't. His lectures are overly verbose and since he slacks on posting the readings, I was constantly confused about the material. It is obvious that his other job, exec. director of Carolina Public Humanities, is his priority and he doesn't make enough time to be an organized/effective professor.

Professor Owre was definitely very nice but the damage that I think is about to occur to my GPA is a major thorn in my side. Although that is mostly due to me TA (who pains me even more), the way the class was structured didn't help much either. Essentially, unless you're purely interested in the topic, I wouldn't take this course.

analysis.name: Vladas Pipiras
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Professor Pipiras was great. Although teaching seems very fast paced content coverage was excellent.
If you do put time in you will definitely get an A . Extremely easy tests and if the entire class is not doing good in it he reduces 0.5 points instead of 1 point for every wrong question. Very easy going grader .
Recommended for everyone.

Professor Pipiras is excellent and easy to communicate with! Sets clear grading criteria, has well-prepared documents, and gives moderately hard midterms. STOR 120 is not a very challenging class and you get what you pay for.

If you're thinking of taking STOR 120 over STOR 155, I would take 155 instead if you have little to no coding experience. Weekly labs and homeworks take about 2-3 hrs each. His lectures consist of him doing the code and you copying it down but fairly quick. He is a nice guy but overall goes quickly and lots of homework.
Professor Pipiras is very kind and understanding. He uploads a lot of useful material on Canvas for students to use. The class is well-planned.

This is a good class. It is a little difficult for those without much coding experience. However, the professor makes it easy to learn and as long as you are being diligent and learning, it's great. Grading is pretty chill and a lot of boosts come in later on. Prof. Pipiras is decently lenient on grading tests which helps a lot.

analysis.name: Oluremi Abayomi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 115 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Beware of this class! It is insanely challenging for an intro-level course. There are no HW/lab drops or curves. You could be on your deathbed and Dr Remi still would not give you an extension. Never answers emails and talks down to you during office hours and when asking questions in class. Goes indepth on easy concepts, but breezes by hard ones.

This class and Professor Abayomi's teaching was not very intuitive for someone who doesn't have any coding/limited stats experience. It isn't necessarily extremely challenging, but I would recommend taking this class when you have a lot of time to rewatch Abayomi's lectures and dedicate to the labs. He is funny and friendly, but pretty strict

The class itself is useful, but the grading was unnecessarily nit-picky. The professor was egotistical and unwilling to answer any questions or provide any sort of help. They spoke with an air of superiority and disrespect that I've never received from any other human being. I've never cried so much over a class. Do not take this class.

This class is just a cheap knockoff of UC Berkeley's Data8—he's stealing their work word by word and claims it as his own. At times he would switch the states from CA to NC to not make it as obvious. If you want to get a feel of how the class would be I encourage you to look it up, and practice. You'll pass the class with flying colors!

Dr. Remi was a very thorough teacher but was very condescending as a professor. He had very little patience and was rude to students on occasion. While his lectures were thorough, he spent a lot of time explaining simple concepts that everyone already knew.

analysis.name: Patrick Vernon
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Not sure why these reviews are bad when PV is really chill. His lectures can devolve into him talking in circles for a while, but the classwork (a few canvas quizzes/discussion posts) and final are easy enough (open note/internet). Professor Gong was one of the kindest professors I have ever had. She is very accessible outside of class and she genuinely wants to help you succeed. review_highlights.comment: I seldom post on RateMyProfessor. But Prof. Warren deserves this. He is inspirational. Period. Does an exemplary job of breaking down those tough acid-base questions. He's also very friendly. After all, it's a Chem class at UNC, so be ready to read. But Dr. Warren is always there for you. To me, he's a Chem god. Reason why I'm now a Chem major.

He's so passionate about chem and has a molecule of the day, that said the chem department is evil so you probably won't do too well on exams. Lecture can get boring but I think that's honestly any chem lecture. Use your resources.

As an otherwise straight-A student, this class butchered my mental health. The tests didn't reflect the class content, which I thought I understood; I did well on daily quizzes but not on tests. Warren was best choice of 3 profs, but department is bad, no curves or EC. I hope no one ever has to take it online again. Ended w/ a 79.3... so annoying!

He messed up our final grades and stressed an entire class of student out telling us our grades were wrong. To add, the test average was terrible and the class in general is a risk to take. Its not even a hit or miss with this professor, it is simply a miss. You will do poorly and that is a promise. Good luck :)

I don't post on RMP often, but I think Dr. Warren deserves it because he is a professor who will listen to you and readily answers your questions even outside of class. He once stayed on for a whole hour after class to explain chemistry concepts to me and a few other students. Therefore, I think you will have a better chance of succeeding with him.

analysis.name: Tia James
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very kind and well-respected within the department. The class is fun and I learned a lot. Tia is hilarious

This is by far one of the best DRAM classes that I have taken at UNC. Tia was kind, understanding, and not to mention incredibly talented. I equate her to the raise your yayaya lady because she is a magic worker with her notes and direction. Would 10000% take again.

Such an amazing artist, performer, and mentor. She only asks that you come to class and put forth the effort, so there's not that much required of you time-wise, but you will learn so much! I left this class feeling fulfilled and with skills that I will always remember. Tia is wonderful.

Very passionate about Voice and Speech and an experienced Broadway actor who really wants her students to go for it. All grading is based off of your performances in class and three small (1-page) papers due at the end of the semester. Highly recommend for anyone passionate about acting, and looking for how to start using their voice fully!
Literally the best professor and mentor. Tia is so caring and creates a classroom that feels like a family. I learned and grew so much in this class. One of my favorite classes at UNC by far.

analysis.name: Ryan Urquhart
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The other reviews aren't wrong, he definitely gets cross with the class sometimes. However, he did a good job of putting us in an entrepreneurial mindset and I got more out of this class than I was expecting. He also offered to write us a LoR for grad school which was unprecedented. Was he my favorite prof? No, but he far exceeded my expectations.

Amazing professor. If you're struggling in this class, it's not on him it's on you. He's tough, blunt, and expects you to act like an adult. People who complain are just soft and not ready for real expectations. If you can "handle" honesty and want to actually learn, take his class. Highly recommend.

I read the comments and had some apprehension coming into the class. I was amazed about how the comments were totally wrong. I'm a Jr and many of the ppl were Sr. who were complaining. All you had to do was come to class, complete the assignments. He was always available to meet via zoom, b4 or after class. Don't pay attn to the crybaby comments

This class was a huge waste of time. I heard that 382 with other professors is actually really helpful but I feel like I didn't learn anything. he was not clear at all on what he wanted and graded harshly. Didn't learn much he seems like a nice guy but takes himself too serious and doesn't teach any material. You have to cheat on quizzes due to ts

Super student‑focused. He invited feedback throughout the term and actually used it. His real‑world examples helped the material stick, and he made sure everyone participated. Would definitely take his class again. To stay in the loop, you must come to class.

analysis.name: Katherine Turk
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I didn't mind prof. Turk's lectures, although there is little to no information on the powerpoint slides so you really have to do your best taking notes. the main thing is that the TA grades every assignment in this course (final too). Even though the recitations were decent, it's like she refused to grade anything 100 (ex-4.8/5 participation)

great lectures, but they were scripted. accessible outside of class in office hours, but the TAs were the ones responsible for your entire grade. 3 short papers, midterm paper, participation, and a final comprised your entire grade; people complained about their grades from TA but I think they were fair and expected college level writing.

She reads lectures from a script in an immersive, storytelling style. Barely any details on slideshows, so prepare to listen and take notes. TAs do the grading for the essays you write. It feels like the grading criteria were not clear. Prepare for boring essay prompts. The lectures are 2 days a week, and the recitation is once a week.

Material was simple and interesting, but lectures were read off a script. Prof. Turk isn't very involved outside of lecture. The reason the class was more difficult was due to the TAs. TAs consistently gave specific and harsh feedback, making it hard to do well on the 5 essays we were graded on. Recitation participation was the only other grade.

Turk is a good professor and accesible for office hours. Lectures were interesting as well as content. Although all of the assignmnets were short papers with such broad and confusing prompts. It felt like even though I knew exactly what the content we were learning was, my grade wasnt reflected because the essays were so difficult.

analysis.name: Uffe Bergeton
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr Bergeton clearly cares a lot about the content but his lectures were not very captivating as someone who didn't already have a passion for the topic. I did enjoy the freedom in the final paper which allowed me to dive into really any aspect of Qin and Han history/culture. If you already know you love the topic, you'll enjoy this more than I did.

He definitely knows what he's talking about, but is terrible at teaching a simplified version of it. He goes off on really long unrelated tangents and is generally confusing. Definitely go to office hours because he is picky. Not to mention, he is white but claims to be "Chinese" as a result of marrying a Chinese woman.

There are quite a lot of readings, but they all relate in a way and most of the readings are online. 2 essays, one being the midterm, and the final being a 10pg paper along with a 5 min presentation. He is a very generous grader and the lectures were pretty interesting. He holds office hours for essay critique so you can score better on the essays.
hard course but he is a nice guy.the materials are hard though, i don't know the stories in the slides even though I'm a Chinese

His lecture is dry and boring. He wants participation but belittles students' opinions that don't align with his. He has a very Euro-centric view on eastern history and culture. He often suggests that because a student doesn't speak English natively, they aren't good at writing in English. But he does give extensions for papers.

analysis.name: Elaine Townsend Utin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: AMAZING! Elaine is a true gem and I would HIGHLY recommend anyone to take her class. It is full of so much helpful and important information and she has passion behind everything she does. She is also super compassionate, and understanding of the chaos that was 2020. She held plenty of spaces for healing and for growth in combination with learning.

As an Education Professor Elaine really knows how to effectively foster a nurturing learning environment where everybody feels heard and respected. She is sweet and fun and lights up every class with her bright attitude and passion for what she teaches. She may honestly be too good for the classes she teaches. She takes radical pedagogy seriously.

Profe is amazing and a true gem at UNC. Her class is so interesting and a must take for any Latine person at UNC. It is a great class to explore your own identity and understand the world around you. Profe creates a safe space for people to be vulnerable and honest about their experiences. You really begin to feel at home in class.

analysis.name: James Umbanhowar
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Terrible.  Not even worth going to class.  I started reading the book before the class lectures and I started to think I could have taught the class better than he did.  He stutters a lot and spends the vast majority of the time talking about simple concepts and completely avoids the nitty-gritty details.  I also hated his voice.
Absolutely terrible.  Lectures made 0 sense. The recitations are the only thing that  saved me from failing

It is true that his lectures are a little vague and he speaks really fast but there is a lot information that he has to cover in a small amount of time. He tries his best to be helpful and make the class interesting and overall is not a bad professor. The class is tough but the exams are not impossible and the curve is usually pretty good.

Umbanhowar's lectures are worthless. He stands up there and discusses vague examples and graphs, and doesn't have a clear point. It's better to just read the textbook to understand the material. The tests aren't too hard and are curved ALOT because everyone does poorly. I would stay away from him and his poor ecology teachings.

You definitely need to have a good understanding of stats to take this class (and understand it). You can get by with all of the assignments by going to office hours and simply doing the assignments (those are 80% of the grade and no exams), but you won't really understand it without a baseline understanding of stats.

analysis.name: Beril Ulku-Steiner
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Had a phony and fake nice personality in lecture but if you approached her one on one, she was inflexible both in her availability and in her willingness to help outside of class. She assigns an case study paper with vague and unclear parameters and expectations, and she has questions on the test from videos we watched in class weeks earlier. SUCK!

Dr. U-S will come to class every day cheery and smiley but DONT LET IT FOOL YOU. It is mandatory to go to class even though the way you will learn the material is purely through reading - she does not help. She will assign a group project and about 11 pg paper but don't count on a good grade, she'll rip you on both no doubt. Tests are ok if you stu

She smiles a lot; don't let it fool you.  Instructions for things are completely unclear.  EXTREMELY harsh grader, tests on things that we never talked about in class.  Scope of information way too large.  Extremely picky.  She was late to every meeting I had with her (meetings that she required), didn't show up, or just postponed them last minute.

Although she was a bubbly professor at 8 AM, I learned very quickly that turns into a very condescending demeanor. She grades incredibly tough and does not give good feedback. It's really disappointing considering how much I was looking forward to this class. The lectures were mandatory but not helpful, pretty much taught myself all the material.

If you can avoid taking Professor US for Abnormal Psyc (or any class), then PLEASE DO. Horrible professor. Ridiculous grader. The group project and accompanying paper was a complete joke, as she graded unfairly, extremely harsh and her rubric was unclear. Don't let the happy demeanor fool you. Also, 1 unexcused abstence failing attendance grade.

analysis.name: Monica Lopez Vazquez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I loved her so much, I am pretty sure any exams/assignments are not created by her but by the department she just grades them but they are relatively easy. Class participation is a grade and she cold calls a lot but is forgiving if you dont know it. Highly recommend!

Loved Monica, can safely say that she can write me a recommendation letter in the future! She is so kind and made me happy to walk into her class every single day; I could not have made this first semester without her.

She made what could have been a boring grammar pre-req fun and she pushed us a lot. Definitely an amazing Spanish professor. Tests were tough but she gave us a huge extra credit at the end which helped a lot.

Very very nice and helpful. She genuinely cared about you and your grade and was accommodating. She was not intimidating and would help if you were struggling. Try to do most of the readings before each class though so you don't get lost.
Monica is a great Spanish teacher. She's super nice, open to questions, and helps you with mistakes instead of looking down on you for them. Make sure you come to class prepared though.

analysis.name: Peter Uhlenberg
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Overall his class is very enjoyable, he makes the class very interesting. Although the class might seem very easy watch out! His exams are very detailed you have to really know it all. A lot of reading, in the book and articles he assigns. Overall I liked him

analysis.name: Daniel Velasquez
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: So the class is history focused but on top of that you get other stuff. Basically lectures give you history overview and then the other assignments provide examples or let you dig deeper, like reading annotations on a website called Perusall. It was actually very interesting and the Prof was constantly engaging with us even though it was all online

Professor Velasquez challenged us to learn the course material on a deeper by giving us a variety of ways to interact with the content (movies, primary source document discussions, essays, podcasts, poems, music). He also presented historical events from many different perspectives, allowing us to have the full picture on topics we were discussing.

He explains class topics really well, it makes class interesting. There are a lot of readings but nothing extremely hard. Also really important to take lots of notes in class for all quizzes and exams.

Very good class and experience with Prof Velasquez. I only took this class to satisfy some requirements but ended up finding it very interesting. He was also very nice outside of class and provides help with papers

Prof. Velasquez is nice and knowledgeable. My first LTAM class, but I'm going to try to take more now since I enjoyed it. It's an overview kind of class but you kind of get a sense of what it's like in Latin America even if you haven't been because of all the media he uses. Take notes in lectures and post some comments to participate you'll be fine

analysis.name: William Lassiter
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 102 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: In his class currently and really enjoy it. Attendance is not mandatory. The tests are lengthy but doable if you study. You also get a two sided cheat sheet for each exam that you can use your ipad to make. He is very accessible and always willing to help you go through a few practice problems in office hours which has helped me a lot.

Dr. Lassiter was an engaging professor. Homework was weekly (sometimes he extended deadlines) and manageable. The exams were a bit long so it will be hard to finish in time if you get stuck, but most if not all of it is addressed in lectures or practice exams, so I would say they are fair! Although I didn't go to office hours he encourages us to.

It was shocking to see bad reviews. He cares for the material, being a teacher, and seeing his students succeed. He has very dry humor but it works for a stats class. The lectures and homework build effectively for midterms and final, and he allows cheat sheets. Attend and do the work on time, the material will stay fresh. I can't recommend enough.

Amazing clear lectures. Opportunities for extra credit for showing up to class (bonus "quizzes"). Homework is manageable and we usually go over a problem the class votes on. Exams are fair and the practice tests prepare you well. Show up to every class and pay attention and you should do well. Prof Lassiter is good at answering questions too.

Just go to class for 2 points to your final grade thru random bonus quizzes(completion). The hardest problem of the HW was usually gone over in class so those were pretty chill too. Exams are super fair, and there were points back for a hard problem. Office hours were really good as well. Overall, nice professor and an interesting class.

analysis.name: Wendy Weber
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 70 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The best teacher at UNC i think. Took her English 105 class T/Th and was never actually in class for longer than 30 minutes. She lets you go early every single day. Has way way less bs assignments compared to other English teachers. Wendy is the homie, take her

Doing the readings before class will make you do just fine. Most of them are short, but we also read 2 books during the semester. 1 open topic paper, 1 group project, 1 midterm, 1 exam. A few discussion posts and attendance checks. Very easy and to the point class. I would take her again if I could; she is very kind!

BRO she had a vendetta against me because the only one who would get points taken off for stupid things. I met with her multiple times and she never changed how hard she graded. For example i said, "amount of people" and she said "you need to put number of people", and proceeded to take off 2/12 points... idk I was the only one with this problem

Professor Weber was so nice and a really chill ENGL 105 professor! She was a really chill grader and I easily got a 99% in the class. If we had a break or long weekend, she insisted we didn't do ENGL 105 work. Overall it was about 2 essays and 2 presentations with little assignments throughout the semester. She never took attendance either.

Dr. Weber was a great professor for ENGL 105. The class was three units, each with two small assignments and one slightly longer paper or presentation. Nothing required too much work, and she was reasonable with time to do work in class. She rarely took attendance, and didn't mind if you missed more than the allowed number of classes.

analysis.name: Abbey Warchol
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took EURO 159 when she was the teaching assistant. She is an extremely tough grader, and the rubric and expectations were often unclear. A lot of classmates ended up receiving lower grades than they thought they would. She's knowledgeable, but the grading felt inconsistent and it was hard to know what she was looking for.
They were super sweet when I took them last semester. Grading was kind of unclear, but also typically pretty easy. Really kind, was fun to have recitation with them!

Taken Abbey's classes for two semesters: TA in History 140(A-) and lecturer in History 130(A). Genuine about her interest in African History. Attend every lecture and actively participate. Helpful after class to review essay prior to submission. Grade is based on essays, participation, and a final group presentation. I am a STEM kid and did well.

Abbey was a great professor! She is very caring and did well with lectures. The class content was interesting and the discussions were engaging. 1 class per week was dedicated to student discussions which helped us better grasp the material. The course was graded based off participation, 2 papers, and 1 final group presentation.

analysis.name: Xinlin Ma
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's just professional and cares about students. She made things more flexible for students even during a hard time. I got more feedback than I expected as a junior. I will say take her class again!

She's the nicest professor I've ever met at UNC! She hopes students can learn from the course and makes the course as easy as possible. The topic is interesting and we have lots of case study about different worldwide cities, such as Chicago, Beijing, etc. She is very reachable after class. I will definitely take her class again.

She was always available to help and had the best, most welcoming attitude. She tried to make learning the material fun and enjoyable, and I believe she succeeded. One of the best professors I have ever had. She cares so much about her students and her field.

She cared about her students and was very enthusiastic about teaching. Attendance was not taken and the class was graded by 7 short open-note quizzes, a presentation, two papers, and a final. All were very easy.
She's very kind and sweet, and always willing to help her students with anything.

analysis.name: Xingyu Cheng
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: It was clear that he had not taught for long, as he struggled a lot early on. His teaching got better over time, and he has office hours sections where he will sit and explain material to you. The first midterm was incredibly easy. The second midterm was a lot harder, but still chill if you study hard. Final is demonic, but he curves accordingly.

I left this class most days understanding the material! He starts with easier content and then builds on it so we have the foundation to understand harder concepts. Some proofs can be a little abstract, but lots of practice can help you be prepared for tests. His study guides were helpful but looking up other practices can be helpful.

Tiger is a really funny and patient professor! He is very approachable and wants all students to do well in his class, but sometimes his explanations were hard to follow. Reading the textbook is optional, but I would highly recommend reading it + doing the practice problems if you want to do well in the class!

Office hours and in-class questions were available and very helpful. The second midterm and final were more challenging than the first test, but he curved generously at the end. The textbook aligns well with the course material and is a useful reference

At the begining of this class he did not really know how to teach well, but as the class went on he got better. There are 3 exams, homework due usually every Wednesday and a final. On exam 2 and exam 3  we got opportunities for extra credit which are the harder exams that really helped my grade. If you pay attention to lectures you will be fine.

analysis.name: Yuqian Xu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She's a really good prof, the material is fairly easy and up until the final its pretty fair. The final was painful also she puts in grades extremely fast (same day we took the final) the final was really hard so just prep for that. I did not hence the grade (had an A all sem)

Yuqian is a great teacher and person, but I disagree with other reviews. Class is extremely test-heavy and the final was surprisingly difficult compared to other exams and course sections. Final dropped my final grade 3 thirds of a letter grade.

Dr. Xu truly cares about her students! She teaches at a very fast pace so we always get out of class early. She's very eager to answer questions and make sure students are successful. She also is open to helping students in non-class related things

Professor Xu is a fun and engaging professor. Her class covers all the content you need to know and I felt I had everything I needed to thrive. Class consists of problem sets, 2 midterms, a final, and a group project. the final was the hardest part of the class, but overall, I enjoyed this course and would take Professor Xu again.
Everything is extremely fair, give feedback real quick. I am not a math person, but I did better than I thought in this class. My favorite professor!

analysis.name: Colin Wallace
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 198 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Wallace is very passionate about his field, and he makes his lectures engaging. The class content is also very easy; if you have even a little bit of experience in anything STEM-related, you will do well in this class. The homework assigned is busy work but is definitely manageable. Attendance is required and can affect your grade.

Dr. Wallace is such a beautiful light in the physics department. I can tell her really loved trains as a kid. And planets. He has a zest for physics that no one else on earth has. He lectures beautifully and in another life was a game show host. His exams are fair and he truly wants you to succeed.

There was a lot of material and a lot of graded things to keep up with outside of class like warm ups, homework, and lecture tutorials. Attendance is graded and exams were harder than anticipated just because of how much material there is. Be prepared to memorize lots of concepts, but you can tell Prof. Wallace loves what he does.

This class is so much more holistic than just aliens! Learning about atmospheres, rocks, using formulas. You'll enjoy this class if you want to a little bit of physics, chemistry, biology, math, geology, etc. Sometimes I didn't feel that his lectures prepared me for the work, but overall, he was an enjoyable, engaging professor.
I received a good grade in Collin's 115 class. My experience was filled with frustration. Wallace contributed to instruction disparities, and the way he handled student concerns was unprofessional.

analysis.name: Xiaoming Liu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Xiaoming is a kind professor who is very passionate about what she teaches. She is slightly disorganized, and slow with grading, but she makes it relatively easy for students to succeed. She doesn't take attendance, and it's not necessary to come to every class.

Xiaoming as a person is a really nice lady but as a teacher, leaves much to be desired. Attendance isn't mandatory so only about 40% of the class shows up on a regular basis. I attended every class but didn't get much out of it. I wondered "why am I here?" The slides are boring and can be accessed online. Not a terrible class but needs improvement.

Xiaoming is extremely sweet and approachable. She understands that it is an intro level class that most people are taking for gen ed credit and even tells you that reading the textbook is not necessary. Her only grades are two midterms, the finals, and participation so it is essential you study for tests, but overall not a hard class.

Xiaoming is a sweetheart. She is really kind and you can tell she wants her students to understand and love geology the way that she does. With that being said, I found it difficult to pay attention in this class, for whatever reason. The material is not terribly difficult to understand, so take some notes and you should be fine.

Very structured and clear-cut class. Xiaoming is a wonderful person and she teaches the material very well. I'd highly recommend for students to take this class whether they are interested in geology or just trying to fulfill a Gen-Ed. Take caution though- you will have to study the lecture slides hard to get an A.

analysis.name: Xiangjia Kong
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took in Spring 2025, and I believe it was his first time teaching. He was not very confident at the front of the room, and he could be somewhat condescending at times. He was late to his own office hours and at times wouldn't show up. He grades the homework strict but drops the lowest 2, and the class was curved. I would avoid taking it with him.

Lectures can be a little dry sometimes, and the time would be better spent going over textbook yourself at certain points in the class. The class can be pretty hard but eventually becomes pretty easy. It was also pretty hard to do well on the homework assignments. He's a genuine guy despite that, and made sure we know how to write good proofs.

Nice guy, horrible teacher. Unorganized lectures, unclear expectations of students, no resources for success. HARSH grader - doesn't accept certain proofs even if they're correct in the textbook. Was late multiple times to his own office hours. DO NOT TAKE DISCRETE WITH HIM. but he is willing to work with students.

He was an okay professor for discrete, but sometimes seemed confused on what he was teaching or by simple questions students asked. A very tough grader and doesn't accept methods other than what was taught in class (even if its in the textbook/still correct). Office hours are slightly helpful for explanations.

Nice guy but harsh grader. He took off points easily by a few things, and homework were harshly graded. Final was not easy as agreed. It's hard to get decent grade in his class although he curved the boundary.

analysis.name: Ximena  Bustamante-Marin
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Though Dr. Marin may seem strict, she is genuinely really nice! Class content is difficult and requires a lot of memorization to be prepared on tests, so definitely do not study last min! But it is really interesting to learn if you are interested in nutrition. Her office hours were pretty helpful to go over exams or any content related questions!

So much to say, so little words. Lectures were a waste of time, she reads directly off the slides and still finds a way to tell us inaccurate information (takes a true genius to do that). Dont bother asking questions because she wont answer them. Pros - she's funny and sarcastic, really appeals to my sense of humor. My advice, dont take this class.

Dr. Bustamante-Marin is a GENIUS in the field and is very knowledgeable. She's the sweetest person if you take the time to actually talk to her. That said, she is a tough grader with exams with tricky wording (which she will not give points back on), and omg the lectures are so fast with sometimes 100s of slides. you learn a lot! DONT CRAM!!

I really like her as a person, she was very approachable and you can tell she knows what she is talking about. However, lectures were pretty uninspiring and the tests were horrendously written. Good news is about half of the questions on her exams are free points, but the others were often very ambiguous and did not focus on core concepts.

Her lectures are boring. They only go over a small part of the assigned readings, so you are basically teaching yourself. If you read the chapters you could skip the lectures. Exams are hard. Multiple select questions. For example, the choices would be A; B; C; A & B; or A , B, & C. Over half of the test consist of question in this format.

analysis.name: Xiangying Huang
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof Huang moves very quickly and has had me lost in confusion since day 1 of the class. Her homework assignments often cover nothing done in class and as such I cannot practice what I learned. The class is graded 80% on multiple choice tests, but with no practice questions, I'm often lost on what to study. She is nice, but her class is very hard.

Her lectures are not helpful when it comes to homework and exams. Exams are multiple choice and do not properly test knowledge of the course (almost impossible to adequately study for). She talks more about the philosophy of statistics and goes through difficult proofs during class rather than covering necessary material that is tested on.

Although friendly, professor Huang's lectures are impossible to keep up with. One week she says she is uploading her notes and the next she says she has stopped. Exams are multiple choice but extremely difficult to understand. Her lectures include maybe 1 or 2 examples while the rest is just her doing proofs that aren't helpful.

Goes through the material as if everyone in the class has already seen it and just needs a quick glance to understand the topics. Does complicated proofs in class; homework and exams are unrelated and difficult. Unless you have already taken STOR 435 and know all the material, this is a terrible professor to have to start learning it.

She spends most of the class time doing proofs rather than providing examples to explain the concepts. She moves extremely fast and barely explains difficult concepts.Two tests that are 12 question MC, which make up a significant portion (40%) of the overall grade. The final (40% of your grade) is a a MC test w/ no partial credit.

analysis.name: Jordan Young
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: There are quizzes for every unit (every 1-2 weeks) but she does review right beforehand and touches on everything that will be on the quiz so PAY ATTENTION! She canceled/moved class online a few times. Notes came from slides and from things she would show on the board like BLS statistics. Current events discussions involve some participation.

Jordan's very laid back, gives lots of remote quizzes and class off days. There was some frustration with varying quiz difficulty and varying harshness of grading on assignments. Not work-heavy, but quiz-heavy with questions pulled from niche things she said like one time in class. She's a bit of a lazy professor but it was a chill class overall.

Unpredictable and unorganized. She seems very chill, but she's a harsh grader and never really has a schedule. Thankfully it's not work heavy, but it's all about memorization of random stats for short quizzes, which is tough. Also it's week 13 and we haven't been given any information about the final project.

This class was an easy A for me, but I think that's because I sat in the front row and Professor Young knew my name and we talked a good bit. If you participate and she knows you, this class is a breeze. Not hard content, but some of my friends that never showed up were in danger of B's. lots of online (easy) quizzes, group project, final.

She was an amazing professor. She was very knowledgeable about the information, but also paired everything with detailed slides that would represent what was on the weekly quizzes. The quizzes were easy if you looked over the notes from the class before and she is very chill.

analysis.name: Yinghsuan Chao
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Chao is genuinely the sweetest person I have ever met and she wants to get to know you. I didn't love her teaching style- I struggled focusing. 2 midterms worth 15% and 20% and a final worth 20%. Content is very hard- exams are very challenging but she is the best option to take it with. Does only multiple choice and is so accessible anytime.

As a person, Dr. Chao is extremely nice. However, her teaching style is not for everyone. She tends be disorganized with her lectures and tends to do things in a more complicated sense. The final was pretty rough but I think that econ 101 is just a tough class. Probably the best out of the 101 teachers.

Take Econ with her! She is the BEST Econ 101 professor. She is so caring and even provides snacks in class! Dr. Chao offers to meet with students individually because she genuinely wants you to succeed.

she probably isnt bad for Econ 101 b/c the content is straightforward, but she is not equipped to be teaching Econ 420 at all. she seems nice but she cannot answer questions clearly and her lectures rarely stay on topic. the exams are not bad if you use outside resources, but in general her lectures offer little help with understanding the content.

She is the sweetest lady, don't get me wrong. But she can't teach. Most of her slides are AI memes and she deviates so much from the content. She doesn't grade the homeworks till more than a month after it is submitted.
What you are taught in class is NOT what you are presented with in the exam. And you're not allowed to ask questions on the exam..

analysis.name: Fei Yu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Quite a bit of work, but she is very flexible and understanding as a teacher.

DON'T TAKE 718 W/ YU! I have taken other UX classes and was very excited to learn more in this class. Instead, I felt like each week hours were wasted of my life. Class was so DULL! She was never helpful at office hours and she didn't give clear instructions on the HW. Also didn't hesitate to call ppl out in class. MEJO 581 with Ruel was better!

Fei is a very passionate teacher. She was always communicative and understanding, so long as you communicate first. The class was organized as one major group-project with various smaller projects and quizzes sprinkled throughout. I would've liked to see shake-ups in team composition so you could interact with more students.

I have never rated a professor before but I felt like it had to be done for Professor Fei Yu. She is one of the most unorganized teachers I have ever had. She assigns a lot of little projects that have quick turn around so we never really have time to understand the material. I feel like I waste my time in her class and wish I had a different teach

I didn't learn much from 718 as the flipped classroom & virtual format puts the full burden of learning on the student. Class time was not utilized well. We'd sometimes use 45+ mins to talk logistics/rubrics & skim over actual content. I will say that Yu responds to emails/feedback readily, isn't a harsh grader, and does games on Zoom though.

analysis.name: Yaakov Ariel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ariel veered away from the syllabus to say the least. There was a required reading of at least one novel, usually more per class.  The readings were dense, the videos were boring, he was confusing, not to mention the 12 pg term paper. I would not recommend. He was also HATEFUL if you ever had to miss a class, even if you were sick.

I LOVED this class. Favorite professor and favorite class and i'm about to graduate. I would take any class he teaches. It's not hard if you try and are thoughtful. I really enjoyed the topics and Dr. Ariel always brought snacks, which was super kind. For the class, we got to visit churches and write about our experiences visiting them.

Great professor. Provided clear expectations for exams and opportunities to help prepare the class. Would highly recommend any class with Dr. Ariel. Honestly, a gem of a human. 

The topic of 242 (New Religious Movements) was unlike anything else I've ever learned and broadened my understanding of other faith communities.
Great professor, gets to know his students, very personable. Would recommend him to anyone.

Dr. Ariel was the best professor of the three. He kept the class engaged through clips, texts, and slides. His essays were the easiest of the three, if you listened to him for 5 mins you could easily score an A. Plus, he gave you hints ahead of time. Great professor, especially if you are a history buff.

analysis.name: Eva Zhao
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of the worst MEJO professors. She gave NO FEEDBACK. Doesn't believe in giving 100s. She told us we did great but the max she gave someone was a 94. This isn't supposed to be a difficult class, but is when she doesn't give any feedback other than a good job, and quickly goes through the slides. We have only done group work all year. DO NOT TAKE!
Take this class with this professor if you want to feel terrible about yourself and want to have your work picked apart to shreds. AKA don't take it.

She is sweet and cares about learning, but definitely made this class much more stressful than it needed to be. Was not super clear on assignment and grading guidelines and graded them very harshly. Assigned a lot of work week to week and gave a final presentation in addition to a very challenging final. I'd find another professor for this course.

Eva is clearly very smart, but she has a hard time communicating her ideas and knowledge to the class. She constantly contradicted herself in class and had to second-guess herself on many things. I don't know if this was her first time teaching MEJO 379 and she just needed a semester under her belt, but I will just say she did not make it easy.

Eva is very sweet. She worked really hard to provide a good experience during Covid, and she was very understanding. This class was a little slowly paced, though, which was maybe good because of Covid, but I found it hard to pay attention most days. I would recommend Eva because of her obvious smartness and kind heart, but maybe not this class.

analysis.name: Zachary  Fisher
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Fisher is an exceptional instructor—clear, engaging, and always accessible outside of class. He sets fair, transparent expectations and genuinely wants students to understand and succeed. He's incredibly kind and understanding when life happens. His teaching style makes the material more enjoyable and keeps the course accessible and manageable.

Amazing person!! I loved Dr. Fisher. He is the nicest person ever, and extremely helpful. Everyone in our class which was small loved him. He is a great professor, and if I had someone as a PI or something, he would be it. The class is whatever you want to make of it, and I think I watched some classmates truly learn and show amazing growth.
Dope professor, easy lectures, amazing materials :)

analysis.name: Muxin Zhang
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Zhang was my studio instructor for PHYS 118, and she was absolutely amazing. She was insanely good at answering questions and would always help you in any way she could. She was the course coordinator this semester, so she did not lecture for the full class. There is not a studio instructor I would rather have. Wholeheartedly recommend!

I had Prof Zhang for my Physics 118 studio and she was amazing. The class was very difficult but she explained everything in a clear and engaging way so it all made sense. The canvas was very helpful and she was always willing to walk you though any problems both in class and in office hours.

SHE IS THE BEST!!! She is super accessible, especially in office hours, and explains concepts extremely well. This class definitely requires some hard work, especially if you've never been in a college-level physics course before, but if you use your resources it is definitely doable.

Phy118 is hard and a fair amount of work, but completely doable. Course was organized really well. Dr. Zhang was my studio instructor, and she did a great job reinforcing difficult concepts taught in lecture. Class isn't super test heavy, either.

Muxin was a very good professor; I had her for studio as well. She is super kind and always available outside of class if you need her. Her grading is very lenient for in-class work and gives a lot of partial credit on exams.

analysis.name: Zoe McHodgkins
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Super sweet and understanding; always willing to let you take things at a later time if something happens, and is very lenient with grading. I shouldn't be doing as well as I am honestly lol and she makes French actually understandable. Open minded and cares a lot, and follows a set schedule so you always know what's up! Highly recommend!
Zoe is great. She is super understanding of people learning french for the first time, and she it a pretty easy grader. Super approachable, but do the nightly homework or your grade will be knocked.

Love herrr. She's so sweet and just wants to help in any way she can. She's very flexible too - I had a cold and she let me retake a quiz a few days later. Participation matters, but that's expected in a language class.

Zoe was a very fair grader and gave good, helpful feedback on the daily homework, as well as quizzes. She lived in Paris for an extended period of time so she is very familiar with how native French is spoken. She is also very friendly and easily approachable. I highly recommend Zoe for French 101.
too informal and unprofessional but very approachable

analysis.name: Chudi Zhong
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Zhong is smart and decent in teaching a tough 500-level course. The course is fast-paced, but the same for all ML classes. She curved very hard, both on non-exam components and overall. You will learn a lot if you keep up with the contents, while the curve won't make your grade too bad after all, since hw and projects are graded leniently.

Lectures are highly theoretical and often difficult to grasp, despite the professor describing the material as easy and intuitive. You'll need independent study to try understanding the content. I wish slides were consistently posted early to read ahead of class. The first midterm was brutal and different from assignments and the practice exam.

The professor is very smart, but the lectures are mostly pure theory and really hard to follow. I spend a lot of extra time studying on my own. The practice exam for the midterm wasn't very helpful, since the actual exam was way, way harder.

Not really any practice in class. Wish there was more homework to provide grade padding and practice, especially after a brutal midterm. She is clearly smart and kind, but lecture slides are posted last minute and lectures are hard to follow. I'm teaching myself the content with Google and YouTube videos. Don't stack many hard classes with this one

Seeing a lot of negative reviews after the first midterm but she clearly realized it was too difficult and made the second midterm easier - class avg went from 65 to 80. 

a lot of homework but no final and shes a really generous grader. will give you full credit on the final project if you put a good faith effort in.

analysis.name: Zachary Yukio Kerr
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Kerr is one of the rare professors on campus who considers the fact that his students are people with lives outside of his class. He is very willing to be flexible as long as you are willing to demonstrate you are putting in effort to the class. Makes an otherwise really boring topic and 8 am class really enjoyable. I would highly recommend.

Honest and understanding of students lives outside of classes, especially for a one credit course. Take this class with him if you can, it seemed he was able to be more flexible with the material than other professors because he helped create the course. Met six times throughout the semester, with biweekly online work and a final group project

Zack understood that the class was only a single credit hour, and only had us do what was necessary to learn the content. I had to meet with him for help with my final project, and I mentioned that I was looking for some good study spots on campus. He took the time after our meeting to send me a list of his favorite places to get work done.

Zach is such a great professor. He seemed to really understand the point of Data Lit Lab and didn't make it more demanding than it needed to be. He was extremely engaging, understanding, and flexible with the class. Overall great guy.

Professor Kerr was one of the best professors I have ever had. He makes class entertaining and truly cares for his students. He is one of the most energetic and fun professors I have had at UNC, especially with his endless jokes and memes. His workload is VERY manageable, and he is very passionate about research. I would 100000% recommend!!

analysis.name: Andy Ackerman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Ackerman is nice, though his class is extremely difficult. His review sheets are no where close to what an actual exam looks like. His grading is harsh and he does not like to give out good grades. Look to take another statistics professor because he is not caring of your grade, though says he is. Dislike him a lot..

Concepts are hard but Andy was helpful in OH. Virtually no material to help you study for exams and HW questions did not always relate to class / exams. Great lecturer and educator in general. Looked forward to class.

Not sure why the MATH186 ratings are so bad, I guess you guys didn't study. Class is super hard, but Andy's a great professor and really accessible outside class. Doesn't give much material for exam prep, but class problems and reviews outside of class are very representative of what the exam looks like. Work is hard but doable, very fun class.
Horrible. Grading is harsh. Does not drop lowest midterm. Grading unclear. Don't take.
Does not care for your grade. The hardest professor to take for stats at Lafayette.

analysis.name: Achsah Dorsey
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Love her! One of the best professors at UMass. Her classes and lectures are interesting and easy to follow. Provides slides before class. She does have a lot of readings but only a few of them are compulsory reads. Fairly easy midterm and final. One final project, 2 other projects and a few Course Reflections.

*ANTHRO 364*
I loved this class. Dr. Dorsey teaches us about professional development as an Anthropologist, and I still use the notes I took in her class to this day.

Professor Dorsey was one of the best professors I had at UMass. She makes learning content fun and super interesting. I have a lot of respect for her. Take a class with her! You'll learn so much without being overwhelmed, and she's always willing to help if you need it.

Achsah was my TA for this class, and it was a pretty TA heavy class (meaning they did all the grading and that's who you actually interacted with in recitation). I enjoyed her a lot! She's really nice and has a pleasant personality, and she got to know us all by name. She isn't an easy grader, but it's nothing insane. Solid choice overall
Dr. Dorsey is a great lecturer and a very kind professor. I would highly recommend her classes, especially Anthropology 313 (Nutritional Anthropology).

analysis.name: Rafael Acosta Morales
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I enjoyed SPAN344 (not 373 344 wasn't an option). This course was chill & insightful. Sometimes it was hard do all readings. Professor wasn't perfect (a bit unorganized... FYI to ppl who get stressed over that lol) BUT he was really flexible and understanding throughout the class which is rare in the ROML department. 8.5/10 class would take again!

This was probably my favorite class at UNC. I usually struggle with participating but the prof is so knowledgeable and funny I felt really comfortable! He is also very kind and willing to work with the class on due dates. Iffy about Canvas, but everything was clear in the syllabus. 11/10, unique experience!

It is clear that this is Rafael's first semester teaching here, which can excuse his unstructured and uninspired way of teaching. Class always felt incredibly dull which is surprising considering the class was about fiction writing (one of the most entertaining forms of writing). Excited to see how he structures future classes, he has the passion.

analysis.name: Michael Acosta
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Mike Acosta is an incredible teacher. Class is never boring and he actually cares about each student. He has a wealth of knowledge and shares it in an understandable way. He emphasizes that the class is to grow, and you don't have to stress about turning in perfect work. You can genuinely learn. If you can take a class with Mike, do it.

What a guy. Easily the best professor I've had at UNC. Acosta cares so much about his students. The man has lived three different lives and has countless hilarious stories he loves to share. He is so knowledgeable and inspirational, and he feels more like a friend than a professor. Cannot recommend him enough. Amazing final lecture too.

He was by far the best professor I have EVER had at this school. I am a premed stem student and I took this class as my sanity class and it was the best decision. I enjoyed this class so much because of Dr. Acosta. The content and the class were enjoyable but it was Dr. Acosta who brought the class to life.

Dr. Acosta has been the best professor I've had at UNC thus far. He is so funny and actually cares about us as students, which you don't see from the other professors at UNC. The lectures were so funny and he related it to screenwriting, which allowed me to learn in a way that I haven't in any other class in my life.

He has some of the most engaging lectures and every class he'll tell an incredible story. Assignments are graded for completion so as long as you submit them on time you'll get an A. He makes the group projects fun and I learned a lot over the course of the semester. Left the class with a new outlook on life.

analysis.name: Jeff Ackermann
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: His class seems easy until you have a test. He doesn't writes his own homework or tests so they don't correspond to his lectures very well. Also, a lot of times he doesn't really know what he's talking about. He's funny so his lectures aren't too boring and there's not much work outside of class but the tests took me off guard.

Absurdly easy. Lectures aren't mandatory and all material comes from slides, which he posts online. No point attending class if you don't want to. HW can be done as a group. Tests are really easy (my ECON 101 class was 3 times as hard!) He's pretty funny and a good lecturer.  Microeconomics need not be daunting with Ackermann. Recommended!19940

Jeff is a super nice guy and his lectures (that you definitely don't have to attend) are funny. However, his tests are not written by him so they don't relate well to what he lectures on in class. It should all be super easy, but I was definitely caught off guard with a horrible final that ruined my grade. Glad it's over.
This is a tough class mostly because the professor doesn't know what he's talking about. He is good at teaching the specific material, but he lacks basic knowledge of topics taught in ECON 101.

analysis.name: Neel Ahuja
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Class was not the best. The professor also made me feel uncomfortable. Like, my eyes are up here.

The papers are the main part of the class. They were slightly difficult because they were on such odd topics I was not used to writing on. Overall, the class was really good. Discussions were very interesting and you read good documents and novels. I would definitely take this class again.

Great FYS - delved into a lot of interesting topics. Extremely discussion-heavy. You get as much out of it as you put in, learning and grade-wise. Besides being a cool guy, he will save your life if you need any help at all with your papers so go see him! Grading's a bit unclear but he seems to notice effort and it reflects. Got an A.

Neel is a super nice guy who is very knowledgable about Caribbean literature. That said, when it is time to write the multiple 7-page papers, you will end up in his office hours and he will save you. He doesn't grade easy and expects you to have it together when you come to class. Participation is key in this class. I would take it again though!

Mr. Ahuja taught the most interesting freshman seminar I could've imagined. He was clear and the work was SO manageable, he was understanding and encouraged us to participate (very necessary!). But overall it was such a great class and there aren't many assignments- barely even did the readings. Take his class!

analysis.name: Shawn Ahmed
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class was awesome. Dr. Ahmed was super layed back and the entire course reflected that. Your grades off of 2 midterms and 1 final (not cumulative) and 2 group presentations. It's very much show up do the work and an A is almost guaranteed. I don't think anyone got under a 80 on any exam or presentation.

This class was very easy in comparison to other bio courses. All midterms and final was take home and were graded very fairly with clear feedback. Only two group presentations and you get to choose your groups. Overall, I highly recommend this class to help boost your science GPA.
Great prof, never showed up to class and only showed up when it was my turn to present. Take home test and finals. He also records lectures and host it on zoom. Easy BIOL 400+ class!!!

I actually took 546, but it was an easy class, as long as you take enough notes to understand the material, all you have to do to succeed is rewatch the lectures and write down what he says with your understanding on the open note tests. He clearly wants everyone to get an A and grades group presentations nicely. Helps if you go to office hours.
This man does not tip servers when he goes to restaurants.

analysis.name: Stan Ahalt
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Stan is a good professor but the class design for Comp-116 was not good at all. It was all lectures, including the recitation, where the class would only involve copying what the professors are typing down. With it being a lecture heavy class, there was absolutely no engagement. Also, there was a big leap in difficulty in the assignments.

Dr. Ahalt taught this class with Dr. Krishnamurthy and together they were an awesome dynamic duo! The workload isn't tough and it's easy to end with a good grade, but the best part is listening to two great data science minds work through problems in lecture. You get a great intro to Python, and I would highly recommend taking the class!

Stan was a very kind and considerate professor however was not the best lecturer. The lectures were mainly watching professors code and follow along without a lot of explanation as to why things were done. This course would be much easier if you have an understanding of programming beforehand, however is not impossible without any.

A fantastic professor and cool guy. He taught this semester tag-team with Dr. Krishnamurthy, and both were great! The course is very well designed. Lectures are helpful but not required if you read the book. Course is easy not in the sense that it's a joke but that you'll know how to code by the time it's done. Highly recommend!

Professor Ahalt taught this class with Professor Krishnamurthy, and I loved it. For me, the workload in this class was very manageable. Both professors were extremely understanding of students struggling with mental health and other issues that kept them from completing work. I would highly, highly recommend this course.

analysis.name: Andrew Ackerman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very available outside of class which is great however he is not very accommodating for extenuating circumstances. Tests are extremely conceptual based and conceptual-based material is barely brushed on in lectures making the exams quite hard. Class was done completely on a chalkboard and refused to post notes until a few days before the exam

Amazing lecturer and explained concepts really well. You can tell he really cares about his students and teaching. Very test heavy however but not too difficult of a course as long as you go to class. Really accessible outside of class and posts his notes right before the midterms/final. Not hard but you'll have to put in some effort for an A

Andy is a great and caring person who answered every single question with much consideration and patience. My only issue with the course is the structure of the class (2 exams, final replaces lowest midterm, homework grades). Very little resources to help students properly prepare for exams and a bad exam can tank your grade. Great guy though.

If Andy has managed to keep me, a graduating senior in an 8AM class, then you know he's done something right. His enthusiasm in each lecture makes the most boring topics engaging. He encourages students to participate, from discussions on ethics to math principles. He is accessible via email or OH and goes above and beyond to support his students.

Fantastic lecturer, always energetic and engaging. You can tell he is truly passionate about the material and teaching it to his students. He cares about each of his students on an academic and personal level. His class was genuinely interesting and the material was important. I know many other STAN majors who are interested in this class.

analysis.name: Katherine Aha
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: WORST poli sci class I've ever taken and I'm a poli sci major who's loved every class so far. She is completely unclear in lectures, has white slides with black writing and she always stood in the corner and talked pretty quietly. Her voice tapered off toward the end of really important sentences so you wouldn't know what was going on. STAY AWAY!

Katie is great - lectures can be a little dry, but readings aren't necessary because she explains everything in class. Always willing to help outside of class, very helpful. As long as you take notes and pay attention in class, you'll do well

I had to take this course for my major but would recommend to anyone. LOVED katie-- there was a lot of reading assigned but honestly if you don't do it she does a great job of explaining everything in class. only 2 papers and 2 exams and both were straightforward and graded very fairly. 10/10 would take another class with her!!
Enjoyed her POLI 236 class. Interesting topic--lectures are sometimes a bit long, but grading criteria and exams are straightforward.
