Even though the material wasn't the most interesting Katherine was able to clearly and concisely convey it during lectures. Exams were straightforward and there was only one paper. I would definitely recommend her class.

analysis.name: Aaron Shapiro
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Shapiro is one of the few professors that doesn't require a purchased textbook, but instead provides us with PDFs of the material. He's very thorough and lectures are genuinely engaging. Attendance is mandatory for recitations, not for the lecture. He was very accommodating when I had to reschedule my midterm due to travel conflict.

Took Comm 455: He genuinely cares about students and has an amazing response time to emails. You really don't have to go to class until you get to the end when everyone is giving presentations. There were 3 really easy assignments, a scavenger hunt, a short paper/video about a soundscape, and an essay on any sound topic for the final. 100% take him

Aaron was a gem!! I am a senior and took his Algorithms & Society class with little to no experience with interpreting data and he made sure that even the hardest readings were made understandable. He is so kind, understanding, and I genuinely learned so much in his class. 100% take this class you wont regret it

Aaron was a delight this semester. He was my first 400 COMM class and his class was not difficult at all. The workload includes writing reflections for readings every week, a sound-related exercise every week, a Soundscape project (got 100 for going out and recording sounds), and a 10-page final (find an interesting topic, it will help). 10/10 Prof

Papers and attendance are the bulk of the grades, originally had 3 papers and a final paper but he cut it down to 2 papers, the 2nd paper being the final. Understanding and accessible, chance to get extra credit with a 3rd paper. Lectures can get dry with little participation, and readings are a bit long, 40-75 pages, but it is interesting stuff.

analysis.name: Aalyia Sadruddin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are somewhat stream-of-consciousness, interesting to listen to but sometimes feels unguided. About 4-5 graded assignments make up your grade, but she's a relatively easy grader. Incredibly caring and willing to speak with you during office hours, but the course would've benefitted from slightly better structuring.

Wellesley - ANTH 101 Really kind prof! Very accessible and inspiring/global with her viewpoint. Wants everyone to succeed and provides the means to do so. If you get the chance, take a class with her!

Sadruddin is an absolute gem. The class is on the anthropology of care and it was a wonderful experience understanding its complexities, both good and bad, especially how evident it is today. As long as you do the reading and participate, your assignment and class grades are fine. She is very sweet and calls our class the "care circle". Love her!
She's teaching at Wellesley now and I took her class last semester. Learned so much in her class, best professor I couldve ever ask for in college. I'd be thankful in my life to have Dr. Sadruddin.

Dr. Sadruddin is the BEST! The course structure is weekly readings and an easy-going class discussion about them. There are several writing assignments, but she grades fairly and provides amazing feedback. She WANTS you to succeed and to love med anth as much as she does. She is energetic and passionate. There is not a class I would recommend more.

analysis.name: Ron Alterovitz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Best and clearest lecture slides in the COMP department. Labs were only hard because the sensors were not reliable but tests were pretty easy. Content is very interesting and I learned a lot. Would definitely recommend taking this class. But remember, there is a lot of unpredictability and a lot of uncertainty in robotics...

There wasn't too much homework, but there is a group project where you build a robot and design it for the given lab days. The labs get progressively harder and make up the bulk of the class grade, and took my group anywhere from 5 - 10 hours a week outside of class to prepare. The assignments/exams were fairly challenging (mostly trigonometry).

He's very passionate about tech., only talked about robots, AI, & internet instead of many topics. Grade based on a few assignments and 2 presentations (7 & 15 minutes). Attendance policy is unclear but as far as I know, he did not record attendance (syllabus said he would take it 3 random days). Lectures are somewhat boring but the class is easy

I took COMP 89 with professor Alterovitz. SUPER easy class. 3 assignments and 2 projects for the entire semester, no homework. Class can be boring sometimes but Professor Alterovitz is super passionate about what he researches and studies. He does not take attendance. I highly recommend taking this class for a FC and easy freshman launch.

A super sweet guy and gives opportunities to make up for low grades (i.e., drops lowest lab grade and extra credit for participating). The robotics labs were pretty tricky and took up a lot of time, but otherwise, the class was relatively fair (I imagine most will get a B at the end of the semester). Super nice guy and a super interesting class!

analysis.name: Aaron Moody
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: We didn't follow the syllabus at all for this course, but it was fine. One lab assignment every 2 weeks ish (total 8) and a final project/presentation, with very lenient grading. Wouldn't take if I wasn't a geog major tho

Dr. Moody is a wonderful person, but lacks the organization and preparation of a professor. Originally took this course for an easy allied science, ended up P/F due to the lack of information for assignments and course information in general. Class slides were often never uploaded and students are expected to understand material from diagrams only.

Dr. Moody is a great person, but do not take this class unless you genuinely care about the topic. I took this as an "easy" allied science and ended up having to P/F it because there were only a few quizzes, 2 papers, and 2 exams & the info on the quizzes and exams is nowhere to be found on Canvas bc he jumps around the ppt and doesn't upload them.

I have to agree with others on Dr. Moody. He's very intelligent, but I don't think he's meant to teach; he's very unorganized, and the lectures make me want to fall asleep. His PowerPoints look like they were made in 2009. I only took this class because it's required for the Geography major, but if you're not GEOG, I do not recommend this course.

Holy disorganization. Syllabus was completely unreflective of the course, he skipped half the content because of how much he rambles, quiz/paper due dates were given out randomly, etc. Thankfully, the content is super easy, papers are graded easily, and two quiz grades can be replaced. Easy A as long as you're ready to deal with the chaos.

analysis.name: Aaron Harcus
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Reads directly off slides, but somewhat interesting class if you're SUPER interested in music. Attendance was literally just a number given at the beginning of each class. Graded by 6 pass/fail assignments and a final project (10-page paper or 20-25 min recorded presentation) and a final listening exam. It's an athlete class, so it's an easy A.

Professor Harcus was a great lecturer, and I really learned a lot from this course! Class is fairly easy consisting of attendance, reading/listening responses, a listening exam, and final project which are all graded easily.

Professor Harcus truly cares about music so much, and he is so interested in all of his students' opinions on the music we all enjoy. He's super chill and very kind. I. At the end of the class, we got to create our final project on any album and explain why it's significant. Even if this was time consuming, it was a really fun project to complete.

Great man for a easy class, just show up to class and do the assignments as you are graded just for participation and short assignments. If you can't pass this class this easy, might be time to transfer out. Unbelievably easy trust me.

Professor Harcus is amazing, he is now one of my favorite Professor here at UNC! I would 100% take his class again! He is very understanding and the assignments were spaced out so it was very doable and I also enjoyed his lectures too!

analysis.name: Aaron  Jacobson
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is a good person & cares about his students. But he can be very hard to follow, unorganized & very fast (not all his fault). He makes lots of mistakes in his lectures. The final exam is much harder than his other midterms because he doesn't write the final himself. Brought my grade from an A- to a C. Go ahead and get a tutor if you want to pass.

During class is lectures are pretty confusing. He moves fast and some of his examples just over-complicate concepts. In his office hours he was more helpful and pretty funny. We almost never had time to review in class before tests when many other 110 classes did, but he tried to host extra reviews outside of class. Tests were not curved.

He is a nice guy but he always messes up in his own lectures and is confusing. His voice and lectures are boring. He is annoying abt curves and won't curve even though the other math department  for 110 do. Overall I wouldn't take this class w him because it's already difficult and he doenst make it easier. He's nice but not a great teacher.

As a person, he's nice and generally helpful. As a teacher, he's boring, talks too fast, and overcomplicates things. He gives partial credit for correct work on exams, and offers corrections when needed, but homework is infuriating and he gets scattered/confused during his own lectures. Some of it isn't his fault, but this class is a huge headache.

If you could summarize I prepared my lecture 5 mins before class into a person. Dude was all over the place and would frequently say he made the lecture slides at 3am the night before so to give him a break. Overall a not so good professor who talked in circles

analysis.name: Aaron Thieme
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He walks around the room and laughs when students say something wrong. He keeps saying "I'm your professor, and you are my student." like he is getting off on the power dynamic. He gives very overly jargonized readings, look up "Sesquipedalian" " He spent 40 minutes having people guess what "belief" meant, only to say it "refers to truth."

Professor Thieme was an all-around great professor. I took PHIL134 with him and learned a great deal. He's incredibly knowledgeable and doesn't leave students with incomplete answers. This class is quite difficult, but the professor is just so charismatic that it's impossible to dislike him. He is accessible outside of class, is never condescending, and wants the students to succeed. Perhaps the material could've been taught more effectively; this is certainly one of the more difficult classes I've taken.
I took Phil 210 with Aaron online and he's great! He genuinely cares about the students and class topics. Be ready to have a reading due every class but it is not that bad.

analysis.name: Ron Bergquist
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 66 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: My third class under this goat, and never disappoints and always a new learning experience. Take him!

Love Professor Bergquist. He genuinely cares about his students' learning and he makes all assignment expectations crystal clear. I took both 161 and 385 with him, both of which were a cakewalk. Just to note 385 has group work and lectures focus a lot on military/historical concepts. He also gives great feedback

Bergquist is a nice guy and knows what he's teaching. The lectures can be boring especially at 8 AM. However, I learned a lot of practical and cool things in the class. Super easy assignments, no midterms, and the final is a presentation. The only thing is that he takes forever to give back grades. I highly recommend this class and professor!

Ron is a gem! He genuinely cares for his students and is passionate about information science. He has a lot of experience, both in teaching and in the field, that makes his content interesting! His grading and work are extremely lenient and he just wants you to learn and engage with the material! I also took 161 with him and he is the best!

Sweet is a word that truly describes him. He is kind, approachable. Based past positive reviews, it's clear his class is easy. However, I strongly urge anyone reading this not to just attend class and then get distracted by your computers. Please take the time to listen to his lectures and his content is genuinely enlightening and inspiring.

analysis.name: Aaron Smith
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Probably the best prof at UNC CS. 301 is not an easy class, to be honest, but Aaron makes it much easier. He really encourages everyone to ask questions during lectures and answer all of them patiently. HWs are intense though, one programming HW each week, but as long as you listen carefully and start early, it will be fine. Will take him again!

SUCH an amazing professor and even more awesome person. UNC comp sci does not deserve Aaron Smith. He makes everyone feel welcome, encourages questions, and is super understanding. Lectures are fun and super easy to follow, assignments are fun... I cannot emphasize how great of a professor and person Aaron is. Would 100/10 take this again.

I adore Aaron! So kind, very interactive lectures, really wants you to ask questions and learn, explains things so clearly - an overall 10/10. IMO he's right under Kris Jordan as best CS professors here. 301 is a great class because of him. He has so many fun catch phrases you could make a bingo.

April 19, 2021. 2:31 PM. Student: "We should make the PollEv answers 25% each." Aaron: "Let's do it." *Class proceeds to be the most epic thing in any lecture from the CS department ever for the next ten minutes. Highs, Lows, near Perfection, Custom Ink T-shirt designs. The whole enchilada.* This is the perfect description of 301. :)

Overall, a great professor! I would say it was one of my best experiences in a class. He is very easy to reach out to and ask questions in class or after class, and is very good at covering concepts from many approaches to ensure everyone understands. Very caring and very passionate professor, in other words, he actually likes his job and it shows.

analysis.name: Grace Aaron
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Going into the final in a few weeks with her.  This semester has been VERY frustrating.  She speaks clear Spanish but expects ridiculous expectations from her students.  She can be fairly condescending in her tone.  Most frustrating is her tough grading.  No student gets over a 95 on participation, per her statements.  She always picks off points.

Professor Aaron is super sweet and southern! I was excited to take this course despite the not so good reviews of Aaron. This course stressed stressed me out. It thought it would be fun to do my own translation & learn general translation info. I learned nothing & had a terrible experience with the project because she didn't follow the rubric & it wasn't right if it wasn't how she would do it

She is a nice person, but she grades so so so so so much harder than all the other 203 professors. She shows no mercy for anything. I spoke during class every single day multiple times and she gave me an 85 for participation, which was very unfair. Also, I went to office hours regularly for help and she was not very helpful. I do NOT recommend her.

analysis.name: Adam Harris
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

I genuinely enjoyed coming to class. The way he taught was so engaging and I liked how he didn't take anything about the course too seriously. Listen. College Thriving is a really annoying class. However, he really did his best with the material provided to him.

analysis.name: Fenaba Addo
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: This class was extremely repetitive with the same content in every single module. Prof. Addo does NOT know how to lecture in any way shape or form. She needs to take a workshop on lecturing. The class itself was boring, tests were fine, just study the review that she posts. Application based. Our assignments were easy 100's. I skipped class a lot.

I found her class frustrating. She is condescending and fails to answer questions beyond the content of her lecture slides. The content is manageable, but lectures are poorly organized. My biggest issue with her class was the volume of tests. A policy innovation and analysis course should focus on research and writing, not multiple choice exams.

She is clearly smart but such a bad lecturer. She gets confused by her own slides, mostly just reads off them anyway, and struggles to answer student questions. She also weirdly giggles so much and it makes me so angry. Exams weren't too hard though and out of class assignments were easy 100s

I feel that some of the negative reviews of Prof. Addo are exaggerated. She is one of the most caring and supportive professors I've had at UNC. She truly wants her students to succeed, is approachable outside of class, and takes the time to explain material when you're confused. If you put in the effort, she will absolutely meet you halfway.

Professor Addo cares a lot and is knowledgable but her lectures were verbatim off the slides. She was not great at answering student questions in lecture either. 4 exams throughout the semester which was a lot but if you study the guide she gives then you should do well on them. Easy class and interesting content but unhelpful lectures.

analysis.name: Adam Price
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Adam is a super awesome guy, and he is funny and very passionate about his craft. The class itself is easy, but there is a lot of busy work. I really enjoyed the first few weeks, but it started to feel a little bit repetitive. You have to read a short story, write a paragraph, and later write discussion posts. Sounds super light, but gets tedious.

I enjoyed having Adam as the instructor a lot. I thought he was very knowledgeable on the subjective of creative writing and was incredibly passionate. The class itself is easy, particularly weighted on your submission of your own 10 page short story. He's very sarcastic, but I find him to be hilarious. I recommend!

Funny, smart, charismatic guy. This was one of my favorite classes at UNC. You read a short story before every class, then discuss it in class. You have a 10-15 page short fiction story (basically about anything you want) due at a certain point in the semester, where it gets workshopped in class. Chill A, cool subject, if you're taking 130 take him

Adam was an amazing professor and his class was very straight forward. You have small readings with short writing assignments before each class and then one final long story that you get to create. Show up to class, participate every now and then, and listen to feedback from your draft and you will get an easy A.

Adam was a super nice teacher and made the class feel very open for constructive criticism. My only complaint with him was his "Do Not" list for writing, but with the way he structured the class it never became an issue. He was flexible as well.

analysis.name: Adlai Lang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: English 105I was amazing with Professor Lang. 1 individual project, 2 group projects, no midterm nor final. All the projects were writing wikipedia pages on topics you choose. You can only miss two classes, but he's very understanding if you explain absences. Super easy grader, and a B is the lowest you can get if you complete all the work.
He's very chill and super kind. Just make sure to turn in the homework on time and you'll get an A. Also, go to his office hours, he is very knowledgeable on classics (lowkey cool)!

An amazing teacher and my favorite professor this semester. Every assignment we did was marked based on completion. I loved how his areas of expertise (I believe it was Latin or Roman linguistics) seeped into the way he taught class. What you learn and get out of this class is based on what you put into it. There was one group project.

Prof. Lang is a great choice for ENGL 105I (Natural Sciences). The writing assignments were all interesting and relevant. They're caring and will work with you on deadlines if you communicate. You'll have homework each class, but as long as you show effort and turn everything in you'll get an A. Make sure to have some scientific topic in mind.

Prof. Lang was caring, kind, well-organized, and overall a really great teacher. Assignments were fairly easy but engaging and had lots of room for creative touches. Good incorporation of individual and personal work. Engaging lectures. Grade was mostly completion and attendance. Would highly recommend taking his class.

analysis.name: Adrienne Erickcek
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Erickcek is knowledgeable and does a good job covering the material. The material is difficult though, and your grade comes down to how well you do on the midterms so study accordingly! Still, they are fairly graded and often were curved slightly (including the final) if she saw the majority of the class struggled on certain sections.

Dr. Erickcek is amazing, this class made me switch my major to astrophysics! Fantastic class, lectures, and professor. The homework can be difficult but is totally manageable if you start on time. Having python experience can be helpful.

She is an exceptional teacher, her lectures are so thorough and well-planned. She is so helpful if you make it obvious that you're trying to understand. The content of the classes are super challenging. she doesn't downplay the difficulty. She delivers excellence in her teaching and expects excellence from her students. It's intense, but worth it
She is really nice, gave good feedback on all assignments, but the material is vast and she doesn't give exam practice problems. So it is difficult to study for those exams.

PHYS118 is hard regardless of who you take it with. The class covers lots of material quickly and you have to put in effort outside of class to do well. That said, Dr. Erickcek is caring and works hard to help students understand difficult concepts. She's a great lecturer and is passionate about the material, great at answering student questions.

analysis.name: Adam Versenyi

The class was interesting and he's an expert in the field, so we read a lot of his translations of the plays. It's a 400 level so there's a 10-15 pg. term paper. Hadn't previously taken a drama class & will prob end up with a A-.

Adam Versenyi is very good at illuminating the meanings of the most obscure dramatic texts, however, he can be a bit boring at times. I have also never gotten bellow or above an A- on anything yet (this is my second course with him). He is very nice, and quite helpful. No extra credit, 2 papers and a final exam which is also a paper.
Adam's class was alright overall. A lot of readings, but that didn't make it too hard to get a good grade. Strap in for the final project, though.

analysis.name: Amy Adkins
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work

review_highlights.comment: I appreciated the clear grading criteria and overall clear communication. There are quizzes with corrections for half points back. The best professor to take 205 with. This class is so difficult but professor adkins made it easier to understand. She offers quiz corrections which saved my grade. Very caring and has multiple officer hours that you should go to. Cannot stress enough how much I enjoyed having her as a professor coming from someone who didn't do good in physics 1.

Dr. Adkins is a great professor. She's funny and very generous with grades (students can get half points back on midterms with corrections). She also does a great job of keeping the class relatively low-stress while still helping students learn a lot. I would absolutely take another class with her in the future.

Dr. Adkins is a phenomenal professor for an intro engineering course. The format of her exams allowed for test corrections which was incredibly helpful when learning the difficult content. I cannot say enough good things about the organization of this course and its format, it was really easy to follow new material and get help from the textbook.

analysis.name: Agnieszka Majewska

Pani Majewska is such a nice lady and she will give you feedback on anything you may have questions with. The homework and quizzes are light. Excited for the next 2 semesters!

Terrible lectures. Overall, the class wasn't too bad, but I didn't learn much from her teaching style. The projects are straightforward and generally enjoyable, so getting a good grade isn't hard.

lectures can get boring sometimes and are a lot of information with barely any words on slideshows, have to actually attend lectures to do well on quizzes. instructor really cares about what she talks about and i found the lecture content to be super interesting and cool to learn about!

Great teacher, very hard exams though but marks very fairly. Lots of connections high up as well, be prepared to work hard and reading the textbook helps too.  I came very unprepared to the midterm and failed it because the material seemed so much easier when he explained it in class. picked it up for the final though

Dr. Aguilar is a great guy, but the slides, textbook, and lectures are useless. Running wall-to-wall, arms flapping around like a coked up muppet is fun to watch, but it only taught me that Keynes is demand side, classicalists are supply side. Are the test and homework questions that simple? No way

analysis.name: Abelardo de la Cruz
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor De La Cruz is so kind and caring, he tries his best to remember student names even in such a large lecture hall. There are a lot of readings for this class but very little assignments, the biggest ones being a group project and 10-page final essay. He is an easy and fair grader, and I found the class material very interesting.

Nicest professor and one of the easiest classes I've taken. Each class has a reading assignment with a summary, but he grades very leniently. There's one midterm, a group presentation, and a final 10-page partner essay. Overall, it's a very easy class, and he genuinely cares about his students and is passionate about the material.

Loved this class. Abelardo is such a great professor and he cares so much about what he teaches. I took this for a Gen Ed credit but honestly found this to be a super interesting class. He is very lenient with grading, he just wants you to learn. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

Dr. Abelardo is by far one of the best professors I have gotten to experience at this school. He is excited about teaching and his enthusiasm makes the course interesting and insightful. In addition to this, he offers lots of insight on first hand experiences, allowing students to get a more comprehensive idea of Indigenous communities.

He's extremely nice and I am very glad I took his class. He was caring and careful in his discussions, speaking from his personal studies and experience in the field. One of the few teachers that actually loves doing what he does.

analysis.name: Abigail Panter
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. P is really awesome. She cares very deeply about her students and her class is not hard at all. I had no tests. She is an easy grader and wants you to do well (very flexible with deadlines). However, her lectures can be very long and all over the place. It's fine because no tests means you don't need to be fully attentive and can space off.

Dr. P is amazing and one of the best teachers I had this semester. She is always available during office hours and always checks in on students. The classwork is useful and not too difficult, with only a few hours of work outside of class each week. No exams.
You can tell that Dr. Panter actually cares about her students and she makes her classes enjoyable. She wants students to succeed and if you put effort in and participate you will do well.

Dr. Panter is the most caring professor I've ever had. She really cares about each individual student and always takes the time to ask you how you're doing. She is SUPER enthusiastic about statistics. She's kind of a perfectionist, but always has a positive attitude. I'm definitely going to keep in touch with her after this class!

Dr. Panter is a wonderful woman and professor. She is so sweet and is always concerned with how people are doing as individuals, not just their performance as students. She is not always clear and doesn't always answer e-mails but she is brilliant and more than willing to help you with anything you could ask for.

analysis.name: Abbie Smith-Ryan
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I overall enjoyed 360 and learned a lot! There were times I stressed about assignment detail, every time it was fine and I received good grades. The exams were fair and she never set us up for failure. The case studies were the main assignments of the class but if the directions were followed and effort was put in, a good grade is very achievable!

Massively regret taking this class with such a disorganized professor. ASR has very unclear grading criteria and is very late on communication. Boring lectures and extremely out of date and unreadable slides. Lots of projects on short timeline and inconsistently tough exams. She feels very cold, arrogant, and unapproachable.

I would not recommend taking nutrition with ASR since it isn't required. Its a tough class with lots of projects and some difficult concepts. Some criteria isn't well outlined and ASR is not lenient. Long lectures and tons of pointless, hard-to-digest (lol), literature you have to read. Also, be ready to get cold called in class.

This class was very interesting and I enjoyed learning a lot of the topics we covered. She also was very good to answer questions and really encouraged us to participate during class. The quizzes were pretty hard and it was really unclear what we needed to know to prepare. Also was quite condescending when you were called out and answered wrong.
Had a hard time following lectures, class slides were out of date, and the tests could be pretty difficult if you did not record every detail discussed in class.

analysis.name: Abigail Knight
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I thought Dr. Knight explained the material pretty well. I enjoyed chem 262 more than chem 261. There are a lot of reactions and mechanisms in this class but its manageable if you read, do the practice worksheets, and go to class. I would recommend. Dr. Knight definitely cared about her students. Exams could be hard if you dont put in the effort

Professor Knight is incredibly caring and kind. I met with her to discuss study plans after not doing so well on a test and she completely helped me improve my grade and the way I looked at organic chemistry. After hating 261, I actually enjoy 262!

Very nice person, terrible professor. If you want to be lost in class with little to no guidance, professor Knight is for you. Quit while you're ahead and either take it with someone else (Not Prof. Beaver), or just do not take this class.

Dr. Knight is a very enthusiastic, approachable professor with a great personality. Her midterms were open-note (and were still EXCEPTIONALLY difficult). Review past/current lectures CONSTANTLY and make sure you are confident enough to answer challenge questions on the material. 2 group projects throughout the semester were good grade boosters.
Dr Knight is awesome screw the haters

analysis.name: Abel Munoz-Hermoso
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 92 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: To start, I had him for 355 (no option to select that on RMP) Abel is my favorite UNC profesor, this is the second class I've taken with him and 355 has been my favorite class by far. Reasonable workload, he is flexible, he is hilarious, class feels like a conversation, he made the entire class friends and I would talk to any of them outside10/10

Chill and understanding professor. Cares more about participation than perfection, make an effort to speak up in class and it'll go far, even if your Spanish isn't great. Communicate issues or a desire for an extension and he'll make it work for you, if he can tell that you care about the class.

I loved this man, very happy and go lucky, makes funny jokes. He makes class engaging and gives you a lot of freedom when it comes to your written work. Not a tough grader but expects participation in class. You can tell he has a passion for Spanish, teaching does not feel like a chore to him, cares about your learning. Reopened homeworks for me.

This guy is the goat. I took him and can honestly say he was one of the best Spanish teachers I have ever had. If you are a student you need to take him (like trust me). His lectures were fun, although the content is hard he makes it fun to learn, and really wants to see you succeed as a Spanish speaker and in the class.

Amazing class and professor. He cares a lot about his students and their success in the course, and he is very passionate about teaching. Grading, assignments, tests, and quizzes were very fair. My Spanish improved so much from this class, so if you are thinking about taking it, definitely take it with him!

analysis.name: Debashis Aikat
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I think Deb is a great teacher he sends a lot of emails but he wants his students to succeed. The class is meant to be an introductory class into the school if you are thinking journalism but aren't sure I recommend this class. This class gives you the run down from all majors within the J-school. If you are a MEJO major, this is an easy elective.

Deb is a very funny guy who made class more enjoyable. He really wants you to ask questions. Material was a little scattered but before exams he will tell you what will be on them, I just memorized those things and got a high A on every exam. Rarely gave homework either. If you want a chill class take one with Deb.

This class is a must take for anyone interested in the MEJO school. Classes are lectures from professors explaining the opportunities within the school. There are only a few assignments and no homework. Minimal effort required to get an A-, but if you want an A you'll definitely have to work hard and pay attention because an A is a 95. Deb is great

Dr. Aikat is the most entertaining professor Ive had so far. He is a quirky guy, but is very knowledgeable about MEJO and loves teaching the subject. You definitely have to go to class because he takes attendance, but most importantly, all of the classes cover at least one topic that will be on the exam. Its an easy A as long as you go to class.

I love him so much! While definitely not tech-savvy, he is so helpful every class and will allow you to directly ask him if your work will net you the grade you want, and he will give areas to improve if it's not what he's looking for. A delight to talk to.

analysis.name: Aimee Deconinck
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She has absolutely no clue what is going on in this class. The piazza is constantly confusing and she frequently contradicts the syllabus in terms of what is graded and required. She is quick to blame others for her poor class structure and lack of prep. Decent person but has no idea how to teach and makes this class an anxiety-induced headache.

She is very disorganized and has no idea on how to properly teach information. Quizzes are worth 17% of your grade, not fair. They are due before we learn the content. The piazza is never answered. If you complain about the quizzes, she says it's your fault. I loved biodiversity, now I don't. Please, save me from this semester.

Disorganized. Lectures, content & hw is super easy but the exams are all trick questions that tank your grade & averages were lower than what's expected for this kind of content. She is patronizing when you ask for help. I enjoy biodiversity as a subject, but this is such a frustrating & stressful class.
Do not take! Says one thing then the next class says the complete opposite. Very confusing and the material isn't taught very well.
You'll hate biodiversity by the end of the semester.

analysis.name: Deb Aikat
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 91 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I honestly didn't love this class, I just loved Deb. Hilarious, kind, caring man. when he says "Dean King, katria, veasey and I care about your success in mejo101" he means it. basically all guest lectures. most are boring some are good. Katria is a goddess. a couple easy papers and tests w/ very clear criteria

Deb is very funny. The class is all guest lectures though so he only taught at most two class periods. Easy A if you show up to class. Final and midterm are all based on guest lecturers and assigned readings. Easy papers. Don't take the final as a joke though it is 40% of your grade.

Deb is SUPER nice and the tests are very easy- mostly common sense and based on all of the readings he gives us. There were a few projects, all of which were graded easy as long as you follow directions. The lectures weren't ever helpful (it's mostly Deb asking if anyone has any questions), but overall would recommend- Deb's a great guy!

Deb's class is not challenging if you show up to lectures (attendance is mandatory) and follow assignments' requirements (his grading is very clear). The content is not difficult and you do not have to deeply understand it to succeed in the class, knowing the terms/events discussed in class and their impact on media is sufficient.

Super energetic and passionate about the subject. Assignments provide a clear rubric and grading generally isn't harsh, granted that good effort is shown. Lectures aren't super helpful but all test material goes along with the readings and slides he provides. Very fun class.

analysis.name: Aidan Young
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: His handwriting is extremely difficult to read. He knows the material well, but struggles to teach it; textbook has more clear explanations. He also gives inaccurate approximations on where students are on the curve throughout the year. Each exam I scored within his "A range" but the final curve didn't align with his mid-semester updates at all.

Extremely confusing and boring lectures. He comes off as condescending, but I don't think he means to. He didn't decide on the grading scale, but it's stupid and unfair, so FYI: A 91-100, B 85-90, C 77-84, D 66-76, F 0-65. Imagine getting an 84, but it's actually a C. And the inconsistent point ranges (9 point range for A, 5 point range for B, etc)

Aidan knows the material well but tended to rush through lectures, however, I took this course over the summer so that's understandable. His handwriting was hard to read at first but over time I got used to it. He responded to most questions on piazza within a couple hours. His tests were doable and there weren't any surprises and the EC was a plus

Besides the fact that Aidan curves, I don't have one good thing to say about the class. Homework was horribly graded as he takes out points for everything wrong but doesn't give you points for everything correct. The exams were super difficult and much worse than previous exams. The whole semester was stressful and I was lucky to end up with a B.

Hard to understand and often taught too fast. His handwriting was incomprehensible and I often had to teach myself topics. Seemed condescending when asked questions and was not transparent at all about grading. The grading scale was very harsh and punished all students who got less than an A. Knows the material very well, but a horrible teacher.

analysis.name: Jayasharee Aikat
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I ended up taking COMP110 just to maintain a 15 hour course load, and it ended up being one of the bests classes I've ever taken here.  Professor Aikat is very clear with instructions, and drops your lowest assignment grade, which makes life so much easier.  Lectures were fun, and she is quite funny at times.

This class definitely required effort. Lectures were ok; easy to tune out or get lost. However office hours is very helping and the assignments help you understand a lot; that why they are worth 50% of final grade. The midterm and final are not so horrible. As long as you understand basics, you will do fine on those. Got 70% on both and got an A.

I took this class Spring 2014; it was 300 kids in GNS lecture hall. The first half of the class is easy; the second is confusing. She had 5 personal office hours a week and 10 with the TAs. She offered 9 points on your final letter grade throughout the semester. Do the work; the first half gets 60% of your grade and is easy. Tests are tricky.

Midterm and final were sort of tricky, but similar to study guide. Programming assignments are 50% of your grade so if you do all of them and study for test you can at least make a B. TAs are very helpful. She gives extra credit opportunities to add 3 points on to your final grade. Class was boring, but she has daily attendance quizzes.

The second half of the semester the material is a lot more challenging and confusing. It is really easy to get lost in lecture, but going to office hours helps out a lot. Parts of the assignments are difficult, but there aren't many and you can go to office hours and knock them out in two hours or so tops.

analysis.name: Akaa Ayangeakaa
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The TA teaches, grades and creates homework for the lab section. Professor simply gives the recitation lecture. In those lectures he is a slow speaker, does not get through all the material in a timely manner. He is also a poor communicator outside of the classroom. He once forgot to tell us about an assignment and then tried to blame us.

Lecture plus supplemeting with textbook make the material clear and manageable. Fun lecturer and engages with students. Grades exams rather strictly, (i.e., you want textbook work) but is very lenient when it comes to getting points back. Akaa wants you to succeed, and he was very forgiving with final rounding. Put in the work and you will do well!

I took 281L with Dr. Ayangeakaa, and again I found that he was a caring professor that only wanted the class to learn and succeed. Homework sets are a little disorganized and can be long, but the lectures are well-structured and clear, and include examples to work as a class or in small groups. Tests are fair and he prepares you well with examples.

Great professor. The midterm exams were both a bit disorganized, but he was honest and fair when grading them. Doesn't take attendance traditionally, but gives pop quizzes throughout the semester as a substitute. Overall very understanding and a funny guy in lecture.

He's a very decent professor. He's a funny guy and clearly knows what he is talking about, and he expects that from you as well. If you put in the work, you'll do just fine. Only reason I didn't get an A is because I was lazy.

analysis.name: Akram Al-Turk
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Akram is a really cool guy that knows a lot about subject matter. The class is pretty laid back and free-flowing and he tries to help the class seems to not be able to grasp a concept. The class isn't SUPER easy, but considering that all the tests are open-note, take-home tests, you should be able to get a solid grade as long as you put in the time

Akram was well-liked by everyone in SOCI 133. He does a great job facilitating discussion and connecting material on a grand scale. The class is consistently interesting, and Akram is always willing to make time to help students that needed it. Students learn not only about political trends on an abstract level, but also perform data analysis.

Best instructor I have ever had. Very understanding during pandemic. Listened to what the students had to say about their situations & really took that into consideration. Not a hard grader at all as long as you follow the rubrics he provides. Lack of pressure in this class really allowed me to learn a lot. Textbook/readings are provided for free.

EE's tend to be lots of work but I found the amount of reading and writing required for this course outside of class to be hard to keep up with, especially when you're spending about 3 hours a week volunteering for the course and not getting any additional credit for it. Disorganized, but a reasonable prof who will work with you.
Seriously the nicest guy. You can tell he really cares about his students and he's super easy going.

analysis.name: Patrick Akos
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Tough grader Not much to grade Lots of paper/book to read Pop quizzes

A class that you get out what you put in. Akos is reading heavy and this takes a lot of time but it helps you understand class comments. Stickler on grading (points taken off easily) but a cool guy and fun professor.
Professor critically grades. There are group based projects and if you are in a bad group you suffer. Will not move you grade up even if half a point away from a higher grade. Overall bad experience.

Akos is easily the best professor I've had at UNC! He is a tough grader though!!!!!! If you say one thing off or wrong, that's half a point off of something you can only get 3 points on. He truly cares about his students and commits to the material he is teaching. Wouldn't call this an easy A class, more like an easy B. Love Akos, not his grading!!
Unfair grader, does not bump your grade even if half a point from next letter grade.

analysis.name: John Akin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Class consists of multiple guest speakers who lecture about boring things. There's a huge final group project and too many readings. The class is super boring and you don't learn anything useful.
If you don't pass this class, you're not alive.

analysis.name: Akilah Swinton
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class wasn't that hard. Just had to go to take class take the notes that she wanted you to know. Read textbook and get a general idea of whats going on. Not too bad other wise.
Very nice and very helpful professor.  We did a lot of group assignments which were sometimes a little elementary but the class is really easy.
She seemed to really care about us understanding the material and doing well in the class. I really liked the videos and guest speakers.

analysis.name: Heather Apple
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Heather is incredible! She is the best professor I have had at UNC. She provides feedback in every class and encourages us to produce our best work. Additionally, she is a creative genius, always coming up with ideas on the spot. A true professor of practice. Thanks to her facilitation, our class became friends. TAKE HER and cherish your time.

Heather was awesome! She is so cool and kind and her industry experience makes her an awesome resource. Assignments were easy and graded generously. You're required to stand up and present your work almost every day, but it was never intimidating and was just an opportunity to get detailed feedback. Definitely take her if you can!

I could not recommend Heather more. Class is primarily presentation-based, but she gives super in-depth, constructive feedback. Lots of guest speakers and practical, real-world advice. I learned so much from Heather and I wish she taught more classes because I would absolutely take more with her.

analysis.name: April Munroe
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: All hail April Munroe. She is such a nice and caring ENGL105 professor. She made the class fun and interesting. She was a very relaxed grader and made it very hard to get below an A lol. I am a STEM kid and hated English but she made me love going to her class.
April is amazing! She's very nice, her class is fun and easy. You do a lot of work in groups with a lot of independence. Very little homework, and a pretty lenient grader. Take her class!!!

April is such a caring teacher. She is always understanding of students needs and the pressures of being a student. She uses a very creative connection between literature/writing and conspiracy theories to make the class interesting and educational. Although there were more assignments than expected, I enjoyed doing them as we chose the topics.

This class was pretty chill and super easy. It's pretty much like a book club. 2 papers based on analysis of your chosen book. Midterm was super easy, she gave us the test the class before. Final exam was to make a playlist on another book of our choice. Don't even have to talk in class, just read books you plan on doing papers and final on.

Pretty standard class. Four papers. Very heavily discussion based. Really thought provoking class about mystery novels and conspiracy theories. One of the better and more fun classes I have taken at UNC. Pretty easy to get a good grade too. Didn't read all the books but will still probably make an A.

analysis.name: Apurba Chakraborty
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This guy is the man. Is very approachable and friendly and wants you to succeed in his classes rather than perform poorly. The presentation you have to do forces you out of your comfort zone and helps you learn about the psychology behind legislature and political issues and bias present today. 10 page paper but makes it an interesting task.

This guy really wants his students to succeed, and while he won't tolerate slacking, he definitely strives to allow everyone to get an A if they are willing to work. Participation matters, but he does a great job of explaining the readings, so just skimming them works. One ten-page paper, but no other homework.

Professor Chakraborty is great. He's not an absurdly hard grader like most of the Poli profs I've had. You can tell he really cares about his students and honestly just wants you to learn something. Definitely a solid choice.

analysis.name: April Lawson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's one of the most understanding and sweetest professors at UNC. I was hesitant to take this class because I had an interest in creative writing but I wasn't entirely sure if I'd succeed in the class. Lawson makes it a great experience and supports you through any issues you have.

April is not only one of the nicest English professors I've ever had but also one of the most creative and considerate. One ten page paper and daily pop quizzes for ENGL 130. Class discussions are always riveting and her paper feedback is so thoughtful. Definitely take a creative writing class with her if you get the chance.

April is super nice and chill - the class is very laid back and not difficult if you do the reading (which arent demanding or difficult but are necessary). There are daily quizzes on the readings, and a final short story. A good class to take 'for fun'.
omg so talented, please stay @ unc forever

analysis.name: Ajay Gandecha
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Me when a grad student teaches better than the actual professors

A unicorn in the CS dept, Ajay is a professor that understands what it means to teach to an audience topics that are difficult in concept. Each lecture is really interesting, and the assignments are so much fun to do. Super understanding, passionate, and caring, two midterms (really easy and worth less than attendance), otherwise all projects!

Ajay is the goat. It's very apparent how much he cares about teaching and how much effort he puts into this class. One of the most useful classes here if you want to go into SWE and I learned lots of useful things from his class. Each assignment is a fun project, and there is a final group project. 2 midterms both pretty easy.

Ajay covers so much content but makes the lectures interesting and engaging, drawing parallels to real world examples. He also introduces projects and homework that are applicable and it's definitely one of the most exciting and fun classes I've taken

One of the best structured courses I've taken and useful for people interested in web dev (whether new or having prior experience). Ajay has an infectious enthusiasm and is both a great lecturer and super approachable outside of class. Programming assignments are frequent but reasonable. Also includes a final project to tie everything together.

analysis.name: Mandy Cooper
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took the class in Fall of 2025. Class was TA-graded, but Dr. Cooper structures it well and doesn't set expectations terribly high. Show up, follow along, and you're in a solid spot to get a good grade. Course was mainly surface-level, though definitely more covered than your typical person would know. Lectures weren't boring or overly interesting.

As a person, Professor Cooper is amazing. She truly cares about us as students, even in a large class. The way she set up the midterm and final was great. However, my TA who graded all my essays was unfair and difficult in grading considering it's a gen-ed. The lectures also weren't the most engaging although she is very passionate about her work.

Dr. Cooper is very knowledgable! She is passionate about what she teaches and is easy to talk to and encourages group discussions. Your TA will be grading everything so I would say to make sure to go to both their office hours as well as Dr.Cooper's if you feel like you should have had higher scoring/asking how to improve for future assignments.

The lectures could get a little long, esp if you're familiar with US history already, but Dr. Cooper was super cool and knowledgable, regardless. Her assignments are very clear, but you are being graded by a TA who can be inconsistent and give little feedback due to the volume of papers. office hours and the writing center can help you do well!

Cooper is super nice and caring. Lectures were very hit or miss imo; some were super interesting, and others felt like a chore. Lots of writing but graded pretty easily (may have been specific to my TA). No tests at all and offers a ton of extra credit; pretty easy A overall, but there are definitely more interesting gen-ed history classes.

analysis.name: Amanuel Gebremichael
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I really liked Professor Gebremichael's lectures and the group discussions! If you aren't comfortable speaking in front of the class, you may not score well in participation though. The material is very interesting and he often incorporated current politics into class. The exams were difficult but curved very generously (15% curve on the midterm).

I enjoyed Prof. AG's sense of humor and how much he cared about our individual opinions in class discussions. Compared to other poli prof.'s, he is definitely more difficult. The class is graded on 3 five questions quizzes, a midterm, and the final. If you don't do well on all of the quizzes, it'll be very difficult to get your grade up. He curves!

Prof Gebremichael is down to earth and engaging during his lectures. We had very interesting discussions and his quizzes were super easy. Don't underestimate the tests though, they are pretty hard and have a detailed written portion. The exams were based on the lectures, so I never did the reading and did just fine. Definitely take this class!

Professor Gebremichael was awesome. I had him for my African American Economics and Inequality FYS, and he had great content, excellent and funny lectures, and was an overall great professor. His grading is stricter for the final presentation and paper, but he gives you more than enough notice to complete them well in advance.

Super fun guy with interesting lectures. You get 3 unexcused absences and my notes were just the slides copied down. didnt read the textbook and did fine. make sure to study for quizzes because if you bomb one you have to do really well on the midterm/final. He curves well though. Try to speak at least once every class as participation matters.

analysis.name: Angela  Ambrosio
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Angela is one of the best Spanish professors that I have ever had. She is an extremely fair grader but also provides good feedback. She made each class fun and not boring, even when using slides to teach. She is hilarious and always made class feel like a welcoming place, and she gives you lots of practice to prepare you for the tests and final.

Angela is so sweet and entertaining, but she genuinely wants to you to learn and understand topics in class. I never once dreaded going to her class. Participation is required and recorded throughout the semester, so try to answer questions frequently even if your not 100% sure. Definitely take Angela's class if you have the opportunity.
Very doable SPAN 105 class. She was kind and graded fairly, and class was genuinly fun to attend. Participation does matter a lot, so keep that in mind.

analysis.name: Ami Ward
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: ** EMES 101L** she is the best. checks off your labs! she understands you are taking this lab for the credit. Took her at 8am bc of how much you want to take her lab time.
Great TA. She was very helpful and understanding. Reviewed necessary material and explained the labs thoroughly. Would recommend.

For EMES 101. Ami was the TA for this class, and I'm not completely sure she knew what she was doing. She didn't answer a lot of questions thoroughly and was not always available for office hours (consistently rescheduled them) or in class. Nice person though.
Easy class. Amy is great with giving feed back. Not a hard class just turn in stuff in time and review notes.
Such an amazing TA! Very helpful during office hours!

analysis.name: Amy Chambless
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I absolutely adore Professor Chambless. She is a fantastic professor. In-class time is typically spent practicing skills, so I would recommend taking time to read/take notes on the assigned textbook pages so the content doesn't sneak up on you for the test. Grades fairly and generously, and always gives clear feedback. Take ITAL 101 with her!

She's very participation heavy, which makes sense with an introductory language course. She's always happy to help and offer office hours, extra practice, and support when students ask for it. She's very patient and encouraging, the class is a very welcoming environment.

I highly recommend Dr.Chambless for Ital 101 and 102; she is an amazing lecturer and has a lot of empathy towards her students. She grades fairly and provides plenty of feedback, as well as resources, to help you improve your Italian. She is very knowledgeable about the textbook content and is always available to meet with students.
She was really nice and really made sure the students understood the material. I slacked off pretty bad and failed the first 2 test but she worked with me and I ended up doing ok. Don't fall behind.

She is very friendly and encouraging! Classes have a lot of fun activities to encourage constant learning.  There are short quizzes (vocab or the grammar concept you are learning), but they are easy and only count for 5% of your overall grade. There are also assignments w/each unit to record a conversation about a certain topic with a partner.

analysis.name: Amalia Ashley
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ashley is wonderful! We had a group book club project, which was really interesting and something I haven't seen before in a class at UNC yet. She clearly cares about her students and makes sure everyone feels comfortable and safe. Her feedback on assignments is great, and she tells you exactly what to fix and why you got points off.

*wgst 340* Professor Ashley's decent. You can tell she cares about the material. LOTS of reading and weekly journals that are pretty tedious and boring. The material was interesting if you are interested in the topic l. Has barely graded all semester so no idea what my grade will be. Service learning for apples was the best part of the class!

If you are interested in the content you will love this class. class is split into lecture, activity, and discussion. You can miss 3 of each. She covers a wide range of topics and truly wants you to enjoy the class. Exams are online with clear feedback for how to improve. One of my favorite WGST classes at UNC!

I loved Dr.Ashley's class. super interesting but you def have to do the readings. She had a lecture, activity, discussion setup for her MWF class which I really enjoyed. Had to read a book for a book club but it was engaging and not overly strenuous. You will learn a lot and should get an A if you do your work and participate.
*WGST 270 Women and Sport. Good lectures and discussion about modern topics. I have no interest in sports but learned a lot from this class.

analysis.name: Amanda DelVecchia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Gave many basic assignments, did them all well. Graded 2 months after assigned, I got 7/9 8/12 etc. Couldn't change my strategy for doing those because it was end of year. She gave surprise grade # of perusall comments we made. Never told us to write comments on all but 2. Got a 14/30 on it dropped my grade by 7% got me a B. Super unfair ridiculous

Dr. DelVecchia is sweet but her class is disorganized and her grading criteria is unclear. There's no way to know what she will decide deduct points for in written assignments. 591 needs a recitation to justify the amount of labs. The pacing and structure is nonexistent, and she is unavailable outside of her office hour.

Dr. DelVecchia is the best professor at UNC hands down! She genuinely cares for her students and wants to help them achieve their goals. She will work with you to find what you want to do then help you figure out how to get there. I haven't has a professor as influential as Dr. DelVecchia in my four years at UNC
wouldnt take again. Lectures were hard to follow. Everyone completed activities at a different pace. Grading criteria for quizzes was unclear. Not enough guidance
She is super approachable and passionate. She sticks to policies in the syllabus and doesn't give extensions as much as other professors have because she wants to keep the course consistent.

analysis.name: Andrea Bohlman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Andrea is fantastic. I would happily take another class with her. I would also give her a 5 if this class wasn't pure fluff. This is more beneficial than music history? The curriculum is disjointed nonsense and the final project was a show and tell of everyone's musical interests. I think music conservatories would laugh if they observed MUSC270.

Dr. Bohlman clearly has a passion and interest in her lectures. She looks forward to participation, reading over the short assignments, and gives great feedback on the midterm. She takes students' workloads into account when scheduling her big deadlines/midterm, clearly showing empathy for her students.

I beg the UNC Music department to do away with this new curriculum. Dr. Bohlman was fantastic and clear but the material she was given to work with was nearly nonexistent. This course caused multiple people to DROP the music major because they have decided to stop teaching anything useful. The dumbing down of the music major at UNC is sad to see.

The main issue with this course was the course itself, not the professor. Bohlman is a zealous, involved professor who will help you with anything-- academic or personal. That said, I didn't learn a lot in this course. The lectures tended to be all over the place and slightly unrelated to each other. Homework is not required, tho assigned.

Andrea is alright; no more, no less. Similar to my experience with her MUSC 120, we learned absolute nonsense the whole semester. We basically studied music through unguided interpretation. Andrea has a knack for calling on students but not really caring for their responses & for giving unclear essay criteria, but overall this class is an easy A.

analysis.name: Amy Cooke
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Amy Cooke's grading criteria was never clear and it took her months to return graded assignments. She also regularly assigned readings at 10pm or later the night before they were due. My favorite part of this class was when she didn't start entering grades until 2 days after the final exam. If you like organization this class is not for you.

Great lecturer and an incredible woman! Her classes are engaging and relevant. However, she is spread too thin. She doesn't have time to invest in her students outside of class or to grade assignments in a timely manner. Two-page papers not graded for 30-45 days. Reading sometimes not posted until 10:00pm night before.

Dr. Cooke is unorganized at best. I found her lectures extremely hard to follow and the criteria for many or her assignments unclear. Her tests are not super hard, but she grades them with little explanation and isn't generous. She is a chronic complainer, grades slowly and will change her mind about test dates and course policies.

If you want to literally never even know your grade in a class then take this class. She makes it a grade to go to office hours and then complains when you go because she is hungry. Every exam is not graded until 1 class before the next exam, most unorganized, rude, procrastinating professor ever and 100% has favorites.

Dr. Cooke is one of my fav UNC professors. Highly recommend ENEC325; truly a class that will make you think and write about complex, important, and relevant world problems related to water accessibility and its implications for humanity. Also, such a funny, loving, passionate, and intelligent person who makes lectures feel like conversations.

analysis.name: Alexis Gillmore
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
She doesn't communicate with her TAs at all. They say my design is fine, then she claims it doesn't meet expectations. No clear grading criteria, completely inconsistent. She's passive-aggressive when you ask questions and dismisses your effort by saying it looks “too easy,” so it doesn't count the day before the due date.  This course sucks.
RUN

Nice person, but not good at teaching. Instructions for assignments are unclear, and grading feels pretty nitpicky. I lost points on a 3D puzzle assignment even though I made six pieces because she said they weren't “distinct enough.” Also be prepared for random pop quizzes on stuff if she thinks people aren't paying attention during lecture.

Do not take this class for a focus capacity. Easy A, but way too much work to justify a gen ed. It is the work of two classes combined. It is very based on group work, and the grading criteria is slightly unclear. Dr. Gillmore is really nice, and is an understanding professor that wants you to succeed but the structure of the class is not worth it.

Unless you really like building things, I would not recommend taking APPL 110 to satisfy the focus capacity. Nothing you do is very difficult, but it all takes a ton of time. Prof. Gillmore is an energetic lecturer and generally amiable, but grading is inconsistent. TAs grade leniently, but she doesn't. You don't know who is grading what either.

Dr. Gillmore is a lovely person, and largely very fair. The assignments did have some confusing guidelines, because the class is taught by multiple professors with countering philosophies. Even with hellish partners in the two major group projects, this class was fairly easy. Start assignments ASAP and have fun in the makerspace.

analysis.name: Alicia Monroe
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Good professor, assigns a lot of long readings but they are discussed in class so even if you don't make it through all of them you'll be able to keep up. quizzes are open book and online with plenty of time to take them, exams were in class essays. Gives a lot of good feedback especially on writing but isn't a harsh grader

Dr. Monroe is a really sweet lady; you can tell she is passionate about what she teaches. There are a lot of readings and long documentary-style videos that you should read/scan and watch (in 2x speed) to help prepare you for lectures/quizzes. Most assignments were due the last 4-5 weeks of the semester, definitely could've been spaced out better.

Doctor Monroe is passionate about what she teaches and that is clear in class. Everything I learned in this class was super interesting and connected to each other well. The only really difficult thing about this class was the amount of reading. While some of the articles are really long, reading them is necessary. Little homework.

Dr. Monroe was very passionate. The readings in 286 were lengthy, you can survive with summaries. All quizzes were open note, open book, directly from her slideshows so they aren't hard to get a 100. On other little assignments grading was a little tedious. The midterm and final are very easy to score high if you prepare well.

The readings/assignments aren't necessarily "hard," they just take a bit of time and grading is strict. Also, she tends to be a bit of a talker and is strangely obsessed with the idea of "bonding"
 and getting to know your "colleagues"... erm, anyway. Nice woman otherwise, I just had a hard time connecting sometimes.

analysis.name: Ann Matthysse
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: No. Never again. Just don't, take it online at any other school. Just not with her. She brings in grant money so somehow they give her access to students. But honestly she should not be within a 20 mile radius of a student. Thank you for singlehandedly ruining my love of microbiology, business it is..

Worst professor I have ever had at Carolina. Every day our lecture consisted of her making general statements that did not match up with the power points. Almost every test you take you will have to resubmit for a regrade because of how many mistakes that are made. I can say that this class has been more stress than it's worth and she needs to go.

Dr. Matthysse is not a good teacher. Her lectures are rambling and go off on random tangents that she tests you on. She flips the switch from sweet old lady to insane and evil in a heartbeat. Tests are really hard and its pretty difficult to study for them. Overall would not recommend taking this class. Look at Mcro 251 instead!!

Horrible teacher.  You will learn very little and be engaged even less.  All you do is memorize old tests because knowing the material from the book won't help you at all.  She even tells you that if you do the reading you will make a C- on her tests.  Condescending, pretentious and not at all helpful.  Read a book on your own.  You'd be better off

The worst educator/person I have ever met in my entire life. Extremely derogatory and just disrespectful to any student she is talking to. The class was unnecessarily difficult which is a shame because I was really interested in the material. To study for exams you studied previous exams and none of the material taught in class or in the textbook.

analysis.name: Alejandra Gaeta-Avila
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is a super nice professor and she will help you if you don't understand things. Workload was fairly light- the hw isn't always helpful but its always super easy. helpful to use chat to break it down when its confusing. Quizzes and exams were superrrrrr easy- she gives you a refrence guide telling you exactly what to know- so just know that!!

She's a great professor who genuinely cares about her students. There's alot of homework and the exams are tough, but she's always willing to help and makes sure you understand the material.
