not a very friendly teacher, other friends in classes would get small cards to help them on quizzes and other exams like oral quizzes. Good teacher, but another teacher would definetely be better
The class is not easy but she makes sure everyone understands the material. Participation is important. She is a great professor but there is daily homework's
Very fun class even if you don't enjoy Spanish. She makes sure everyone knows the material in class and is attentive to students needs. Homework is informative and good (but not fun) practice.

analysis.name: Martha Alexander
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Sra. Alexander is phenomenal! She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Homework is limited and if you prepare for tests, you'll do great. She's always there to help you and with her help the class isn't too difficult.

went to office hours for help, she implied she thought I wasn't trying or simply was not smart- offered no help to improve my understanding. I left feeling discouraged, the opposite of the purpose of office hours. She gave me a low participation grade even though I spoke 2-3+ times in every class, missing only 2 (both excused). absolutely absurd.

Don't be fooled by her kindness or her sarcasm. Tries to be funny but makes Spanish harder than it is. Participation is RNG, exams are 50%, and all papers and speaking is subjective to her harsh grading. Does not answer questions properly in class. Had to self study and learn to pass with a decent grade in the class. Take any other 203 professor.

Don't listen to the good reviews that say she is helpful, can teach, and is caring. She doesn't answer questions properly (literally said "I think that is the correct answer because it just is"), grades very harshly (points off for grammar), participation is biased and 10% of grade and not a free A. Take literally any other professor for 203.

Professor Alexander is super laid back and does not have heavy expectations. She doesn't expect you to be fluent in Spanish, and reviews a lot of key concepts. She grades very leniently, and she's very transparent about exam content. We spend most of class just working in groups; it's very low stakes, and casual. I would take her if you can!

analysis.name: Sudhanshu Ashu Handa
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Love ashu!! Very willing to help outside of class, lots of jokes throughout lecture to keep us engaged, and lots of step by step help to make sure we are really following what we are doing! TAs were great as well. Loved the treats ashu brought in (though wish we got to try his brownie recipe). If you can take a Class with ashu, do it!

Professor Ashu is an amazing. He's incredibly engaging, bakes cookies for his students, is clearly passionate about the material, and makes his expectations/what we need to know for exams very clear. If you attend the lectures, utilize your recitation TA's and their office hours, and take good notes you won't have a problem in this class!

Ashu is super nice—he brought us cookies/cupcakes and even gifts when he traveled for research. The class itself isn't super hard, and the curves were also really generous. As long as you come to the class, do the problem sets, and attend review sessions, you will do fine. Favorite class & professor—definitely + highly recommended!!!

Professor Ashu is a really caring professor (he baked us treats often and got us gifts when he travelled)! He doesn't provide powerpoints for his class, so attending his classes would be really helpful. And the exams are hard and he's tough grader, but his exam grades and the overall grades are curved generously, so it's not too bad.
TA Laraib Kamal has anger issues.

analysis.name: Ashton Rooney
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Ashton Rooney encourages students to participate in Spanish, and he grew my confidence. He doesn't care if you aren't proficient, as long as you try. He is lenient with grading, even though he does have to follow the Span 203 grading guidelines. His class is engaging, fun, and educational. If you are nervous to take Span 203, definitely take his.

One of the best profs I've had. He genuinely cares and doesn't expect perfection, just effort. I hadn't taken Spanish in four years, but Ashton helped us learn and stay engaged. He doesn't control the class structure, but he makes the most of it. The tests are tough. Prep and do VHL early. I am not the best at Spanish and still managed an A-.

I came into this class super scared because I hadn't taken Spanish since my freshman year of high school. However, Ashton made it such a supportive and fun environment, and I ended up doing great on all the exams, essays, etc., because he focused on building our confidence.

analysis.name: Alyssa Byrnes
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 113 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Incredible professor, my first time taking any sort of comp sci class and I love it now. Explains things very well and has a very clear and forgiving grading system. Very easy A if you show up to class and do the assignments on time, don't be scared by the "12-15 hrs/wk" they talk about I studied a couple hours for each quiz and ended with a 97.

Pass/failed. Didn't post recordings, which for material that has meticulous steps and reasons for them makes it incredibly hard to review a concept more than just seeing the end result. Tests made up 90% of the grade, and were taken entirely from homework questions. Rewarded cramming over really understanding the material imo. Still a nice person.
Everyone knows she's the best! COMP 455 is known to be hard, but she explained the concepts in a way that they stick with you forever.

This was my first time coding, and Dr. Byrnes was amazing! She explained things clearly and was very nice. It was fairly easy to pick up the material. EC is given if you turn in exercises early. Quiz practice questions are harder than the quiz questions. Practice memory diagrams, go to office hours, go to quiz review sessions, and you will be set!

Definitely the best professor to take COMP 110 with. As someone who had never touched a line of code before in my life, lectures were extremely interesting and the content never felt like too much. Assignments were dispersed throughout the semester and never felt like too much. Just practice memory diagrams before each exam and you'll do great.

analysis.name: Idris Assani
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 72 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Before taking this class I loved calculus. It was so frustrating taking his tests because they were nothing like the homework assignments or the problems in the book. That isn't even the worst of it. He doesn't give partial credit although he says he does. You could spend 20 minutes working one test problem and make a small mistake towards the end
Avoid at all cost! GPA killer.
GOAT of a professor. Super awesome guy and really cares about the material and about his students. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! He will help you. Super great guy, really recommend.

Prof Assani cares about his students. His lectures make 521 like learning a new way of thinking. Go to office hours and ask for help, he wants you to succeed, so he will help. My sole complaint was the disparity in difficulty between this year's final and the material we had seen all semester/last year's final, but he does challenge you to think.

Professor Assani is incredibly intelligent. You'll understand that after hearing his first lecture. But not all intelligent people are great professors. Professor Assani rushes through tons of materials in one lecture each week, leaving the other day purely for quizzes. You'll more than likely be relying on online resources to learn the material.

analysis.name: Ashley Anderson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 122 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Great class and professor overall, but didn't love the communication between professor and I. She's very nice but unavailable. I showed up to her office hours once, waited an hour and a half just to find out that she was in Europe and didn't notify her students. This was a week before finals. But everything other than that about the class was fine.

Professor Anderson is disgustingly and dangerously educated. She makes lectures engaging and is very knowledgeable in pretty much everything she talks about. Attendance is required. There's weekly quizzes with five questions and two papers, along with the midterm and final that make up your grade. She challenges you, but an A is possible!

I took POLI 130 with her, and she was pretty great! Informative lectures, clearly knows her subject matter, and encourages class participation. Readings are the main homework, and are necessary to know for the midterm and final. Additionally, I would recommend checking the lecture handouts for the key terms, because those will also be on the tests.

no one cares that she went to Stanford and Harvard. this is a 100-level class. she's unaccommodating: i had to take weekly quizzes while hospitalized. grading feels TA-dependent, As are rare (94 = A, no rounding). i was docked for recitation participation despite university excused absences. not an easy A, and she acts like it's your only class.

Super interesting lecture and class material. Anderson is incredibly knowledgeable. None of the assignments are very difficult; however, almost impossible to get an A, given 80% of your grade comes from just 4 assignments (2 papers and a written midterm and final / have to really crush the papers) + extra credit assignments were really dumb imo.

analysis.name: Asya Passinsky
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I've heard Philosophy at UNC is pretty tough, but Prof. Passinsky made the class as interesting as she could and she brought in philosophers to talk with us. The daily amount of work is not actually that bad, but the papers are crucial. She doesn't give specific criteria but if you make your paper topic specific and overly clear you'll be fine.

Since this is a philosophy class, your grade will heavily depend on participation and papers. If you are not a good writer, I would NOT recommend taking this class because one bad grade on a paper can cause you to fail. It would have been extremely helpful if the professor looked over rough drafts since two papers were over half our grade.

Professor Passinksy is really intelligent and she puts a lot of effort into her classes and gives her students opportunities to actually talk to the philosophers we discuss in class. She is a tough grader but she is available in office hours to talk about your paper before submitting. If you're not a good writer, skip this class.

I loved Dr P's class so much I decided to minor in philosophy. She seems cold at first but she's just like that. If you reach out to her she's super nice and the course itself is super interesting. If you have a chance to take her classes definitely do, it's rewarding but not crazy hard.

analysis.name: Ashok Krishnamurthy
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I know some foreign professors are bad, this one is NOT. He just came from Ohio and taught this semester's 116 kind of tag-team with Dr. Ahalt. Both were extremely helpful and practical. Assignments were well-designed and they were flexible on dates. Lectures were good, not required. I highly recommend Dr. Krishnamurthy for any level class!

COMP 116 is tough no matter what but Ashok is by far the best option. He's funny and a patient lecturer. His extra-credit/take-home policy for midterms are way fairer than Majikes' and honestly saved my grade. He also offers a ton of options for extra-credit integrated into the assignments/worksheets and he doesn't take attendance. Really cool dude

Ashok is such an amazing professor. Though I'm not sure why he is teaching, because he is a research professor and that's his main focus. Regardless, he is very caring and will curve exams based on the class average He also lets you fix your midterms, and your correction is 70% of the midterm's final grade. Overall, and easy class and a great prof

This class is definitely a bit different than most other classes in that learning is HIGHLY dependent on you doing the assignments and understanding the mechanism behind it. That being said, the class is pretty chill and Dr. Krishnamurthy definitely goes over a lot of useful, fun, and interesting material in the class. It's manageable.

Ashok was a very kind and considerate professor however was not the best lecturer. The lectures were mainly watching professors code and follow along without a lot of explanation as to why things were done. This course would be much easier if you have an understanding of programming beforehand, however is not impossible without any.

analysis.name: John Arnold
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Arnold reignited my passion for creating art. Although I hadn't taken an organized class since early high school, I was able to produce detailed drawings I was proud of by the end of the semester because of Professor Arnold's guidance and encouragement. I truly believe any student under his instruction is capable of immense growth.

This was the last class I took to finish my degree and I was so happy! Mr. Arnold was great at teaching the fundamentals of drawing. He got us out of our heads about perfectionism. I gained a lot of skills in this class than I have in past art classes. Bonus, he plays great music in class during drawing time! Highly recommend!!

He is very clear in his guidelines but is also very flexible and willing to work with you. He teaches the basics but encourages self-exploration of the topics. There is no textbook, and there are also no tests, just two portfolios made up of classwork and a final project. Very good class for improving your fundamentals and learning technique.

Phenomenal instructor! Incredibly kind and cares about your individual success and growth. He's easily accessible and makes his expectations incredibly clear. He makes learning the basics of drawing fun and interesting and gives amazing feedback.

analysis.name: Arthur Eddy
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: His teaching style was often disorganized and course expectations/grading criteria weren't communicated clearly. Assignments required a significant amount of work, sometimes without sufficient guidance or clarification. Lots of guest speakers. Overall, the instructor did not seem very flexible or understanding when students raised concerns.

Prof Eddy was great, very accessible, and helpful with questions. There is no rubric for any assignments, which made it sometimes difficult to understand feedback and grades. The class is boring because its a prereq, but Prof Eddy did provide good advice about the real world and had educational guest lectures.

I learned a great deal in Prof Eddy's class. He cared for all his students. There is a ton of group project which makes class fun. There were a few guest speakers from different industries that added to the class. I highly recommend his class.

I don't go here, because I'm in high school, but this guy is my godfather and I would like to mention that. He's pretty good at being a godfather, I think, but please don't let him wear suits. Otherwise someone might mistake him for Jeff Bezos and that would be bad.

This class was a bit different from my other classes, but in a good way. His class is combo of lectures, group projects and guests to speak to the class along with the main project. I learned a lot from his class.

analysis.name: Ariannah Kubli
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Take her! Absolutely amazing she really cares for her students and it is very easy to earn an A if you turn everything in on time. She uses grading contracts so if you meet all the requirements you can get the grade you desire. Super nice, projects are engaging and she provides clear and constructive feedback.

Professor Kubli is kind. She was always accessible and willing to help. It is clear that she cares about her students. The projects were not too hard and you got to choose what you wanted to write about for all of them. The class is contract grading, so if you do the work and go to class you will get an A.

She is the best. I hope she stays a teacher because she has enthusiasm and the smarts to back it up. Such an easy class and not too easy where it was boring. If you're checking rate my prof. to see if she's a good teacher, the million 5/5 reviews should tell you YES

She is amazing and super flexible whenever you need her to be. very very easy and straight forward class but also super interesting. The class is what you want it to be because every project is very personalized and targeted to your interests. HIGHLY recommend her!

I definitely recommend Ms. Kubli for ENGL 105. The assignments for the class are actually interesting and she is a super fair grader. She's also very forgiving if you need an extension or extra help for an assignment.

analysis.name: Aria Tsoulouhas

review_highlights.comment: I took RELI-101 with professor Tsoulouhas this semester and it ended up being by far my favorite course I took. Prof. Tsoulouhas is very kind and displays a good knowledge of subject matters present in the course. She is not difficult to reach outside of class and you can tell student success is a priority. I would take class again with her.

An interesting course. I learned a lot while investing a reasonable amount of time. Discussions were also worthwhile. Quick aside: Students at a school as prestigious as this one shouldn't lash out because the professor prohibits plagiarism, or because they assign college-level amounts of reading. It makes us all look bad and devalues our degrees.
Professor Tsoulouhas is very organized with her Canvas being extremely accessible and all of her rubrics/deadlines being very clear. This class has a lot of group work and class discussions.
Be prepared to read.. Make sure you cite every quote. Not a fun class

analysis.name: Valentina Arismendi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

Val is a great teacher, and I found her lectures to be informative. She is very available and graduated not long ago from UNC, which makes her more relatable and fun than other professors. I enjoyed the guest speakers she brought to class, and she is more than qualified to teach this class. I would highly recommend taking any class with Val.

Said it was her first semester teaching and it kinf of showed. Good class overall and really learned a lot but it was a bit disorganized at times. Gave a lot of time in class to work on projects. It was online so not my most memorable but Val made UX easy and seems like shed have good connections if you want to go into that field.

analysis.name: Arne Kalleberg
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Kalleberg is the goat. He is a caring guy and is very knowledgeable in sociology. He is an expert in the field and very well respected around campus and nationwide. If you can take a class with him, jump on it. Do what is asked, which is not much, and you will make an A. 5/5 class.

Dr. Kalleberg is the goat. He is an expert in his field, very laid back, and a very caring guy. Absolutely take his class if you can. Do what he asks, which is not overwhelming, and you will succeed. 5/5 class and 5/5 prof.

Class was interesting and engaging, and super easy. If you're not doing well you're not trying. He mostly stands out for how he is as a person! He really cares about his students and makes an effort to know everyone. He's not the most tech savvy, so we spent a lot of classes with him on the phone with its, but we laughed it off! HIGHLY recommend

I LOVE ARNE. Would regularly drag myself out of bed only to see him. Love his cutie NY accent, made me feel like I was back home. Content was easy. Lectures were not super heavy. He's just a sweetheart and I love him.

Was a decent lecturer. Course content was pretty simple and easy to understand. Multiple short readings, but not too much to handle. Laughed when a student asked about extra credit... but overall was alright.

analysis.name: Ellen Atterbury
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Ellen is an amazing professor who makes it easy for students to succeed. She makes expectations clear with rubrics and grading criteria, and is a very fair grader. She leaves great feedback and resources for students to learn and improve. The exams were pretty easy and projects and in-class activities were fun and engaging. Overall great class!

Not sure how anyone could rate Professor Atterbury low, she is great! The class is pretty standardized for projects/tests but Atterbury prepares you well and encourages in-class group discussion which is super helpful if you actually want to learn the language. Midterms and final were easy if you just study a couple days before.

(Spanish 204) This class is pretty standardized for quizzes/tests and assignments but Professor Atterbury was super understanding all semester long and gave helpful feedback on assignments without being overly harsh. Make sure to talk in class and do your readings and you'll be fine!

I didn't like her as much as other reviews. What made me mad is nothing was assigned in Canvas with specific dates so it was easy to forget due dates. Attendance is mandatory and you have to participate everyday.
She was really amazing, we always know the expectations. She makes the class fun and educational!!

analysis.name: Atiya Husain
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Atiya knows how to be engaging with her students and gives many examples to ensure that you understand a topic. She made complicated theories seem like elementary school with ease. She is always calm, cool, and confident. Highly recommend

Great Professor overall, took her in the 2024 winter term, and her lectures were truly engaging. There's something admirable about her, from the way she speaks so eloquently, to how she engages with the class by eliciting introspection into our consciousness. Atiya is a great teacher and her lectures are very interesting. She does a great job of relaying the material in a clear way. There are 3 take home tests, each worth 20%, and an in-class final also worth 20%. She gives pop quizzes on the reading almost every class, but they trickled out at the end. The readings are all online, no textbook required!

analysis.name: David Attewell
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: He's the sweetest guy, always asking for feedback on where he can improve as a professor. Lectures are interesting and the grading system is extremely fair, consisting of a presentation, two 5-page papers, a final, participation and 3 pop quizzes. Very open to giving feedback during office hours and encourages class discussions on relevant matters.

David Attewell was my favorite professor during my first semester at UNC! His lectures were engaging, he values class participation, and he truly makes an effort to get to know his students. You have a few assignments throughout the semester but his grading criteria is clear. He is absolutely brilliant and I could not recommend him more strongly!

David is one of my favorite professors at UNC. He's young which makes his lectures more interesting because he thinks about current events and relates to his students. He's a lenient grader and SUPER caring about his students and the quality of his teaching. Just make sure you are participating in class and doing the readings. 10/10 recommend.

I absolutely love David! He is so knowledgable, approachable, and caring . He explains concept well, but lectures can be dry. Fair grader on papers and no midterms! There are 3 pop quizzes (easy) but just on the readings so if you read you'll do good. I would do everything I could to take Attewell's class.

Professor Attewell is very knowledgable in his field and lectures with confidence. His lectures and powerpoint slides make politics easy to learn and he has made learning super accessible to non-political students. Highly recommend, be sure to take notes of his slides and read the case studies.

analysis.name: Ava Geenen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: PHIL 140: Very nice prof. but class can get dull. Worksheets give good overview of papers but the subject matter is really confusing, especially for your first philosophy class. Half of class stopped attending. Papers are hard but if you go to office hours and the writing center you can totally do well. If you love philosophy, you will 100% enjoy.

Ava is a great professor. She understands the material extremely well and, more importantly, can explain it well. Her readings were thoughtfully chosen and refreshingly contemporary compared to many introductory-level philosophy courses at UNC. Additionally, her unit quizzes required meaningful engagement with the texts, which helped learning.

PHIL140 was an awful experience. The class material felt like a giant circle leading back to the same discussion and topic we had on the first day of class. Paper grading was harsh for the class, and the lectures were very discussion-based, yet dull. Half the class stopped showing up throughout the semester, if that says anything.

This course was fairly difficult for an introductory class and contained a lot of reading and lectures. Professor Geenen was always willing to help outside of class and had some interesting lectures. The material was pretty comprehensive as well.

Took this class for a gen-ed and was disappointed. She takes lateness into account and if you arrive a minute past class start time, poof! your participation goes down. She grades harshly- even after meeting with her several times about a paper she gave me a B+ on it and her critiques are absolute nonsense. Will not give you the grade you deserve.

analysis.name: Benjamin Arbuckle
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload

review_highlights.comment: Sitting in on Arbuckle's lectures is like story time for the class.  His enthusiasm and excitement for teaching the material rubs off on you, and this is being written by a science major & minor student.  Exams are easy to study for as long as you put in effort the night before or so & listen to the lectures generally.  GREAT class for gened reqs!

Best class ever! There were no midterms or finals. One 5 page paper in the middle of the semester, but not difficult if you don't leave it to the last minute. Professor Arbuckle is understanding and kind. While his lectures were not required, they were very interesting and worth your time to attend. Would 100% take a class with Arbuckle again.

Minimal feedback given throughout the class, didn't grade any assignment until the day before grades were due. Very unclear final essay rubric and if you don't write in the exact style he is looking for, you will not do well. But you wouldn't know what that style is, because he doesn't grade anything or give feedback throughout the class.

kind, very interesting, understanding prof. easy A. 1 paper due in the middle of the year making it possible to actually be interested in the content. you get downgraded if you use AI but are given the (optional) chance to revise the paper at the end of the sem. this was good incentive to be more ambitious with the work resulting in an A.

Amazing class!! Professor Arbuckle is so nice and caring. He is accessible at all times of the day and often answers emails very quickly. He answers any and all questions. Professor Arbuckle's lectures are very interesting and sometimes showed images about his archaeology experience which was incredible to see first hand.

analysis.name: Sage Aviles

Lectures weren't engaging and lecture materials came directly from the textbook. She would basically just repeat everything we've already read with a few in-class activities here and there, which was overall not very helpful. Don't take this class if you can help it.

analysis.name: Avi-Dan Santo

Very easy but very boring. Slides were just many bullet points on a blank screen although he tries his best to make it more interesting. Participation is the majority of your grade, and you have no actual exams just papers.

Good professor but super wordy and long winded. He was nice and clearly spoken, but kinda weirded me out sometimes. He had guest lectures all the time. Not a hard class at all, but be prepared to listen to boring lectures.

analysis.name: Ava Stone
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

Ava is extremely nice, and caries her warm demeanor throughout her lessons and lectures. She urges students to participate in class, which facilitates great camaraderie between classmates, and is always understanding to any issues that may arise and responds well to motivated students who demonstrate effort in her class.

Ava is really nice. Her class can be difficult but she recognizes effort and is really nice when you're struggling. The IPAs are really clear and easy to do well on but the tests are a little more difficult. Overall, she's a good teacher and I would def take 102 by her if she taught it.

analysis.name: Avery Wilson

As long as you pay attention in class and put in the work outside of class, I couldn't see how anyone would leave this professor a less than stellar review!

analysis.name: Laurence Avery

Willing to help you understand the material but pushes you to be your be best.   A+++

Nice guy. Clear, knowledgable, definately old school.

analysis.name: Lorna Avilés
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Aviles is hands down the best professor I have had at UNC so far. Participation matters to stay engaged, but class would fly by, as she's a great teacher and not a boring lecturer. TAKE HER CLASS!!!

Professor Aviles is amazing. Her lectures are interesting and engaging and she doesn't take herself too seriously. Her course load is made to challenge you and help you succeed (if you put in the work). She returns graded work so so fast. Seriously, she is the kind of professor that makes you happy you paid for college. Take her class.

Don't let other reviews fool you, this is NOT an easy A class. There are a handful of grammar quizzes throughout the semester that can tank your grade, the in-class essays that can be graded somewhat tough in terms of grammar, and the examsare fairly graded, but you have to study and be familar with the content.

I took prof Avilés for span 344 and loved it! You will spend a lot of class time discussing readings, the lesson, etc with peers and I feel it really improved my speaking skills in a chill environment. The papers aren't hard and you can often take them in your own direction to keep it fresh. There is a group presentation but it isn't hard. Take it!

One of the best professors I have had. She grades SO quickly (got my final exam grade back 6 minutes after the grading period had ended). She gives great feedback and does a good job of keeping everyone on track. There is a good amount of weekly homework, but its worth it and is helpful in understanding the class material. Really awesome Prof.

analysis.name: Karen Auerbach

She is kind and was gracious to me when I was struggling, giving me extensions and hearing me out. She appreciates participation and will notice if you are active. The lectures are a hectic and hard to follow, but you can still do well if you can't pay that close attention to the material. Final was not hard; what was on it was what was expected.

Everything said about this professor is true. While she is very kind and knowledgable about this topic, she is equally unorganized and her lectures are very hectic. Her quizzes are specific and detailed, make sure you truly understand the readings with dates/minor details before taking them. im halfway through the sem & only have one grade put in

analysis.name: Aubrey Hart

Mr. Hart is a phenomenal person and teacher! I had him for both ITAL-101 and ITAL-102, and overall, the Italian department at UNC is AMAZING! Aubrey is a great teacher and is super encouraging and understanding. For sure, I would recommend taking any ITAL courses with him.
I had Aubrey for 102 and he was great! he cares a lot about his students and makes sure you know it's ok to make mistakes and not be perfect. I would gladly take a class with Aubrey again!

analysis.name: Audra Wormald

I actually really enjoyed the course content and thought she was nice but kinda judgemental and it is really reading heavy, cases were fine and easy to do well on the quizes. Group projects were annoying and some of the grading doesn't make sense, same with soem of the assignments. SO make sure you look at all the files and canva pages.
Professor Wormald cares about her students. She and I had a great conversation after class that she mentioned to me later through the course. She encourages responsible use of AI.

Audura is terrible. The class is miserable but she is the only professor that teaches this mandatory class. It might be impossible to get an A in this class. She dropped everyone's participation so much. I talked in every class, didn't miss one, and still got screwed. The group project grades were so harsh. Worst prof I've had in Kenan Flagler.

analysis.name: Audrey Sachleben

I would 100% take a course taught by Audrey again.

Audrey was a great instructor for this class. It was extremely straightforward and she did her best to make sure both her lectures and simulations were engaging. analysis.name: Aubrey Lewis

review_highlights.comment: This is a hard class, but Professor Lewis grades fairly. She's very sweet and doesn't cold call.

tbh I think the problem with fren105 is the class itself, not the professor, but the model just felt a lot like she wasn't doing much teaching, and we had to just figure everything out on our own outside of class bc that's how fren105 is set up. the online textbook is not very helpful, either. duolingo was my best friend. she's very nice, though.

Aubrey is first and foremost a sweetheart. She does her best to make class engaging, but overall this course sucks. It's not her fault though, she's a TA who is stuck doing what UNC has decided Fren105 should do. The textbook sucks too. It's not unreasonable in terms of what you're expected to know, so while you have to self-teach, it's not awful

The problem is really mainly just the structure of FREN105, Aubrey is really nice but the structure of the class means there isn't much opportunity for her to teach, its very self-taught and the textbook was kind of weird. There are a lot of different grades though so it's not only based on tests/quizzes.

Aubrey was great! She really made an effort to teach us to speak the language, but didn't make us feel bad when we messed up. Was very accessible for office hours, and prepared us well for the tests. Would definitely take again!

analysis.name: Aurora Yu

review_highlights.comment: Professor Yu is incredible! She's passionate about what she teaches and Existentialism is one of my favorite classes I've taken in my time at UNC. Highly recommend!

Aurora is great. Several of my peers aren't pumped on the course content, but they all admit they have reading/discussing philosophy, so take that with a grain of salt. Put effort into the readings. analysis.name: Aubrey Leary

As far as math goes, Professor Leary tried her best to make the material understandable and clear. She was great at giving time for questions and answers, as well as for students to learn and practice on their own time during lectures.
This was the most poorly run class of my life. Terrible, just terrible.

analysis.name: Aubrey Snowden

Class was alright, some of the plays we had to see in person were somewhat interesting but overall not too fun of a class. You could tell Snowden felt that her students didn't seem to care too much about her class and she combatted this with 8 mandatory attendance checks which were annoying.

analysis.name: Cemil Aydin
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: One of the easiest classes that you can take at UNC. Cemil himself isn't very involved in the grading; the grades you receive are completely down to the TA (mine was pretty nice). You seriously don't need to show up for class though and there isn't much homework.

Weekly writing assignments that are around 400 words, but the readings with it are very long and dense. Decent lecturer but goes on a few tangents. Gives out points for discussion and attendance, so show up or communicate (he was pretty flexible if you told him why you were out). Midterm was an essay, final was a take home exam and in person essay

Had a really good time in this class. Prof was very kind funny and entertaining, he is very knowledgable and is always going into interesting tangents he picked up from his years of research that tie into the class. Not a harsh grader at all and is very understanding. I took him for History 538 The Middle East and the West learned a lot Recommend!

There is weekly assignments averaging around 400 words and lengthy readings with them. The TA grades most of your work and at times can be very particular on what his is looking for. Unless you want to learn about the Ottoman empire, I would not take this class.

Dr. Aydin was absolutely amazing, and this was my favorite class this semester. He is incredibly knowledgeable and offers an important and different perspective on many historical events. This course ties in with many current-day events, wars, and disputes. Note: there is a lot of reading, but 50% of your grade is recitation, highly recommend it!

analysis.name: Jeffrey Ayers
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: fantastic teacher/lecturer, has review sessions and tons of practice posted before the midterms/final. super helpful during office hours. discrete is a hard class, the first midterm is often misleading and the course piles up by the end. only concern id say is that you don't know grading scale until end of semester.

Considering this is an advanced math class, Jeff made the class as painless as possible. Even though we meet only twice a week, Jeff does his best to teach all the material in lectures to avoid outside reading (you will most likely be reading anyway). It's bittersweet that he is graduating this December, as he will no longer be teaching.
Discrete is a tough class regardless but Jeff made it manageable. He was accessible outside of class and was as helpful as possible.

He's a grad student, so there's not much I can really say other than he's just okay at teaching. First half of the class is MATH 110 review, but the second half is rough, and I don't think he was prepared. I'd take him again, but only if I had to.

Ayers was amazing! He curved the tests that the majority of the class did bad on (20 points usually). He provided us with exam reviews before every exam which were extremely helpful. He is an amazing prof that wants us to succeed. However, the final was HARD. I had a B+ going into the final and ended up with a B- in the class even after the curve.

analysis.name: Cemil Aydin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof Aydin is a GREAT professor. He is so passionate about what he teaches and is very caring. Class is pretty lecture heavy and there is a lot of reading, but material is super interesting and he is a very fair grader with reasonable expectations. I highly recommend.

Professor Aydin was the most understanding professor out of both semesters of online classes. He's very passionate about his work which focuses around decolonization and every class was fun to attend. 10/10 would recommend taking a class with him!
Cemil is a good lecturer and he cares about his students, I took a class I had little to no background in and he made it incredibly interesting. Would highly recommend taking if you are into history.

analysis.name: Lindsay Ayling
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof Ayling has been one of my favorite professors at UNC so far. Very knowledgable about the subject area and makes the topic interesting for students. SO SO caring and accessible outside of class-- she really wants students to succeed. Would absolutely take another class with her.
Very knowledgeable about the subject matter, very kind and understanding, and overall great prof. Readings are pretty dense though.
She's a wonderful teacher and would absolutely take a class from her again.

analysis.name: Ayana Younge
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Younge is super nice, upbeat, and willing to help. The class material for Busi405 is commonly seen as common sense, but she finds a way to make it interesting through class activities and games. The tests are a little long and will push you to work a little more quickly than normal, but the classes tend to performs well. Homework is minimal.

Shes awesome. Show up to class and youll do very well in the class. She genuinely cares how youre doing and was willing to move assignments around based around how we were doing. Tests will push you for time, but getting 90% on them padded with all the homeworks will give you a pretty easy A
Super nice professor. Always had interesting exercises and brought lots of energy to class. The tests were insanely long and difficult for no reason.

analysis.name: Azza Ben Youssef
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Azza is such a light spirit who makes learning french enjoyable. She has a sense of humor which is refreshing in a classroom environment and she grades very fairly if anything she tries to give you as much credit as she can within reason. The course covers a lot of material, but she makes sure to go over specifically what we will be tested on.

She is such a kind, supportive, and funny instructor. She treats each student with respect despite different levels. She also explains cultural and relevant background info. She is just funny and seems to really enjoy teaching. Make sure you do the pre work. She is a fair grader. Participation matters and will help you succeed.

ABY was one of the nicest professors I've had. She speaks very fast but she has a true passion for teaching french and ensuring that we understand everything. I would definitely take another class with her.

Professor Youssef is by far the better of the two french professors I have had at UNC. She is much easier in grading and is sassy which I think is super funny. She is also super accommodating with grading (I forgot to submit half of a HW assignment and she gave me full credit for it). Overall, her class was the best french class I have taken.

Azza is the best professor I have ever had. She encourages everyone to speak in French each class and I can testify that this has improved my French so much. She is very graceful correcting us when we make mistakes so we learn but are not afraid to mess up. She wants everyone to learn and succeed and knows how to help us do so!

analysis.name: Amanda Aziz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Amanda was a good professor. Her lectures were very informative and she cared a lot about students' well-being. However, her criteria weren't always clear when it came to grading papers. I often got feedback that I didn't follow the prompt when I would address everything in the prompt. The class was easy, but don't expect to ace the papers.

Amanda said at the beginning of the semester that she wanted this to be a class that you could put on a temporary back burner in times of stress or difficulty. She values her students' physical and mental wellbeing above all else, which is clear in her easily approachable demeanor and ability to accommodate each student in their unique situation.

Amanda is one of the best instructors I have met at UNC. She tried to make everything easier and more convenient to her students. She could explain some confusing concepts very well. She is always very patient and very responsive to emails. The short answer format of the midterm and final is not easy, but overall I enjoyed taking the course.

I loved POLI 215 with Prof Aziz! She is always available via emails or at her online office hours. Although the course was async and there were lectures 3x a week, she kept them pretty short (25-30min) and always asked us for ways to make class better. She was very accommodating and she's a great person! 10/10 would recommend

Amazing professor and person! She cares about her students mental, physical health and wellbeing. I learned so much about myself and about how groups function within society in her class. I would highly recommend her.

analysis.name: Brandon Bayne
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The class itself wasn't that much work: 10 discussion posts and replies, 2 quizzes, 1 midterm paper and a final project. But Bayne had no rubrics, barely any guidelines for assignments, and grading was random and subjective. He also didn't grade the majority of our assignments until the last week of class which was stressful and frustrating.

This was my favorite course so far at Carolina. It made me reflect on my own faith and consider ways we could be doing better. Professor Bayne is super knowledgeable about both Christianity and Native history. Sometimes it was tough to confront so many difficult moments, but he always gave us helpful context and led creative group discussions.

this class was a gen ed for me but i loved this class. prof and TA are awesome and i learned a lot. not a lot of hw for the class, probably an 1-2 each week but readings are required and they do notebook checks. exams were easy and theres xtra assignments to pad out ur grade. overall a super nice guy who wants to see students succeed!

I LOVED this class and the teacher. He is a great lecturer and I was never bored in his class. He is very clear on his assignments and exams. If you put in the work, this is a very easy class to get an A in. he gives and adequate amount of work. There is a lot of readings but they are enjoyable. He also made us food for the exam.

Dr. Bayne and Carla were amazing this semester. The classroom environment is very engaging and interesting, and both are very caring. As long as you pay attention and study the exam guides, an A is nearly guaranteed. The best professor and TA duo I have had at UNC so far.

analysis.name: Erin Baker
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Extremely exam-heavy(85%)and unforgiving grading. Changed the grading scale weeks into the course. Penalized the entire class for "AI use" with no evidence. Rarely responds to emails. If you want a fair, transparent, or supportive instructor, avoid this class. Change your schedule around if you must, do not settle for Dr. Baker, you deserve better.

Dr. Baker writes all her notes on a blackboard and doesn't post notes that you can go back to. Half the time she has to look at her paper to see the work she did before continuing on the board. The way she does problems is more complicated than it has to be. She is so strict about sig figs but messes them up on answer keys and lacks consistency.

Dr. Baker made CHEM 241 a terrible experience. She is incredibly immature and lacks professionalism. While some students used AI on an assignment, instead of punishing those who did, she punished the whole class. She did the same thing on participation grades. She is condescending and acts like she got her feelings hurt and needed to retaliate.

Nice lady, terrible prof. Do you want to succeed at UNC Chem 241 - don't take Baker. That's a fact.  Why would a professor have to curve and give extra credit for each exam?? Because most students did bad!!! It's a sad story; people fought to get into this class, just to be played in the end. This is the Carolina STEM experience.

I 100% agree with her response to students using AI to cheat but I want to focus on something else: her class is incredibly disorganized, but everything from the test comes from lectures that make little sense. Slides/textbook don't correspond with her lesson. She is generous with curves but it does not make up for her inability to convey content.

analysis.name: Tonya Balan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Balan was awesome. There are 2 quizzes and a final group video project. A couple things do get a little technical with some code and using the correct formulas, but if you study, you will be fine. Attendance is optional but she brought several guest speakers who were interesting to hear, so I'd suggest going. Very good experience.

Super chill and knowledgable professor. Final project was fun and just enough of a challenge. Gemini makes all labs and homework a cakewalk. Quizzes are clearly laid out beforehand with ample review material. Incredibly easy class and material is taught if you actually want to learn it. Take if you need a stats credit but don't want to learn stats.

Dr. Balan is good at making things make sense, especially if you have no expereince in computer/data science. Her class is very easy but it is just her lecturing, labs on friday are when you  get to actually interact with class material and the people in your class. Final is a group project, but watch out for quiz 2 it is harder than quiz 1.

Dr. Balan is very kind and a great professor. She makes all assignments very easy and clear. Had some guest lectures in the course which was very interesting too! As I already took other data/comp courses, it was a bit boring at times, but otherwise good content! I would definitely love to take more courses with her in the future! 5/5!
Prof. Balan is very nice and sweet, definitely take her course!!!

analysis.name: Bella Randle
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: i absolutely adored poli130 with her! she's a very good teacher and her lectures are very engaging and she definitely knows what she's talking about. not an easy a and there's reading due for every class with quizzes but the reading helps and if you do it you won't struggle.

Bella is an amazing professor! Poli-130 was by far my favorite class this semester. She made the class engaging, but there are readings due every class, with weekly quizzes. Some of the readings are pretty long and our final project was fairly difficult. Not an easy A, but Bella makes up for it with her awesome lectures and love for the class!

Definitely have to put in effort to get good results. Good lecturer and engaging. Does a great job of keeping up with the syllabus and all readings are available on Canvas so nothing to buy. Lots of quizzes but always straightforward w/ no trick questions. Kind and approachable. Loved Bella!
Very sweet and fair grader. The subject is interesting and she leaves space in the syllabus to discuss whatever the class wants to.

She was my TA for Professor Anderson's POLI 130 course. She was helpful going over information and condensing the material to help students better understand the readings. There were 2 absences available for the recitation. Overall great TA/Professor and person. She is really understanding and nice!

analysis.name: Todd Austell
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 347 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Todd is the type that believes you don't have other work outside of his class. Of course you need to invest time into chem classes to do well (everyone knows that), but the time he expects you to put in isn't reasonable for anyone that is taking more than 12 hours. Love yourself and take someone else. P.s. he writes his own reviews, so watch out...

The tests are extremely difficult, and the reviews for them aren't given with a key. He asks students to "compare answers" on a forum instead of giving a key to the exams.. He's a caring professor, but his class had to have been the most difficult class I've ever taken at UNC. The final was 1/3 multiple choice with a whole section of short answer.

Todd does care about studentS; however, he doesn't care about YOU- a student. He likes to be liked by all, but is short and narcissistic when it's one-on-one. He also expects WAY MORE than a student can do in a semester and still be successful in other classes, but he doesn't care. Many useless book problems. Final was my highest grade. LOW avgs.
Well definitely a cool guy, he certainly doesn't care about the success of his students. Would not recommend taking his class.

Makes Orgo much harder than it needs to be. Controlling with note taking format, syllabus contains no scheduled list of daily activities, assignments on Mastering Chemistry are put up irregularly, making them harder to get done by the deadlines. Sometimes writes his own positive reviews on here, so beware. Not as good as he makes himself out to be.

analysis.name: Teressa Bergland
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 99 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: As others have said, her exams are quite long.  However, she has recognized that the exams weren't completely fair and offered revisions worth half credit back.  Her lectures are pretty good and she's very accessible via office hours.  Homework is pretty light.  She's not perfect but def way better than some  of the other stor profs here.

Rated her 2 (not 1) bc she does genuinely have a passion and it shows in her good lectures. HOWEVER, she is not meant to be a professor. Harsh/rigid grading and closed-note tests aren't sensible for a coding class, and tests (that she made) not graded for 1-2 months. She tries to do too much then penalizes the students when she finds out she can't.

SHE IS A GOOD TEACHER. People need to chill on her because she is genuinely good at her job, but she teaches a hard class so people are bound to get bad grades. She does her best, and while it takes her a long time to grade, she is very generous with extra credit. You are going to struggle in this class if you dont like STATS, but she does her best

I do not understand other reviews. Is she the best professor? No, but she's a fine one. It's clear that she's adjusting to teaching here, but, her exams were quite fair. You'll struggle if you don't show up to class/study, but you'll do fine if you pay attention. Not an easy A, but you'll get a good grade if you show up and put in a little effort.

You need the textbook to survive this class bc she will just read off slides in the most boring manner. She is nice, but that is different from good. She is poorly organized and is constantly going "woe is me!" bc of how poorly she plans and manages her time. Haven't gotten multiple assignments graded (from months ago) and the final is in two days.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Brunk
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took the honors section of chem430 and loved it. We did a capstone project and got to present our work at the Undergraduate Research Symposium. I was able to learn new how to work with data and even apply some of what I did to my own research! It was hard at first but I learned a lot about myself and team science. This was my fav class at UNC.

Dr. Brunk is kind and clearly cares about her students. She is very busy, as most research faculty are but she answers questions when you bring them to lecture. The flipped classroom can be an adjustment, but it reflects med school style learning. Biochem is challenging (DUH). Homework load is heavy-it helps and can be a grade saver for exams

This class was really hard but really good. It changed my view of medicine and it changed what I want to do with my life. I love the real world applications and learning how to work with data. I loved the lectures on precision medicine and things that are really happening in science.

Took Brunk because Hogan's section was full - worst mistake ever. My friends in Hogan's section had a walk in the park compared to what Brunk put our class through. Prone to mistakes in videos/lecture, very confusing explanations when asked for clarification (which I had to ask at office hours bc she never responded to my emails!), tricky exams.

She is rarely available and actively makes it harder for you to find help. She doesn't let you email her so you can only get help from the TAs. I had to have my final exam rescheduled and she refused to help me out. Keep in mind it was an EXTREMELY easy fix. Don't expect any notes or videos to be posted, and her modules don't match with the exams.

analysis.name: Becky Butler
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class was mainly focused on Dr. Butler going through slideshows and discussing readings in groups. It's not the most organized, but as long as you somewhat pay attention, the class wasn't hard. If you commit some time to the readings or oral histories, getting an A is very doable. That said, you could get away with skimming the readings.

If you're looking for an easy or filler class, do not take this course. It is graded on around six different components, making it more demanding than expected. Dr. Butler is a good person, but the lectures and assignment details were very unorganized. The exams were also poorly structured and much longer than they should have been.
Do not take this course if you're just looking for an easy filler. Dr. Butler is very kind, but the lectures are often unorganized and the exams are much longer than they need to be.

There are a decent amount of readings. There is a group interview, and a final paper along with a 10min presentation. There are only 2-3 homework assignments, and there were about 3-4 tests, all being online, including the final. The class was decently heavy on participation but it was always fun and usually was discussing the reading with someone.
Really great professor. Very accessible. LOTS of work. You will discuss the readings in class, so you have to actually do them. Learned a lot though.

analysis.name: Prakash Belkale
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: His English is so good that Even i could understand what he means with listening score of 15 in TOEFL. Come and take his class quickly!

Prof Belkale is really nice. I didn't attend his class often but he replied emails fast and was helpful during office hours. Also he graded by percentage, like top 10% for A and another 10% for A-. He always said this class is challenging but I didn't feel so. The class is about basic logic and number theory, very fundamental for math majors.

I highly recommend Dr. Belkale! He is a passionate professor who loves math and appreciates hard work and dedication. Plan to read the textbook and attend lectures. I always felt welcomed in his OH and I encourage attending! His lectures follow the textbook precisely, and exam reviews give test hints! His class reminded me why I love math!

He lectured for 75 minutes straight on the chalkboard so you had to interrupt him out loud if you had a question, but he explained clearly. If you like super neat notes, he is not the guy for you. But if you can follow along with "arrow logic" you'll be fine. Midterms are EXACTLY like the practice ones he gives, but the final was departmental
I liked this class a lot.  I thought it was pretty easy and the homework was actually based on what he did in class, which I thought he explained well.

analysis.name: Joshua Beaver
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 302 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Allows you to drop your lowest test grade but if your overall test average is still a 50 or below, you're screwed.

An easy class is not representative of easy material, the same way a hard class is not representative of difficult material. It's clear from these reviews that despite challenging material, everyone is putting in real effort to work through it. The frustration comes from how that material is poorly translated to tests and quizzes. :(

Like poetry, this class continues to degrade any hope of redemption to the very end. I've never had a final at UNC that has felt designed to take the ENTIRE 3 hours, in a similar way to the past quizzes, just longer. A passing grade would be a blessing. They say they want us to succeed, but kick us while we're down.

So far, Dr. Beaver has been a decent professor. CHEM 101 is not an easy class but he's very energetic and wants everyone to succeed. He usually explains everything clearly and also gives you time to process and understand the chemistry problems that are done in class. As long as you continue to study consistently and do the HW you should be fine.

Verily, this course is no mere pursuit, but an odyssey of torment where only the steadfast glimpse enlightenment. The lecturer bestows knowledge in fire and fury, yet we, mere mortals, are left scorched, grasping at fleeting truths. My soul writhes beneath this incantation of madness! And yet, is not true wisdom born from suffering?

analysis.name: Ruth Von Bernuth
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Ruth von Bernuth is the best prof I've had here yet. She's so knowledgeable and passionate. I came in struggling with grammar and I've seen a big improvement in my writing now. She was a little slow with grading but the assignments were fair and doable. She's caring and wants to get to know each of her students. Her office hours are helpful!

She is so sweet and SO passionate about what she teaches. I had her for Fairytale class and it was so sweet watching her speak and lecture about the content. Attendance IS mandatory (I made the mistake of not going to like 4 class periods thinking attendance didn't matter) but honestly the class is so interesting that I never dread going.

Probably the sweetest and most caring professor I have had at UNC! Definitely cares about her students and loves her job! Her feedback and grading criteria aren't always the most clear at times but she is very willing to meet with you outside of class and office hours!

This class is interesting and fun. I didn't expect to like it when I first signed up, but I did. The professor is great, but she's not good at keeping up with grading. Only two group projects and two essays throughout this course, but this class is reading-heavy.

This is a pretty difficult class if you are still not confident in your German. She talks very fast and expects you to already have a good understanding of difficult concepts. Other than that, she is very sweet and accommodating.

analysis.name: Shankar Bhamidi
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Definitely in the top 2 STEM professors I've had at UNC. STOR 435 is very hard material but he is hilarious and great at explaining the material, and there are many office hours every week.

Highly recommend taking him for 435! Very fair exams and grading, and he allowed us to use a cheat sheet on the final. The hws take a while, but the exams were all variations of hw or practice exam problems. He's also very accessible outside of class and explains difficult concepts in 435 well. Definitely would have done much worse if not for him.

Professor Bhamidi is an excellent professor and cares deeply about the success of his students. On multiple occasions I was able to meet with him outside of his scheduled office hours because I had class during his office hours. He curved the grades at end of semester. Also a funny lecturing that makes a hard class more enjoyable.

The best professor I have had at UNC so far. He is inspiring, intelligent (and great at explaining), clear with what he expects on homework and exams, and is readily available to respond to questions. Also has a good sense of humor.

Shankar is incredible! STOR 435 is a very hard class, but he explains things so well and makes the course as straightforward and clear as possible, and the exams are very fair. Lots of homework, but they are very helpful. He is also hilarious.

analysis.name: Reema Bhattacharya
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof accused me of plagiarizing the final despite having no evidence and threatened to fail me if I didn't respond in a day (during finals). Obviously I didn't cheat and was able to prove it. Make sure to keep a record of all of your work. If you are looking to spend hours on assignments just to be accused of cheating, then this class is for you.

The class structure and course site were convoluted. The course is simply a laundry list of links to articles and videos with little "teaching". For this professor's section of the course, there were eight assignments, a midterm, and a final. None of which helped me learn substantially. Recommend avoiding.

INLS 490 is one of the most valuable classes that makes me feel more prepared for the job market.  Despite the fact that I am not a technical person, Professor Bhattacharya went out of her way to encourage me. You truly get what you put into it. The final project was creating a training; although we had to self-learn the software, it was worth it!

INLS 490 - Reema was accessible outside of class, however, I feel like she did not care for us at all. Her instructions were so confusing and she would contradict things she said. She would also change up her idea of projects after I had already submitted them. She is just all over the place. Overall, I can't say I learned much but it was easy

taking inls 490, the learning design class. she gives off this superiority attitude where she feels like she's better than everyone else. her feedback are short and not helpful. she doesn't seem to care about her students. her modules are full of spelling errors, which show how little effort she put in and she don't care. 

avoid this class

analysis.name: Kanika Bhalla
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I love Prof. Bhalla for reason that she focuses on learning real stuff than just grades. How can one not be fascinated to attend a class where a professor shows stand up comedies to facilitate language learning! She's super cool, I could approach her like a friend, she talks to students in their language by giving reference to Instagram memes, etc.

Kanikaji is an alright professor but there have been many times where she does not show grace to her students. She is not extremely forgiving and the way that she grades is rather harmful -- in the sense that she takes points off like nobody's business. She is fair in class but expects a lot of participation -- talking once a class is not enough.

One of the best professors I have taken classes with so far. She is really understanding and tries to make students comfortable with the teaching materials. I would love to take class with her again and have enrolled with her course in the next semester. I am super excited!
Wish she could stay at UNC longer! Loved her classes. Always used to look forward to see her in class!

analysis.name: Susan Bickford
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The grading scale is difficult, but it's not impossible to get an A. There are 8 quizzes; two are dropped. You essentially need near-perfect scores on the remaining six, but she tells you what the questions will be in advance. The best advice for this class is to go to office hours for your papers to talk about them well in advance of the deadline.

She reduces grades when your interpretation is different than hers, even if you provide textual evidence. The class itself is insightful, though I don't think it reaches a philosophical level. The class material is philosophical but how we approach them is not. Grading is too tough and reading&writing is too much for a 200-level class.

Approaches philosophical materials in a strange way, mixing high school-level Engl, Philosophy, Polisci, and Classics but lacks depth in any. Extremely tough grader, focusing on trivial details. Avoid 270 if you dislike being disciplined - only by rewriting papers to her exact suggestions will you earn a decent grade. Tokens make little sense.

She's awesome, the only thing that sucks is her grading scale. It's almost impossible to get an A. She is so caring, engaging, etc. I thought I was going to hate everything about this class and I didn't, I actually kind of loved it. Seriously my ONLY issue is the grading scale, you have to get a perfect grade on almost everything to get an A.

Professor Bickford is kind and knowledgable but her class is TOUGH. She's a very harsh grader and expects expert knowledge from her students. The amount of work that you have to do is not comparable to the grade you will get - it is next to impossible to get an A. If your GPA is important to you, take another political philosophy class for credit.

analysis.name: Jackson  Bittick
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Jackson is an AMAZING professor. He explains concepts clearly and obviously wants his students to learn and succeed. Very accessible and helpful office hours. Mandatory in-person group discussion posts every class, but basically graded for correctness. 4x papers that were super fun to write. Very lenient grader, just not many points to lose.

Down to earth and offers extensions. Reading before class, and then the next 2 classes, you spend time discussing and analyzing the argument presented. In each class, you turn in answers for participation credit. There are 4 papers and a final exam. In each paper, you argue against one philosopher in the unit. He gives amazing, detailed feedback!

Jackson picked some really interesting papers for us to discuss this year! I learned a great deal about ongoing issues surrounding AI, as well as more general Philosophy topics! He was pretty strict on the papers, but it was worth it in the end with an easy final exam. Jackson is a fun, young professor and I enjoyed taking his class!

analysis.name: Brian Billman
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 119 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Professor Billman makes a rather boring subject, interesting.... going into the class I was expecting it to be a rather dry, difficult topic, but his lecture style keeps you engaged. The lectures are VERY important however, as they comprise most of the exams... definitely recommend!

I like his personality, but he tends to go off on a rant during lecture. I also find it hard to pinpoint exactly what I should be focusing on while I study. Going to class is a must. He uploads his ppts, but they don't go into much detail and are mostly pictures.

The lectures were very dry and included him talking for 75 min with pictures on the slides. Paying attention the whole time was almost impossible. The exams were very difficult, multiple choice with an essay question. The two recitation essays were not bad, they are what probably saved my grade. I would not recommend taking this class for a gen ed.

Took this class as my friends as an 'easy A'. Easy A's do not exist here, you're gonna have to put work in to get the grade you want. You gotta go to class, pay attention, and study. If you do that, you'll get a good grade, but don't think it's gonna be a joke of a class you can take as a filler. Class is fun and interesting.

I found his lectures to be pretty interesting since a lot were about personal work he did down in Peru. Quite an easy class if you put in work for the essays and keep engaged. Would definitely take him again I love his sense of humor.

analysis.name: Raphael Birya
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Amazing professor, but I wished he had given better instructions for assignments mainly the final paper. He encourages everyone to participate in discussions read the articles and watch the videos.  He does give extra credit if you attend all his lectures and submit all your assignments!

very understanding teacher and cares about connecting with his students. all he asks is that you participate in class because it is primarily discussion based. even if you don't know the answer he only asks that you try and say something. very easy class, tests fair, homework is always very easy. love professor birya he's so nice and such a king
I would love to eat BIRYAni with him.

Dr. Birya is a kind and interesting professor with great stories. However, grading guidelines are unclear and there are often confusing typos on exams. An A is a 95. Fair amount of dense readings. Usually there would be a 10+ page paper and textbook chapter to read for each class. Come to every class, as participation matters a lot for your grade!

Such an annoying class if I'm being honest. When asked for information on the exam all his responses consist of are 'Do not worry' and 'You will be fine'. Provides a tremendous amount of reading and work for an introductory class. I do not recommend taking him as this class mainly just memorization. The exams wanted you to remember specific quotes.

analysis.name: Lucia Binotti
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lucia is very kind and a great lecturer! I wasn't sure what to expect from this class but I ended up learning a lot, she made the material very interesting. As long as you participate thoughtfully, this is a wonderful class

Binotti goes with the flow, willing to change assignments if students are busy, and also passionate about Spanish literature. Participation, a group project, 5 small papers, and a final paper made up the whole grade. She is very friendly; loves when students participate (20% of grade) and share their knowledge of the few required readings/tv shows

Binotti is so energetic and fun in her lectures that they aren't boring; however, you do need to show up in order to get a good grade. There is LOTS of reading for her class but honestly you don't have to read it all. The only grades are participation and the occasional paper, which she grades very fairly and they are based on the lectures.
