Oi if you have the option to take Lucia's digital spanish 260 course TAKE IT. It is much easier than regular span 260 and a lot more laid back and fun. I thought it was an easy A;  the end of year project can be a little demanding but it's a fair balance because you don't have to do very much during the year. Also it's an EE credit :O

The professor is very unorganized. The homework is not clearly explained and the assignments are very vague. She will call on you frequently and will be condesending if you do not know the answer. Everything is done digitally and she doesnt even know how to work it. I would not recommend this course unless you are a native speaker.

analysis.name: Gary Birdsong
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If you've ever asked yourself any of the following questions, you must take this class: 1. How much weed do I have to smoke to become a homosexual? 2. Is Obama really a man, or a gay-terrorist-devil? 3. Where can I find a source of condemnation in my daily scheduel today? In summary, Professor Birdsong is what it feels like to chew 5 gum.

Passionate about the subject, though sometimes gets off topic. Known to repeat his point several times per lesson. He's a big devil's advocate and loves to contradict his students. You can skip buying the book with this one; he references one or two passages, but completely dismisses the rest of it.
Easily one of the best professors on campus. Easy discussion-based class, very passionate and very informative.

Very clear syllabus and grading criteria. Gary makes the do's and don't's of the class known right off the bat. He usually has them written right up on his signs for clarity. Despite his passion for teaching, I have failed this class. I'm still a bisexual atheist. Gary provided no feedback but to "roast in Hell". I'll see you there Gary!

Gary was my favorite teacher at UNC, and I'm pretty sure I learned the most from him. And unlike a lot of UNC professors, he never minded answering even the dumbest of questions and never shied away from controversy. Yes I failed his class and am certainly going to hell, but I'll be there with the rest of my Tar Heel friends. God Bless you, Gary.

analysis.name: Gary Biglaiser
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Gary teaches the class as an honors class, uses poorly developed slides, and threatens to beat us with a stick. Homework accounts for 10% of your grade. The TAs do not understand the assignments/problems,the homework is completely irrelevant to the exams. The TAs would say "I do not expect any of you to get this right, I barely understand it."

Jawn was a grind, bank on riding the curve. Slides were never useful (majority of class). If he does a problem on the board though, it might be on an exam. Useful things: recitation, finding book answers online for hw problems and learning from those, old exams, review sessions. Dude also definitely has adhd

I heard a lot of complaints about the class before I took him, which surprises me in hindsight because I didn't have any problems with him. He explained the material well, answered questions well, had simulations and review sessions after class for students, and was a fair grader. Decent class, relatively exams. Says "suppose" a lot.

Gary is a VERY nice guy. However, he taught us like we were phD students and I took nothing away from this class. All lectures were power points and there was 0 practice(besides extra textbook questions which were unhelpful). Help in the aide center was not helpful in any way either. If you want to learn 410 or even get a good grade, do NOT take.

Great guy, bad teacher. Very disorganized slides, few examples, mostly explained math but not how to apply it, still you had to go to class or you'd be completely lost (attendance not mandatory). HW assignments are only worth 10% but very long and only 1 problem picked at random is graded. 90% of grade is exams. Very arrogant TA, as clueless as us.

analysis.name: Codey Bills
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Codey is great. The issue is the formatting of this class. There are only so many assignments so your grade is a reflection of how harshly you are graded on the final assignments which are worth a majority of your grade. Codey is helpful and teaches the class material well. He is hilarious and makes the class go smoothly. Harsh grader, though.

Codey is amazing. He's so funny and very easygoing. He is happy to help and meet after class anytime. For the COMM 113 speeches specifically, he's a tough grader, but if you put in the effort and show you care you will do fine.

He's a real gem in the communications department. He is very knowledgeable on the topics he teaches and makes very abstract concepts easy to understand using references and lingo that students use. He is happy to explain any topic multiple times until it sticks. His anecdotes are always random but funny and do not drag on.

he was my TA for COMM120, definitely chillest of the TAs. gave us 100s just for turning most things in and wasn't nitpicky about other grading. usually late and sometimes cancels recitation, funny guy and doesn't expect you to be overly prepared (because he definitely isn't!) sweet guy

Great guy and very approachable. He made everyone feel as comfortable as possible when speaking. Gave back detailed feedback and was very encouraging. He is kindhearted and understanding. I would definitely recommend if you want to get an easy A with a kind and constructive professor.

analysis.name: Elizabeth McLaughlin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 438 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: do not trust her, she wont give any partial credit EVEN when you deserve it! i self studied everything for the final and ended up doing well ONLY because of that

While very knowledgeable and willing to answer questions, the professor's teaching style was rushed and felt unfit for students learning brand new content. The homework was very hard and not useful for tests. However, the TAs and ULA were super helpful.

Dr. McLaughlin doesn't follow lesson plans or the syllabus schedule. She puts little effort into teaching, but has intentionally harder exams than other professors and refuses leniency (i.e. dropping the lowest midterm) unlike other professors. She is passive-aggressive about people not coming to class, even though she knows her lectures are bad.

Heard shes great for Math-232+ but do not. DO NOT take her for math-231. Shes horrible at teaching the material and KNOWS it and makes the exams insanely hard that even TAs have trouble explaining the material. Told TAs to "grade harshly" to spite students that didn't come to class. Go to another profs lectures to learn. Take exams when needed.

After taking AP Calc and MATH130, I had a fair understanding of the topics, but after Mclaughlin, I have never been more confused about calc. After having near-perfect attendance for the first two midterms, I decided it was a waste of time to continue attending. She makes new notes for each class period and has not followed her posted curriculum.

analysis.name: Andreley Bjelland
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: outstanding instructor at TCU who genuinely cares about her students and their success. She makes the material easy to understand and is always available to help. The class itself is very easy and a great option for an elective or a less stressful semester. Highly recommend!

Ms. Bjelland was an amazing teacher with the most chill class. There is not much homework and most of the work you finish in class. Couple projects over the semester but she helps so much and makes them fairly easy. 100% recommend taking this class you wont regret it.

Dr Bjelland has the chillest and most engaging class. Some quizzes and discussions to do in class, but she's willing to help with all of those as long as you ask her. Tests aren't that hard also. Really caring and passionate about her work and her students
Dr. B was my favorite professor this semester, hands down. She was so caring, funny, and always helped me when I needed it. Four projects, but all are very straightforward. TAKE HER!!
So easy its not even funny. She grades projects a little weird but other than that the class was perfect.

analysis.name: Kerry Bloom
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very smart researcher. Absolutely horrible professor. Doesn't give feedback. Doesn't teach anything. DO NOT TAKE. YOU WILL REGRET. DO NOT TAKE. YOU WILL REGRET.
Do not take this class with this professor, whatever you do do not take this class. Exams are hard and are overly graded. This class is worse than Orgo.
Absolutely horrible. Worst class I've taken at UNC

Take home exams- as long as you go to office hours, he will help you get an A on all of them. As long as you participate in class every so often, you will do fine. Definitely a bias grader, helps if he likes you and you seem interested. Going to office hours is enough to get an A in the class.

The MTs and finals are open note, collaborative, and Prof Bloom will help you out if you go to office hours. His main thing is that you show up to class (he doesn't take attendance, but he notices who is there), ask questions, and pay attention.

analysis.name: Blake Faulkner
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Teaches nothing but the will to die. I CANNOT STRESS ENOUGH NOT TO TAKE HIS CLASSES. Unapproachable and rude. I consistently felt as though he was teaching a lot of nothing, then expecting an unattainable amount of work and careful thought with no content.
biased grader takes his hatred for life out on his students because he had an affair and a child and lost his pastor job at a church.

By far the worst learning experience I've ever had. He does not communicate very well (kind of ironic considering what he teaches), he does not seem to care about students. This man should not be allowed to teach anything except what not to do as a teacher.

Would not recommend. Blake was a hard grader and did not provide helpful feedback. We had three papers and a midterm and we didn't get our grades until the week of the final (the final is today and I still do not have my midterm grade). Not responsive to emails. Very snarky and rude overall. Probably should not become a professor if he gets his PHD

Such a rude and cocky teacher for a 100 level class. Extremely tough grader. If you want to inquire about a bad grade, you have to formulate an argument as to why he should regrade, if the argument is deemed illogical or is wrong he will not respond to your email, will not remade, and "reserves the right" to give you a lower grade.

analysis.name: Sarah Blanton
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: professor blanton was so knowledgable and passionate about spanish and clearly cared about helping her students succeed! she gave great feedback and was always kind when redirecting students during class and on assignments! the workload was completely manageable and she was a very fair grader! i would recommend her to anyone taking spanish!!

Professor Blanton is a great instructor who truly cares about her students. The class was challenging for me since languages aren't my strength, but if you already know some Spanish, it should feel manageable. The assignments are easy, but the exams are tougher, so regular studying is helpful.

Professor Blanton is sweet and very helpful. I enjoyed her class even though I didn't know it was all online originally. Most of the work is done in the Alcanza textbook, while classes were spent reviewing and practicing the material. Would definitely take a class with her again!

I love Ms. Blanton. She is so kind and really cares about her students. I was afraid I would not learn much since it was an online class but Ms. Blanton made the zooms very interactive and easy to learn from. I learned a lot and I definitely recommend.

I would definitely take Span 100 with her again—she was so kind and the perfect teacher for learning a new language. Even if I made mistakes during my speaking exams, she was generous with grading as long as I stayed in Spanish.

analysis.name: Paul Blom
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's a solid professor and a decent person. While nobody loves ENGL105, his section is good. You learn how to write. I'll leave it up to y'all whether you think it's appropriate for a student at an elite school like UNC to complain about being required to attend class and do simple assignments. To me, this is anti-intellectual and very dumb.

Super nice guy and good class overall. He made lots or resources available and taught helpful foundational writing skills. My one complaint is that he takes a while to grade. He clearly cares a lot about teaching and puts a lot of effort into the class to make it engaging. I highly recommend his class for English 105!

I love Professor Paul! He is so sweet, and you can tell he is a genuinely good human being. The only things I would comment on are that he takes a very long time to grade, and his lectures are also boring at times. However, his expectations are clear, and he tries to be as engaging as possible. Take him if possible!!

Every single day you have a homework assignment. So if its a M/W/F class you have to read something for each of those day and post a discussion post (three to four questions to answer). All of those readings will also be on the final. SO be ready to read. Also he is a very slow grader. Although caring about his students I would not recommend.

Cares about his students and will understand if you ever need an extension. However, missing one class reduces your grade by a point, and if you come in late, he'll give you a .75/1. There are a lot of extra credit opportunities to fix that, though. A discussion post is due before every class, and he assigns both a final project and an exam.

analysis.name: Sarah Bloesch
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If you're taking this for a Gen-ed, I recommend! She was very nice and the class was pretty easy. Lectures could be kinda boring and readings were long, but she went over them. She gives a clear study guide over the midterm, 3 essays with clear rubrics, and weekly reading quizzes. Just wish the TA gave more feedback on assignments.

Super caring professor! Easy class, just don't be rude and occasionally add something to conversations. The tests were pretty easy, essay-style but she gives you some possible prompt beforehand so you can prepare. Recitations were basically just a rant sesh about the current state of feminism and women so honestly super fun class

I enjoyed this class Professor Bloesch is great and very knowledgeable. She prepares you very well for all the assignments she expects of you. There is a lot of reading but you can get away without doing it because she goes over it during class. There is a recitation which is mandatory but not too much work overall.

Professor Sarah Bloesch is an outstanding educator! Her Sexuality and Salvation class in Women and Gender Studies was engaging, thought-provoking, and eye-opening. She fosters an inclusive environment and encourages deep discussions on complex topics. Her teaching style is clear, passionate, and approachable. One of the best professors I've had!

Attendance in class isn't mandatory but recitations are. They were pretty interesting though. Bloesch is a good professor and her lectures pretty much some up the readings. Although, if you do the readings there's not much to pay attention to in class. Exams were easy too as long as you did the readings.

analysis.name: Dennis Blair
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: super tough grader. Did extra credit papers and still got a bad grade because all he counts is the finals. Assigns way too much reading.

Not many chances to learn from a practitioner like the Admiral. He clearly puts a lot of time into his syllabus and lectures, and you won't hear stories like his from just any PWAD/POLI prof. Practical final paper, loves to support his students (rec letters, connections, etc.), and incredibly knowledgable. If you read & participate, you're all set.

Professor Blair is a brilliant man. He doesn't take attendance and rarely quizzes on readings, but it'd be a huge loss to neglect either. He's also glad to help his students professionally, his tips and reference letter being immensely valuable as a former admiral, DNI, and a talented professor. So make an effort, learn a lot, and ask for advice!
The Professor is a very intelligent man. His lecture style does leave much to be desired however. If you don't like reading do not take this course.

analysis.name: Taylor Blankenship
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I feel lucky to have had Taylor for 187. She brought real-world experience from her career into class and was accessible whenever we had questions. Her grading criteria are clear, she's funny, and she made web design seem less scary. The JavaScript section kicked my butt, but if you show you tried you'll be okay.

Taylor is such a caring and kind human, but she isn't the best teacher. A lot of times when asking questions and being confused, she would seem equally as confused and almost act as if you should know the answer. If you take this course, Google and ChatGPT will probably be your best friend.

I really enjoyed my time in this class. This was her second semester teaching this course, but she really values her students. Coming into class every day was a joy as she often makes funny comments throughout her lectures. I highly recommend taking 187 with her!

analysis.name: J Troy Blackburn
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The other prof for this class is easier, but this class was my favorite for the semester. Blackburn is an amazing lecturer, he is genuinely interested in making sure you understand the material and is down for any questions. He moved a test because it was on the same day as an anatomy exam too, he wants to give everyone the best shot they have.

The class is only lectures that weren't very detailed and very hard to learn from. You have to listen to his lecturing to understand the content, so if you miss a class or don't take notes for a class, you're going to be very lost. The class is also only made up of tests and quizzes, so if you flunk one, your grade is done for.

He was alright. I wish there were more assignments other than the tests and quizzes because they make up your whole grade. Never communicates via Canvas or Outlook and never updated the syllabus (which was crazy because he changed the dates of almost all the tests). He's very nice but if there is ever another section take it with someone else.

I did not enjoy this class, even as someone interested in physiology and neuroscience. Blackburn was incredibly lecture heavy, a big departure from other professors I've had in EXSS. Your grade is 3 tests (90%) and 3 quizzes (10%). I got A's on the MC parts of exams and quizzes and failed the short answer because of how vague the questions were.

He's a really nice guy. He's willing to work with you and in class he gives great examples to help you understand. Hes funny. Looks like a Doogie Howser and Ryan Secrest love-child, but in a cute way. Go to class and pay attention and you will be fine. Ask questions if you got to, he's willing to help!

analysis.name: Lori Boyer
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The most disorganized professor I've ever had. Already have had multiple assignments with due dates that weren't properly communicated or adjusted, even though she said they'd be moved. She's super entertaining, caring, and a fun person, but for someone teaching business communications, you'd think she would communicate more.

I honestly did not know how to rate Dr. Boyer; she's an incredible person who deeply cares for her students and is extremely reasonable. However, she is disorganized and often very behind in getting back grades to students, and in this particular class, grades are very harshly-like all other 401 professors. I would recommend taking it with her!

Difficult to get an A, A- didn't require much effort, but that's honestly just BUSI 401. Discussion based class with lots of small group work and in-class activities that aren't graded. Assignments were applicable and didn't take too long. They're graded harshly, but again that's just 401. Interesting lecturer, and I actually enjoyed going to class

She's funny and makes classes engaging. Hard to get an A, her grading criteria is very unclear at times and the feedback is not great either - sometimes even contradictory. 401 kinda sucks in general, so among the options I think she's one of the best to at least have a fun time. Just accept you will prob get an A- even if you try really hard.

Boyer's cool and a great lecturer who made class engaging. That being said, she is so nitpicky when it comes to grading. You can clearly do everything on the rubric but she'll take off ten points for no reason. I guess that's just 401. Also all her assignments are written/graded by AI which is pretty annoying since it leads to unclear guidelines.

analysis.name: Greg Bocchino
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Greg is great, I heavily recommend this class for anyone even slightly interested in public health! We just met once a week briefly on zoom with mandatory attendance, but Dr. Greg is very understanding and offers alternative options if something comes up for you. The only grade is the final paper and he wasn't a tough grader at all.
Attendance is graded; just come and listen. Only 1 essay is graded at the end of the course. Gives you directions for every paragraph that needs to be on there.
super chill class. once a week class online and attendance was mandatory. had to have camera on. only assignment was a 800 word paper. learned a lot about how to get a health career.

This class that introduces you to every public health field out there. It is a pass/fail class with only one essay due at the end of the semester. The guest speakers would each come one per week to talk about their specialty and answer any burning questions you have on career choices. Dr. Bocchino is a great resource for future Grad level planning.

Professor Bocchino was definitely the best professor I've had at UNC this far. His class is very chill as your whole grade is made up of attendance and your final paper. Very interesting content wise and you learn a lot from the guest speakers. I would definitely recommend this class

analysis.name: Ben Bolling
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: (Writing in Law) Super easy grader with rubrics to follow. Available for questions. Manageable/concise assignments, a few group projects, open note quizzes. Extremely thorough feedback. Nearly everything he says is funny. Slightly slow grading but many opportunities for revision. Not prelaw but no regrets on taking this course.

Just straight up mean and condescending, easily offended. Took a student outside mid-class and I could hear him yelling. unclear assignments & class is a lot of work. assignments build on ones before which wouldn't be so bad if he could actually grade anything so u knew what was going on. when he does grade comments come back clearly ai generated.

Ben is a very engaging teacher and gives helpful and detailed feedback on every assignment. He's also a pretty easy grader. He took a long time to grade on some assignments, but it was understandable due to various uncontrollable complications throughout the semester. By far my favorite professor this semester. Don't listen to the review bombers.

Ben is an amazing professor and an amazing person. I thoroughly enjoyed taking Writing in Law and I learned so much from him. A couple group projects and every unit was structured. Definitely more difficult than a regular 105, but so worth it if you are considering law (also worth it if you aren't). Prepare for a busy schedule but a great class!

Dr. Bolling is a great professor who is extremely willing to work with students, field questions, and provide clear rubrics and guidelines for course material. His Writing in Law class is great at teaching students about the importance of consistency and brevity in writing, and I found the course material manageable to keep up with.

analysis.name: Jennifer Boittin
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I wouldn't recommend this class as a GenEd. Professor Boittin is fine, but lectures are slow and lack clear slides. Grading depends heavily on your TA and often feels subjective, with little feedback. Attendance is a major component of your grade, and participation doesn't guarantee an A.

Boittin's lectures are bone-dry, rambling, random, and occasionally border on offensive. My biggest gripe was our unit on terrorism, which Boittin devoted to justifying why the radical beliefs of those who murdered hundreds in Paris and Nice were not to blame for the events, but rather some abstract failing of European society. Just disappointing.

Meh! That probably sums the class up well. Began interesting, but lost its intrigue as time went on. She is very knowledgable, yet this is quickly offset by her lackluster voice and seemingly disorganized lecture topics. Assignments were given at random and quizzes felt devoid of any lecture material. The recitations surprisingly saved this class.

No clear grading rubric. Quizzes were short answer style with little time to complete them. Feedback from TA's on quizzes would tell you to "add more detail" when you only had 10 minutes to handwrite an answer making it almost impossible to do so. Grade was essentially up to your TA. Unreasonably hard for a 100 level course. Would not recommend.

Professor Boittin is a nice person and an engaging lecturer. My issue with the class lies more in her TA's. I was graded very harshly on
few assignments and was not given a clear rubric or instructions on how to improve. Participation makes up a large component of the grade and despite attending and participating full credit is not promised

analysis.name: Jessica Boon
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She gives great feedback and is always available outside of class through email. She is very kind and welcoming of questions. As long as you do the work correctly and participate during class, grading is extremely fair. I would highly recommend her, especially to students who want to improve their writing and critical thinking skills.

Professor Boon is great! This class is heavily part participation and there is a lot of reading prior to class, but Boon keeps class super interesting. I would really recommend this class because it not that hard, but you do have to put effort in. There is a good bit of writing, but Boon is super helpful in and out of class.

I took this as a fully asych Maymester and was honestly surprised by how harshly she graded for how few assignments there were. Her comments were brief and unhelpful even for low scores, so you never know what you need to work on next time. She always required "more analysis" despite putting strict word limits on writing assignments. DO NOT TAKE!

A great professor. The things that UNC students write on here really devalue the degrees from this school.  Who's more qualified to say what level of work is appropriate for a 100- or 200-class? A professional with years of experience, or a teenager fresh out of high school? Stop crying about having to work hard. You're at a top college.

The directions for the discussion assignments are always so straightforward with word counts all under 200. Yet, no matter how much detail and connection and out-of-the-box thinking you do, she always wants something more. It doesn't seem possible to do so without surpassing 500 words, yet it is never enough. The grading is so arbitrary.

analysis.name: Brian Brew
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Hes a Goat. Always made it so fun to show up and as a student who is the type to sit in the back and be on there phone I was front row always paying attention to him. He does expect effort, but with how engaging his teaching is its impossible not to put in effort. Chill grader, genuinely funny guy, and great political takes. Made me want an A

Incredible professor with true passion and inspiration for his students. Gave so much grace when I struggled due to personal reasons and let me take the midterm a week late. Such an incredible professor, take his classes!!!! So funny and attendance isn't graded (but it's important unless u look at the notes) No electronics but so interesting.

brian was a pretty easy grader. one 10-12 page paper, a midterm, a final, and a couple of assignments that required you to go to office hours for a bit. he was pretty nice but he did go on random rants about primaries where he screamed for like 5 mins. there are lots of readings but you can just skim them enough to write the discussion posts
He is a great professor that is easily reached outside of class and cares about the success of his students. I highly recommend you take a class of his if possible.

Brian is pretty great. He clearly loves political science, and that is shown in his lectures. He isn't a very harsh grader, and if you are interested in political science, you will enjoy his lectures. POLI 208 had two papers, a midterm and a final exam, and none of them were too difficult. It's a good class to learn in and not worry about grades!

analysis.name: John Bruno
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: My favorite professor so far at UNC. His exam was so easy and was straight from the study guide. His lectures were interesting and he sometimes brought his dog to class. This course is taught with two other professors and he by far was the easiest one.

This is one of the best professor's I have ever had, he really cares about his students and is very passionate and knowledgeable about this course and topics. Definitely take this class, very easy and super interesting.

Dr. Bruno was by far my favorite lecturer on the FoF teaching team. His lectures were insightful and easy to follow, and he always brings his dog Mr. Lizard to class when he teaches. He gives an in-depth synopsis of the fishing industry and the fraud within it. He is also accessible outside of class and offers advice who show the initiative to ask.

Dr. Bruno was the best professor in FoF. He made lectures very interesting and was always knowledgable on what he was doing. Hes funny and is always very kind to the students. FoF as a class wasn't too hard but the quizzes were very detailed so I reccommend at least reviewing before. Everything else was graded easily, including the final paper.

One of the best professor ever met! He really supports and wants student to learn how to do research and understand sustainability related topics. Grade is not a concern for this class (he's grading fairly and  leniently) but understanding science & research is the goal.

analysis.name: Carribeth Bliem
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 315 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bliem is such a sweet lady and is passionate about her work. However, the online format made this class pretty difficult. The course is entirely self-taught; you must watch a lecture and complete a warm-up, pre-class quiz, and in-class activities every time before class. I would have definitely done better had this class been in person.

Chem 101 is going to be a tough class no matter what. Bliem is one of the better chem profs imo and actually cares about you succeeding and understanding. Lectures can be boring and monotone, but I actually enjoyed them and thought she was really funny. Exams will be harder than you expect, be sure to study everything before and after class.

Gen chem is going to be hard, no matter who you take it with because the exams are made by the department. But Professor Bliem is by far the best in the department for gen chem. 102 is over 200 people, yet she will answer every single question, answer every email, and encourage you personally throughout the course if you talk to her.Take chem w her

CHEM at UNC is very difficult; however, Bliem knows her stuff and is very kind. Her lectures are very helpful for exams. I've had a year of gen chem with her, and my experience has been fine. Definitely a lot of work, but the professor for gen chem has little bearing on your grade. Just go to Chem Possible and use other outside learning materials.

Professor Bliem is very kind and funny. Chem isn't an easy subject but she is really approachable and supportive of students. I think she does a good job of explaining concepts, and I honestly enjoyed going to lectures. Bottom line for UNC intro chem is you going to have to put in the work, but there's also support systems out there.

analysis.name: Bradley Hammer
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 86 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Boy oh boy where do I even begin. Dr Hammer....I have looked up to him ever since I first met him. The way he lectures and strikes passion into our minds. I wish it were possible to freeze time so I would never have to watch him retire. And now he's getting older, but still the goat, my goat. Thank you Doc. You changed the game of English.

Dr. Hammer is a VERY intense person who cares a lot about this class and his students. He gives long and difficult writing assignments and will not be afraid to rip you apart. However, my writing improved 10-fold because of him, and if you are a pre-med student plz TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM, you will benefit so so much from it despite the workload.

Dr. Hammer is one of the most intellectual professors you will meet at UNC. If you're taking his 105i Health and Medicine, he'll try to scare you out of it, but don't be fooled. He's genuinely really sweet and really cares for his students. But his work is VERY time-consuming. I wouldn't say it is difficult, but it's just time-consuming

Dr. Hammer clearly cares about his students. Additionally, as a premed student, he sets you up with useful resources that will help you for medical school. That being said, the class is largely him going on random (but entertaining) tangents, and all the homework assignments are group work that take hours. It's not "hard", but it's a lot of work.

Would only recommend for a certain kind of student. The hardest 105 section for sure, but if you put in the work, you'll learn a lot. He's scary at first, but when you get to know him, it's clear he cares about his students' success (+ very funny). Provides tons of outside support (peer mentor, free tutors, office hours). Participate in class!!!!

analysis.name: Bryn Werley
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Even though I am having to retake CHEM 101, that is not a reflection of Professor Werley. She is incredibly encouraging and kind. I constantly find myself remembering things she said during lecture that are finally clicking now. Professor Werley truly cares about her students, and I am very grateful to have had her as a professor.

no matter what Chem101 class you take they are all the same. Werley was more on track with lesson plans, but she often rushed through it. If this is your first time taking chem ever (i never took chem in hs ) UNC chem is really hard.... I got weeded out! Read, go to tutoring, dont cheat on smartworks. The actual exam is 2x harder than the practice.

It isn't the professor that is hard, but rather the content and class itself. A fast paced class, and heavy on content. Tests are extremely challenging, and weigh heavy into your grade. It is nice to have a recitation to talk things through. Professor was easily accessible and willing to meet outside of class time to go over study habits, etc.

Chem 101 is a standardized course, so it doesn't matter which professor you take, but Werley is pretty good. In her lectures, she often goes into detail and asks for questions from people. Chem 101 is a hard course - I recommend finding another student who has already taken the course and asking for advice on studying, you're going to need it.

Chem 101 is a weed out at UNC, so no matter the professor, the class is hard and takes a lot of work and studying outside of class time for you to do well. However, I found Prof. Werley to be a lot more engaging than the others. The one time Zurcher had subbed for Werley, I found the lecture extremely boring and just unengaging.

analysis.name: Brett Whalen
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 86 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Nice professor but unnecessarily tough grader with difficult exams. Not an easy gen ed. Don't take unless you really like medieval history.

Choose another Gen-Ed. Professor Whalen is passionate, a great lecturer, and accessible, but the course is challenging. Grades only depend on papers, midterms, and finals, all graded harshly, expecting a historian's level of understanding. There are also daily readings which are long and boring. Class is also lecture heavy.
Dr. Whalen is obviously incredibly passionate about the Medieval period and his students. Interacting with him is an excellent way to improve the uniqueness of his class.

Dr. Whalen is a great professor. He really knows his stuff and is very excited to be teaching it. He structures the class so it does not burden you too much. However, the assignments do not have clear grading criteria. Overall, a great class though and I would definitely recommend.

Avoid taking this class. Prof Whalen was a good lecturer and overall decent prof. However, the essays in this class are horrific, and are graded EXTREMELY harsh. Never have received less than a 90 on any paper at UNC, but got a B- avg. on all the writing assignments in this class.

analysis.name: Burç Köstem
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I'm in one of the first classes Doctor Burç has given, and a very he's kind and engaging professor. His class is very reading-heavy with few assignments, and class discussion is suggested but not required. Lectures are interesting (if you enjoy learning about objects with cultural significance) and reading heavy.

Class has pop reading quizzes that count towards grade (10%) for accuracy. They are not hard (mult-choice), but can be tricky. Each midterm is 25% and open note. Note that second midterm is on LDOC... You are given prompts and write two short essays. It's very manageable. Final paper is 40%. He grades fairly, but he can tell if you are bs-ing him.

Burç is actually the kindest professor I have ever had. He's super passionate about what he's doing. Expect about 2-3 dense readings per week but can get away with not doing them especially if you ask questions in class. Grades were made up of two essay exams, annotations, and a finals essay.
Really thoughtful and caring. The readings can be dense, but lectures make things clearer. Grading is fair and not a ton of busywork. If you actually show up and engage, you'll learn a lot.
The most kind and passionate professor I've had at UNC in my 4 years!! He genuinely cares about his students and explaining difficult concepts.

analysis.name: Mindy Buchanan-King
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Mindy was an amazing professor who genuinely cares about her students. She is super lenient on attendance although participation does impact your grade. You get 3 unexcused absences. There are open note quizzes with extra credit for the readings that are super easy in addition to 2 papers in place of exams. Class is discussion based.

Mrs. King was a great professor and genuinely a really nice person. She gave very helpful feedback and allowed for resubmissions, which made the class both useful and pretty easy. Overall, it was a solid class and Mrs. King was a good prof to take 105 with.

I took Mrs. King for English 123 and she was amazing. She was very understanding and is willing to work with you if you have outside issues. The class was comprised of  discussions, weekly open note quizzes (and a midterm and final paper ( no exam). It was a very engaging class, just be ready to read so you can engage in active discussion
Really cares about her students. Put the work in and you'll go far.

Professor King is a very interesting instructor. She is very accomodating when it comes to deadlines and is passionate about her work. She follows a contract grading system which alleviates lots of stress. The projects were interesting and easy to get a good grade on as long as you put in a decent effort. Would definitely recommend her class!

analysis.name: Bud Kauffman
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you're taking Arabic at UNC, take a class with Ustaaz Bud. He is by far the best professor I've had here. Despite having the class 4 times a week, first thing in the morning, I looked forward to it every time. He is so engaging and encourages you to speak and practice as much as possible. He's accessible out of class for general life advice too.

He is a really good teacher, he made a really tough language seem super doable and was very uplifting. He is really smart and gives little side anecdotes about roots of words and stuff which makes the classes interesting and less mundane.

I took 102 with Bud three years ago. I was dealing with significant mental health challenges, and had 40+ assignments that were late. I communicated this with Bud, and he accommodated me to his fullest capacity, and I passed. Now I'm about to graduate, and I still remember his kindness. His class is challenging no doubt, but worth taking.

I entered the class with absolutely no knowledge of the language and came out of it pretty confident and with a good understanding of a lot of content. He is an amazing teacher and improved my freshman year's first semester. There is a lot of work, I usually felt as though all I did was the work for this class but it is so worth it.

Oh Bud. Just an interesting man. He is really an enigma. I have been with him for multiple Arabics and I still feel as if I don't know anything about him. Anyway he is a great teacher and a great person! He cares about everyone, always makes class fun, and is really understanding. He puts his foot down for grading and missed work when appropriate.

analysis.name: Steven Buzinski
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 106 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Huge group project. Exams contain very specific questions from reading and the reading is really long. Very likely to get bad grades on exams if haven't taken psychology in high school or haven't read textbook very very thoroughly which will take tons of time.

He's a pretty good professor. Probably not my favorite, but he's an approachable person. Definitely eye-candy and great to listen to, but sometimes I'd be a little confused at the concepts he would explain. We had probably 4 guest lecturers (3 TA's) which really influenced Test 2 badly for me (multiple perspectives). Overall, I'd recommend.

Dr. Buzinski? Oh you mean the GOAT. Second time taking one of his classes and honestly they should let him teach everything. He is an incredible lecturer who makes class fun and clearly cares about his students. Upon first glance it can look like a lot of assignments but I promise they are not bad at all. Exams are super fair as well.

Professor Buzinski is an amazing teacher, and his lectures were super interesting. Grades are 3 exams, online learning quizzes, and a semester long project. The exams are straightforward; if you attend every class, you should do well. The course-long project is clear and approachable, broken up accross the semester. Overall, an enjoyable class!

Half of the course lectures were for lectures, other half were for project work. Super slow at getting grades back but all assignments were easy. Four exams, drop lowest score. Structure of class forces spaced studying, which makes exam prep easier later on. Can be flaky/slow over email, so get questions/requests in as early as you can. Nice guy.

analysis.name: Marcus Bull
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Would not take this class again if given the chance. He is extremely inaccessible outside of class and not accommodating at all. Lectures for over an hour with no visuals, no notes, nothing but talking at you. Extremely strict about everything. It feels like he doesn't respect students or even want us in the class, teaching us seems like a chore.
very supportative of students! go to his office hours and he will love you. amazing professor. be prepared to read and talk in class

This class caused me more stress than all my other classes combined. The lectures were unhelpful, full of vague, disconnected information and random pictures that you have to memorize for the tests. While he says history is not about memorizing facts, the test questions are very specific. The papers are difficult and time consuming. Not an easy A!

Professor Bull gives amazing lectures, but you're grade in his class hinges on only an handful of grades. 3 papers, a midterm, and the final are all you are graded on. The papers, however, he expects a lot from the papers. He expects a lot of analysis using a limited number of difficult to understand sources. TAKE HIS ASSIGNMENTS SERIOUSLY

Loved this class with Prof. Bull. There's only 3 papers, a midterm, and a final, so make sure you do well on everything in this class. The midterm and final weren't that hard, but the papers are graded by the TA's, so pray you get a good one, (I had Hager and she was great). There's also participation, but it's an easy 100 if you show up.

analysis.name: Juan Carrion
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I had Juan 2 times for Spanish. I hate Spanish, but Juan truly is an amazing teacher. Both courses, the students started quiet, but by the end of the semester, everyone was talking together.Juan truly cares about his students and he explains the concepts very well. I am so bad at Spanish, but I would take another Spanish class if I could with Juan

He want students to succeed and class is generally engaging and interactive. He's not a harsh grader, and offers extra credit. Sometimes he doesn't know how to explain certain grammar rules, which probably comes from being a native speaker, but he is overall a good teacher, and I learned a lot.

Juan was super kind and funny, overall great class. He made sure you knew what you needed to do and graded pretty easily. However, being a native speaker of Spanish sometimes it was hard for him to explain why certain grammar tenses are used and when they are used which is definitely a really hard part of Spanish 204.
He's super sweet & encouraging even if you're nervous about your spanish abilities. Grades pretty easily/fairly, but participation is weighted really heavy. Overall totally recommend, he's a cool guy
Señor Carrión is one of the best Spanish professors you can have. He is very funny and engaging, and this class truly helped me expand my Spanish vocabulary.

analysis.name: Karl Castillo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Total of 4(?) group projects, he keeps randomly adding them. Forgets to unlock canvas files. Doesn't answer emails. Exams have niche questions. Questions are worded poorly. Cold calls in class. Lectures are boring. With COIL, this class feels like 2 classes worth of work. Loved him for 490; I dread attending 442. Quiz every class. I'm frustrated.

Bio 457/EMES 442. Long tangent filled lectures. Super unclear exams, that aren't application based & are random facts from one-off slides. This class was sooo easy but when it came to exam time, people lost a lot of points because of how stupid the questions were. Would not take a class from him again.

Dr. Castillo is a passionate speaker. He is insightful and holds office hours and will work to make sure his class succeeds. I have taken 4 classes with him so far and plan to take more! There are also extra credit opportunities if you go to class.
This class was about corals and it was so interesting. There is a project, but the topic can be chosen for wahtever you want. As long as you try, you will succeed.

The professor is very lecture heavy, which are not very clear, and always gives pop quizzes. He has a very intricate and unclear grading system. Throughout the semester he promises that if you do all the extra credit you will be moved up a letter grade but after the final exam he claimed that no extra credit will be given or contribute to grades.

analysis.name: Ralph Byrns
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 101 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Class isn't very helpful, what he does say about econ in class is right from the book (that he wrote). But you need to go on Fridays for the weekly quiz, which is pretty hard. Lots of resources for help outside of class and lots of online assignments (which you have to pay for).  "Does that sound right?"  Worst class at UNC though so....

Coming into Professor Byrns' class I had no desire or interest in economics. In fact, I was only taking the class so that I could apply to the Kenan-Flagler Business School. Upon arriving into Byrns class, I became interested in econ as a result of his genuine interest and his amazing teaching style! He's not only a teacher but also a great mentor!

I consider Professor Byrns to be one of the most interesting people that I've met in my entire life. He did teach the history of economics (which can be dull), but he kept the class engaged with life skills and small tidbits that you'd never find elsewhere. I was so sad to see him leave UNC, but I know he loves to teach, regardless of the audience.

the only plus side to this class is the crazy amount of unexpected extra credit given at the end that prevents you from getting the horrible grade you think you have all semester. Minimal effort is need to pass this class with a C, and if you really want to learn you better read your textbook and ask your TAs for help, because byrns does NOT teach.

If you are serious about learning anything about economics, be prepared to teach yourself basically everything from the book. Unless you want a laugh, don't go to class except for Fri. Byrns is highly entertaining but if he spent half as much time actually teaching econ as he did trying to be funny, I might have actually learned something from him.

analysis.name: Gabrielle Calvocoressi
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Calvocoressi goes above and beyond for her students, is clear and communicative, and is very understanding. She is a sweet person and truly tries to ensure everyone grows in their poetry in whatever way she can.

God bless Gaby! I had the best time taking Intermediate with them, and I found myself walking away from the class feeling fulfilled and supported as a poet. They did have a tendency to ramble a little bit, but it was always interesting and engaging. They prioritized us as a class and community, and I would pay to take them again!

Gaby is a phenomenal person who will take personal interest in your work, my poetry has dramatically improved thanks to her advice. Also her class is just wonderful to be in, it's something I always look forward to, no matter how busy my other classes get.

Gaby is brilliant, as a poet and as a professor. I will 100% try to take as many classes with her as possible. She gives you so much freedom to explore and experiment within your writing. There is no judgement and she's super understanding. Her feedback is always helpful and the class environment she cultivated was superb. PLS take her if possible!

Gaby is such an amazing person and professor! I was nervous going into the class, but Gaby created an open and caring environment that allowed me to learn more than I thought possible and improve my writing exponentially! I was always excited to go to class, and it was easily the my favorite class I've taken at Carolina. Take a class with Gaby!

analysis.name: Carlina Duan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Duan is amazing, I had no poetry experience before and she had such a welcoming class for all levels. You do have to go to class and attend all workshops, there is no test/exam and the final was reading our completed poems and she brought drinks and food. I recommend this class to everyone I know!
Professor Duan is very accessible but was not the most understanding. Assigns a LOT of work, one of my heaviest workloads I have ever had at UNC, and a lot of it is not productive work.

Incredible! absolutely amazing professor who cares about every individual student. I feel like my writing improved so much over the course of the semester. This class was never a source of stress, but you can get so much out of it because of the poetry workshops, and Carlina's constructive comments on every poem you write.
Professor Duan is an angel on earth, truly. She is incredible, caring, and kind, and fosters the safest space. Her knowledge is vast and her acceptance is unwavering.

analysis.name: Cdc Reeve
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Honestly, THE BEST professors I've had here.  If you don't like reading or are closed minded you probably won't enjoy the class.  If you are willing to challenge yourself some then you will GAIN SO MUCH.  I could sit and listen to him lecture all day. Don't go into the class looking for a grade, look for an experience and the grade will come.

Great at simply laying out major problems. Enjoyable lectures that were well delivered. Many mostly well-chosen assigned readings in this course. I am sure his other classes are more difficult--PHIL 112 (sometimes taught by others) is an introductory/overview course. He knows his Greek! And he can rattle off extensive quotes from various texts!

Reeve is a great, clear professor who really knows what he's talking about. He is pretty intimidating though, so if you don't have a good TA, your questions may not get answered. He very clearly outlines the readings so you don't really have to read the books, but the exams are not easy at all, unless you're pretty good at philosophy already.

Reeve is a joy to listen to and he really knows his stuff (and is quite aware that he knows it). Readings can generally be skipped if you attend lecture, but they can help to understand the material. This class can be a challenge if you don't think the way Reeve does, but if you do you're golden

Reeve is quite possibly one of the most intelligent men alive. He is just bursting with information. He doesn't really care if you speak or not because he loves to be able to just share what he thinks and why. Do your readings, it'll help immensely. He only gives 2 grades a semester & no exams, so you'll need to do well but he wont let you fail.

analysis.name: Celeste Seifert
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I think the class is really easy, and it's not hard to get good grades if you actually try. Yes, sometimes we have to do unnecessary busywork, but Professor Seifert is pretty accommodating for most things and is pretty nice.

Super easy A for me. Just do what you're supposed to and you'll be fine. Class was mostly developing a research project over a semester, which wasn't too stressful, and the grading wasn't too tough either.

Professor Seifert has by far been my least favorite professor at UNC. ENGL105 is meant to be any easy class for freshmen to take and get through but Seifert makes the class unnecessarily complicated. She is unbelievably condescending and rude to her students. For a grad student, she has a very high ego.

Don't take this class! They grade easy with a lot of papers, but if you want a teacher that will be at least a little bit respectful this is not for you. Celeste is rude and treats us like children. at points they were very rude when answering a simple question. I never wanted to participate in this class because of how discouraged I felt.

Easy class but professor is incredibly rude and condescending. Honestly treats students like they are in middle school. She is an easy grader but if you are looking for a respectful and mature professor I do not recommend. Also coming to class was the biggest waste of time, she would take 20-30 minutes on an activity that should take 5.

analysis.name: Silvia Ceballos
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ceballos is a great professor and makes 207 super easy to understand while also teaching you a lot of useful information. Exams are very fair and are designed "for a bad day", so she makes it very easy to do well in the class. Homeworks can get a little tedious but you work in groups, and they prepare you well for the exams too.

She is a great lecturer and takes the time to review everything you need for the class. Exams are very straightforward with lots of partial credit given just for attempting. Super caring and seemed to actually enjoy teaching.

I had her for both BMME 207 (circuits) & 365 (systems & signaling). She is an amazing professor that understands that the topics can be hard. Because of this, homework can sometimes be on the heavy side, but is always worth while and amazing test prep. Never grades harshly and always is clear for dates of tests or due dates.

I had Dr. Ceballos for BMME 207 and she was amazing! I was really scared about the class going in but she took the time to explain the basics really well. She had amazing methods for solving circuits which I had never seen before in other classes. The exams are based off of the homework she provides. I can't recommend this class enough!!!

Dr. Ceballos is an enthusiastic professor and helpful professor. Her notes are always organized and well-explained. Her homeworks prepare you extremely well for her exams, since her exams are always easier than the homework. There are times when she goes over her notes too quickly during class, but she posts them online in a timely manner.

analysis.name: Cary Levine
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 158 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Levine might be a good professor for art, but for Gender, try to steer clear of him. He went the whole semester telling us we only had to "interpret" art subjectively, and then 2 classes before the midterm, he told us we had to memorize a bunch of art that we covered, their creators, and their history. Highly disappointing, do not take him.

Do not take gender as your triple-I. The class overall has very little structure, and the professors do nothing to help. Levine is very condescending and expects everyone to think art history is the most important thing in the world. This class is definitely harder than it needs to be, and the teachers DO NOT CARE.
Terrible professor with no common sense. Did not have a clear syllabus, plan, or anything regarding how the course works.

Gender was the worst class I've ever taken, especially because of the Art History section that Cary Levine taught. He would yap for a whole hour and the only thing I learned from his lectures was that women felt oppressed.The exam FORCES you to memorize artist names and dates for no logical reason in which you will forget about the next week.

Do not take gender (IDST116) The material is boring, class is not structured well, way more work than any other Triple-I. LONG, boring readings 3 times a week, 3 difficult quizzes on those readings. did NOT prepare us at all for the midterm. I'll be happy if I get a 70 on the midterm because this class is so dreary.

analysis.name: Cecile Ruel
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Ruel is genuinely the sweetest woman. She's definitely a tough grader but pushes you to be the best you can at French. She has so much advice for learning a new language, but her lectures are a bit boring. The small classes force participation but since she only teaches from the textbook the classes can get repetitive and easily skippable.

I love Prof. Ruel- take her for a language if you can. Normally these courses are taught by PhD students and it is so much better to have her- she is a good grader. She's as French as they get and does a great job getting everyone to speak. Our class has such a fun time speaking about all things French but she still covers content needed for exams.
This course took exactly as much effort as it should have. Was a little difficult at times but none of the work felt unnecessary. Fair grader and funny, good energy in class.
Super nice and helpful, in class and during office hours! French 203 is pretty grammar heavy, but she does a good job incorporating cultural knowledge and conversation skills.

I took Roml-89 with Professor Ruel, she is kind but I did not appreciate her teaching style. Professor Ruel barely graded assignments, she also is unclear with instructions and talks in circles. Although the course is called French Coastal Ecologies, we barely focused on the environment of the coast and instead talked extensively about culture.

analysis.name: Cecilia  Benninger
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. B was definitely one of the best professors I have had at UNC! She always keeps her lecturing super concise and engaging. She brings a lot of real-world and personal experiences to her class and would start every class by talking about news and sports going on in the world. I would 100% take her for MEJO-153 if you can!

If you are looking for a more hardcore journalist perspective that 153 is typically notorious for, this may not be the class for you. The class was comprised of a variety of smaller assignments that included interviews and answering questions from the textbook, and was extremely manageable. If you want to complete 153 with an A, take Benninger.
If you're looking to take Mejo 153 take it with professor Benninger. She is super down to earth and genuinely cares about her students and wants to see them succeed. Literally goated.

Dr. B is the best professor to take Mejo 153 with! She is super funny and genuinely cares about her students. We only took one test (mini quiz) the whole semester and our final was a social media project of our choice. She does not try to trick students at all. Big class discussions were a regular thing though, so have something to share.

If you need to take 153, take it with Dr. B! Not a ton of work and no tests/quizzes. The final project is a social media research project but you get to choose your topic and as long as you don't wait until the last minute you will be fine. She's awesome!

analysis.name: Celina Larios
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Celina is very fun! Energetic and engaging, she worked very hard to get everyone to participate in conversation and join discussions. Lots of readings, and participation matters a lot. Very little homework (other than reading before each class), and she's a very lenient and kind grader. Class content was boring sometimes but she made it enjoyable.

Profe Larios is so much fun. She creates a welcoming environment for students of all different Spanish levels to practice speaking. As far as 255 goes it is much more difficult than it was presented in 204.
Class time is fun but there are additional quizzes, projects, and large papers that are not related to speaking at all.
I had quite a bit of difficulty with SPAN203. Profe Larios worked hard to make sure her students understood the material. She was a fairly tough grader on things that I felt were subjective.

analysis.name: Celia Shiau
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: AVOID AT ALL COSTS. If you want to accept the greater challenge and see how well you can teach yourself, then this class is just for you. If you have common sense, then drop this class, this school, and this life. Just quit.

BIOL 545 was one of my favorite courses at UNC, largely in part to Dr. Shiau's teaching.  The 3-hour class structure was sometimes a little hard to sit through (not her fault), but she did her best to make the entire lecture engaging.  Literature-based teaching style was great and I would definitely take the course again.

Truly terrible class and professor. Dr. Shiau is super sweet and approachable in her one office hour, but cannot teach to save her life. Class was a waste of everyone's time as she could not convey a single idea. Textbook readings are awful and dense, but she tests from readings. If she's the only choice, take this class another semester.

Dr. Shiau was clearly passionate about the material, but lacked organizational skills. The class material was incredibly interesting and the small class size was great, but I often felt like she emphasized small details rather than the big picture. Overall, she is a great person, but the 3 hr lecture format of this class was not ideal.

Nice and knowledgeable, but exams were tough. Required you to know very specific details and processes from her slides, but she said that she wanted us to remember concepts from her class moving forward, which makes sense. Use GRQs to get a sense of the topic, and then gain more information in class. Not a lot of content, just a lot of specifics.

analysis.name: Yasmin Cedamanos
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: So amazing!! Please take this class if you have a chance, we learned SO much and Professor Cedamanos is an incredible teacher. Even if you struggle with Spanish she is so kind and accommodating while also pushing you to try your best. Learning Quechua as a language and a culture has been such a treat take this class!!! Fun projects as well!!

Span 105 moved very quickly, about 1 unit/3 days. However, Prof. Cedamanos was a very kind and approachable person. She is a picky grader, and very detail-oriented. You must participate several times each class to get a good grade! Much of the pacing is out of her hands, but she follows it closely, so make sure not to miss any assignments!

She is very nice and the content is not super difficult. The problem is that she grades much harsher on the pronunciation assessments compared to other teachers in the section. All in all she isn't terrible, just try to get Professor Lindquist instead if possible
Very great in class with clear lectures and examples. Helped a lot with gestures when learning. There was a lot of homework and the class did move pretty quickly.

analysis.name: Thomas Chandler
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is extremely smart, but kind of goes beyond the course material to explain what can be done in further math classes (which is great for math majors, just not my thing). 2 midterms and a final, final can replace the lowest midterm. A bunch of homework sheets that are way harder than the exam questions. Super nice guy with plenty of office hours.

Chandler's a super well-organized prof with amazing lectures, and the content isn't too hard. He's definitely passionate about the class and wants everyone to learn/pass. Homeworks and practice exams aren't too difficult and prepare you well for exams. Strongly recommend taking 383 with him, it'd be a mistake not to. Also take linear algebra first!

Best math class I've ever taken! Classes are extremely structured to really make you understand the concepts, beyond just knowing the right equations/methods. Very smart guy, but explains it clearly. Office hours are extremely helpful. Weekly homeworks and midterms are only 4 questions, very similar to the practice. Definitely take him if you can!

Super engaging professor. I would only recommend you take him if you are a math major. He dives very deep into theory and as a non-math major myself I found it hard to follow. Exams are just four questions and the second one is a lot harder than the first. Very application based as well, which I enjoyed.

British, lively, and efficient at explaining concepts and clearing up confusion. He shares his lecture notes, and practice sets mirror his brief, straightforward exams. Graded by weekly HW, two midterms, and a HARD non-cumulative final that replaces your lowest midterm.

analysis.name: Cecilia Martinez-Gallardo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: In the kindest way possible, CMG is very disorganized. She is very passionate about the topic however the whole class is confusing. Unclear grading criteria, putting incorrect answers on exams, etc. She is impossible to reach on email, and we don't even know what our grade is in the class. It sucks because she's a great person but not disciplined.

Interesting class, grade based mostly on low-stakes assignments. Do the readings/daily discussion questions, participate in class, and write a current event for basically half of your grade. The other half is a 5pg essay, group podcast, and 3 tests (multiple choice, short answer on final). She is super knowledgeable and made the class enjoyable!

She's passionate and very sweet but very hard to reach outside of class. Your grade is hidden the whole semester and you can not even calculate your own grade most of the time because she never grades most of her things. Midterms can be tricky, just study your notes hard because some of the questions are really specific.

She is very passionate and kind but is not clear on grading criteria and refuses to open her email and respond to any questions. Only way to reach her is genuinely in class after the lecture. Super sweet but no sick days or absences so make sure you show up.

She was a good professor who made the content and class interesting. However, if you like knowing what your grade is, don't take this class. She hasn't released any grades, and it's the day of the final exam. She also tends to make tests tricky, saying that there could be more than 1 right answer, but that she's looking for something specific.

analysis.name: Chérie Ndaliko
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Rivers teaches a very interesting course. I learned a lot about Africa and found myself wanting to learn more outside of class. There are 2 major projects, 2 quizzes, and various in class activities. My TA was very fair on grading, as was Professor Rivers. This course is very informative and interesting, and I'd 100% recommend taking it.

Professor Rivers is a great teacher and is very passionate about her work. The class is easy, graded by short papers, simple in-class assignments, 3 main projects, and 3 presentations. Light grading, simple content, and you get good feedback on everything you submit. Mandatory attendance, and expect some lecture and presentation days to be boring.

She is my favorite professor I've ever had at UNC, she's so incredibly passionate and cares more about her students actually gaining knowledge and understanding of the natural world, than she does about numerical grades. She's the type of professor every student wants to have. No matter how much you put in you will leave a smarter person

Professor Rivers is my favorite professor I have had during my time at UNC. She is so kind and passionate about what she teaches- and though I am not a GEOG major, I gleaned so much from this class that will prove valuable for life. If you have the chance to take GEOG 294, do so because it is an incredible, rewarding experience.
She is super nice and the class is very though provoking. Class is all about participation in class discussions and presentations. She is super understanding and just wants to see everyone succeed.

analysis.name: Cinthia Arango Sosa
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I loved Prof Sosa! She's a really lenient grader and is so sweet and understanding. You definitely have to participate in class, but as long as you do, you'll get a good participation grade. It's a flipped classroom, but the exams were pretty easy if you've taken Spanish in the past (plus they tell you what's on the exam). Try to get her for 203!

I had missed out on two years of Spanish and was still able to keep up well enough, especially considering how little previous Spanish teachers had taught me. Every time I had to make up quizzes due to medical reasons, she was very understanding and accommodated for me. She was also pretty lenient with grading at some points. I highly recommend.

I loved her!  She is super sweet and a very understanding professor usually willing to take things late as long as you contact her and explain. She never called on anyone or forced them to answer. She brought us candy and food for our end of semester presentations which was not required of her. She is very approachable and just a sweet prof.
