I have never enjoyed Spanish and this class proved it. Professor Arango-Sosa was amazing and was always willing to meet with me when I had questions. No matter how hard I studied, the exams killed me. A huge portion of your grade is participation. She doesn't care if you're grammatically correct, as long as you speak in Spanish.

She is nice, and has a pretty defined structure for the class. Occasionally, she struggled with the technology aspects of online teaching and she pretty much reads from the textbook, but she explains it well. Probably not the best SPAN 105 professor, but she is definitely better than a solid amount of them.

analysis.name: Massimiliano Cirulli
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Massi is a great teacher as well as a person. While he is strict, he is also funny. He makes learning another language cool and fun. His positivity and encouragement he gives to students make them want to learn more. Because Spanish classes at KU fill up crazy fast, this language is a good alternate. Italian is closely related to Spanish.

Massi is awesome! He cares so much about his students and puts in a lot of effort towards class. You have to do work outside of the class- as with any language- but it is easy if you stay on top of your stuff. He makes the class fun and everyone is involved during it. Attendance is key

Honestly, I didn't put in much effort and only took the class because it was a requirement. However, Professor Massi made it fun. He is an easy going guy, and the overall atmosphere of the class is relaxed.
truly caring and amazing professor

analysis.name: Menevis Cilizoglu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I had Professor Cilizoglu at St. Olaf College, where she taught Intro to International Relations. It was a relatively laid-back class, but paying attention, doing the readings, and participating in class certainly helped. She's passionate about the subject matter and entertains student questions. However, her class isn't very engaging so beware.

Menevis teaches POLI150 for a small class (30-40 students) and it makes it super interesting because she always tries to engage in a debate. Her course is clear and easy to understand, and she is always available if you have further questions out of class. The multiple choice part of her tests are easy, the short questions are harder.

Love Professor Cilizoglu, fantastic professor who is well qualified. She does a great job at making class interesting while combining wit and humor. Test's were pretty tough but would take anything by her again.
Never taking again, will waste your time. Very unorganized.

analysis.name: Cicek Beeby
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took this class having been told it was an easy A with a different teacher. This teacher in conjunction with Matt Schueller present long and extremely dense powerpoints on overwhelmingly mundane history. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Working hard for a B-/B. With that being said, Beeby is more interesting than the other lecturer and teaches better .

Do NOT take this class. Material was extremely boring, and the midterm was full of ridiculously minute details that nobody could be expected to remember. She is a nice person but not a good teacher, gives unclear instruction regularly and is difficult to understand. I would recommend avoiding this class at all costs.

The only hard part about this class is trying to pay attention and take notes for 75 minutes straight, other than that, the material that would be on the test was extremely straightforward and the tests were exactly what was in the notes/ power points. The textbooks aren't really necessary and they are really expensive I wouldn't recommend buying.

This class wasn't too amazing, but it is a WB gen ed. It wasn't awful but the papers are tough and the tests are worse. Cicek was a pretty entertaining lecturer for the material but it wasn't enough, especially to keep my attention for an hour and a half. If you like ancient history, then go for it, otherwise you may want to look elsewhere.

Cicek did not make lectures very engaging and interesting, so it was very hard to pay attention. Her power points were vague. My friends and I absolutely dreaded going to this class. The tests are very hard, she expects you to know all the drawn plans of each city. This course could have been better if taught by someone else.

analysis.name: Joseph Cima
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The limit as x approaches a passing grade in this class basically doesn't exist. He has cool classical music playing in his office during office hours though, so take advantage of them. You're better off getting the cafeteria workers to teach you calculus than this guy.

He holds consistent office hours but his communication skills are so poor that it's pointless. He'd start on one topic and forget what he was doing midsentence and move on to a different example. He didn't know how to do half of the problems and mainly read frm the book. We had one test all year and ambiguous grading. Worst teacher I have ever had.

One of the worst math professors I have ever had!  This class is known to be hard, but his absent-mindedness and unrecognizable scribbles on the board did NOT help.  Had to drop this class.  He's crazy smart and has good stories, and he's nice (he pulled a box of kleenex out of his desk drawer during office hours one day) but he cannot teach!

Worst math teacher I've ever had. Always gets lost in the problems, can't use technology, made us all buy books that he wanted to use not the ones the book store sells. Unorganized. You never know what section you're learning anthe examples he gives have nothing to do with the homework and neither has anything todo with the tests. Enjoy

I frankly thought that he was the most horrible teacher there is!  I mean I didn't understand a word he was talking about.  You should only take that class if you are willing to teach yourself, which defeats the purpose of having an instructor, right?!  Anyways, never take his class...taking his class will mess up your gpa.

analysis.name: Christopher Roark
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 134 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The only people who liked this class are the ones who do not care about their grades. I actually had a stroke trying to understand all the contradictory points in the materials.

Overall lectures are confusing, problem sets only minimally help solidify concepts taught in lectures, and his responses to questions on campuswire are often vague. Chill guy but not great at helping to understand material which is already difficult. Takes up time trying to be funny at least once every lecture but speeds through difficult concepts.

I learned from this class by rewatching his lectures. His lectures and homework are full of mistakes. It's the kind of mistake that confuse students. He also said the wrong things in class multiple times. For example, "Demand curve moves leftward...I mean rightward." MULTIPLE TIMES. It was a very frustrating experience.

I like this better than 420, and he's genuinely a really nice guy which makes it a lot better. It isn't super easy content, but my complaint is really just that he makes the homework sometimes unnecessarily hard. One question will be completely fine, easy even, and then the next has math so convoluted that a TI-84 can't process it. Just annoying.

Professor Roark is great! I've had him for both 420 & 425. He is generous with curves, accessible, and provides PLENTY of test prep. There are weekly assignments, but he will sometimes extend deadlines. Had an injury I was out for a month for, so he met with me via zoom to keep up. Hard content, but if you do hw will do fine. Take with Roark!

analysis.name: Claudia Malhotra
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Malhotra is very knowledgable about marketing, and it makes lectures great. The flipped format is helpful for learning, and I find her, and her directions clear. My complaint would be the group cases, as I spent more time fixing others work and formatting rather than actually using marketing strategies. Grading is subjective and unclear.

30% of grade is 3 case studies she grades very tough and also includes an unrealistic page limit. For exams it's literally just hundreds of definitions, which is fine but she creates really niche arbitrary questions that I don't think trust ones true knowledge of Marketing. Very tough but also very nice at the same time. Would never take her again

Claudia is someone that was meant to be a teacher & it is so evident. She is so caring and understanding of her students & I genuinely appreciate her as a human being sooo much. Honestly, I won't say this class is easy, because I didn't find that to be the case. But taking her class was worth it because she is so knowledgable, passionate, & kind.

Amazing professor, cares so much about both her students and the material. Her passion and fun in class activities made this one of my favorite classes at UNC. Cases were a lot of work but graded fairly (loved new rubric system). Midterm/final surprisingly hard, definitely study and practice term definitions. Highly recommend, learned a lot!

Claudia is an incredible professor who clearly cares about her teachers and is very passionate about marketing. She always brought energy to the class and it was never boring. The class does have a lot of work and the case assignments can be tedious. The midterm I thought wasn't bad and final was harder. Both very heavy on memorization.

analysis.name: Christopher Clark
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 67 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Clark is awesome. Focuses on the significance of the material, not facts. His tests are reasonable and he is an interesting lecturer.

Love his lectures and enthusiasm for the class. His slides are organized, and lectures are eloquent and easy to follow, and exams are reflective of what you've done in class. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you need to go and also read the book to do well. TAs are in-charge of 35% of your grade, so make sure they like you in recitation.

This class is Minority Representation. There are 3 exams (none of them are cumulative) and he gives you a study guide a few days before each exam. There is one research paper towards the end of the class. Really interesting and fairly easy class. He goes over the readings in his lectures

Great professor, but lowkey not the easy A I thought it would be. Exam questions come from study guides. Essays were a time crunch since he tended to delay releasing prompts, but they were not too difficult. He has funny tangents in class. Great guy, make a lasting connection with him! Grades: 3 essays, 2 exams, participation (attendance)

Prof Clark is one of the most caring professors I've had at UNC. Although his classes are lecture-heavy, he throws in lots of engaging material (campaign ads, speeches, etc.) and plenty of jokes. Take a class with him if you can!!!

analysis.name: Clay Williams
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Clay is one of the best professors I've had. He is super charismatic, cares about his students, and super accessible outside of class. The feedback given on assignments is so valuable. The class moves fast with assignments almost every week, but it's very manageable. I would hands down take another class with him in a heartbeat!

Clay is so awesome! He is super funny, kind, and a great professor! He really wants to help his students succeed and creates a very easygoing, fun learning environment in the classroom! The work is straightforward, and it's extremely likely you will get an A! Would take his class over and over again if I could!

Professor Williams is honestly one of the best professors I have had. There are quite a lot of assignments in the course, but I always felt prepared. Clay gives incredible feedback and cares so much about your success. I truly feel like I'm a better creative person because of this class.

considering his first time teaching, did a not bad job! do expect assignments to kind of hit at the same time, but they aren't hard to complete and there are options to rework for a better grade. definitely got to take away a decent amount of skills!

Clay was an absolute joy the entire semester. Deadlines and grading criteria are super clear, and you have an automatic two-day grace period for every assignment. Not sure what he's teaching now, but whatever it is, take it!

analysis.name: Josh Clemson
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Josh is new and has room to grow, but the class improved a lot throughout the semester. The midterm was tough but he took accountability and allowed test corrections and provided extra practice materials. Allowed us to submit a draft paper for feedback, and exams had EC. Keep up with the readings and participate and you'll be fine. Nice guy.

Josh seems nice and could be a good professor, but he made PLCY 581 way harder than normal. We had two harshly-graded papers and a hard midterm. Josh did give chances for corrections on midterm, but paper grades were unnecessarily nitpicky and unclear. This class ended my 4.0, and I never really felt like I had a real chance of getting an A.

You should immediately consider taking anyone else. His grading was unfair, harsh, & inconsistent. He also offers no actual assistance be it office hours or online. He made the notoriously manageable core PLCY class absolute hell, and ever other section had it much easier which was really unfair and disheartening. Not kind, capable, or helpful.

Trying to succeed in his class felt truly Sisyphean. You can go to office hours, read the textbook, pages and pages of the readings he assigned, and still not feel confident for his assignments. He was such a discouraging instructor. His syllabus said that effort does not mean success and boy was that true. Take anyone else for 581.

I think with more experience he could be really good professor because he knows the material well, was accommodating, and quick to answer emails and questions. However, I know from working in pairs with different people throughout the semesters that most people found his lectures hard to follow, which was the main issue.

analysis.name: Jordan Claytor
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 164 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: He was a good prof but the exam questions were designed to trip you up and some of the questions were very poorly worded. The exams make up 70% of your grade so you're out of luck if you get lower grades on two of them. The written responses were easily misinterpreted and worth a lot of points, so I would say to make sure you read carefully!

Although Claytor is nice as a person, this can be easily overlooked when the exams are worth so so so much of your grade. From someone who is OOS and always had an A in high school bio/chem this is super difficult esp if you have other hard classes. The tests are there to stump you and really are tricky even if you know material.

course is entertaining but the lectures are almost useless and everything relies on self-study. Each question is 3 points out of 20, and one mistake means losing all 3—dropping to a B. It counts heavily toward the grade. Covering 150 pages in three weeks all on our own makes the setup unreasonable, with a grading system that feels truly unfair.

This class isn't too bad, there is a good amount of work before and after class but it's pretty easily managable. The exams are pretty difficult, but one gets dropped and there is a bunch of resources to help get you ready. In general, Dr. Claytor is really caring about his students and he's very engaging.

Professor Claytor is great, teaches things in a way that is understandable and fun, and truly cares about students. BIO 101 is just a very difficult weed out class. Tests are weighted super heavy. Claytor made it enjoyable, but it is a lot of work and difficult to get an A.

analysis.name: Clark Gray
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Do not take this class if you are not good at weekly quizzes on lengthy papers. The quizzes are hyper specific and they are not open note making them quite tricky as they are a large part of your grade. The work wasn't necessarily bad, but Dr. Gray is not accommodating or flexible on any assignments.

Extremely picky about grading papers/labs and would take off points for the tiniest things. Also had extremely specific weekly quizzes that were closed note and based off of multiple readings that were laughably long. Kind of nice, sometimes? Kind of also passive agressive.

Do not take him for GEOG120. He is lazy when making notes for class and his tests are way too specific. Unless you plan on dedicating a large amount of time to studying for this class, do not take it.
Pretty straightforward class, interesting (but lengthy) readings and complicated quizzes. Grading was pretty inconsistent, but fair ins ome cases. He did not  fw me but was pretty chill to others.
had weekly quizzes, really nice guy, would definitely take it again

analysis.name: Cristobal Clemente
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Easily the best professor I've had at UNC! He is fair and non-judgmental, and he turned around my entire perspective on Spanish. He's a talented professor, and a cool guy all around.

He is the best professor at UNC. He really cares about your grade and loves it if you go to office hours. you can make an A if you study, he is a fair grader, and he usually tells you what to study for quizzes and tests if you ask him. He doesn't tell you when assignments are coming so make sure you look at the syllabus. Take him for sure. 10/10.

The best Spanish teacher I have ever had hands down. Not only does he know everything about Spanish (native), he also tells you what is important and what is necessary to know to be an actual fluent speaker. Readily available to talk about topics outside of SPAN, he is constantly teaching our class the culture and history of spain. Take him!!

Prof. Clemente is the best ever. Super caring and kind guy who recognizes the common pitfalls and works to help you avoid them. He is Spanish himself and likes to share fun phrases or stories about Spain. He cares about you as a person and you learning Spanish. He is just awesome!!

This professor was one of the nicest and most understanding professors I have ever had. He always helped with any homework, test, or general questions I had and did whatever he could to make sure students understood what he was teaching. He always made everyone laugh and wanted everyone to succeed.

analysis.name: Clara Yang
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
Dr.Yang is great and super caring for students! 
Def needs a lot of practice to make lessons smooth, and it matters a lot whether you've worked on the things taught in the previous lessons. 
Piano is never easy but Dr.Yang makes it inspirational.

Took Piano Lit with Professor Yang. Great teacher. Really wants to see all her students succeed. She is very accommodating of students and, as long as you let her know ahead of time, you can miss class occasionally. Her lectures were clear and captivating. All in all, a great teacher, passionate about the subject material.

Dr. Yang is one of the best pianists and professors I have ever had the pleasure of meeting. She always finds ways to improve your skills as a musician and is there to help you achieve any musical feat you desire. I have seen so much progress  and development in myself as an individual since taking lessons with her.
One of my favorites at UNC. Just one of the kindest and most intelligent people on campus. I love this woman.

analysis.name: Claudio Battaglini
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. B is the best professor to take 376. He is so passionate about the material and keeps you engaged in an 8am class. This is a tough class with a lot of material, but the exams were pretty straightforward and he always wanted his students to succeed. He is so understanding of circumstances, but you need to put in effort to do well in the class.

Dr. B was truly a great professor. He completely cares about his students and is really invested in the material. He sometimes goes over lecture time, but not too much. We didn't entirely stick to the syllabus, but he ended up giving points back for free essentially. He offers extra credit; I would totally take this again!

I took LFIT 113 (Weight Training) with Dr. B. I was nervous to take this class because I have no previous weight training experience, but Dr. B was an amazing teacher! He is so friendly, patient, and caring. He was very understanding of our individual needs and helped us create our own personalized fitness plans. I highly recommend LFIT with Dr. B!

Dr. B is the best. He is caring and super enthusiastic about the material which makes it easy to pay attention, he is hilarious and uses his expertise to help give real life examples. His tests are focused on the material he repeatedly mentioned and the very few homework assignments were easy. Pay attention in class and you will do great.

just had him 409 (wasn't and option) not 410. The class is super chill and geared to exposing students to different clinical population and how exercise can be used to aid in their disease treatement. Your grade is composed of a semester long group project and article reviews. Dr. B is super enthusiastic and approachable!

analysis.name: Marsha Collins
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took Cervantes class with Dr. Collins - reading heavy, obviously, but we took Don Quixote piece by piece and she knows so much about the book, so lectures were interesting, even at 8AM. Did not provide super clear feedback about grading criteria, but wasn't harsh, either. Take notes in class and you'll be prepared for the minimal essays + exams

Professor Collins is a gem! She is very eloquent in how she describes curiosity and the imagination and is so intelligent. On top of it all, she is one of the sweetest people I have ever met! If you have the opportunity, take a class with her. Although there is plenty of reading(I don't like to read), I thoroughly enjoyed the class and lectures.

Amazing professor. You read a lot of books but she covers them thoroughly, so as long as you take notes you're fine! Few tests (Midterm, 1 paper, 1 group project and final). Gives comprehensive feedback and she's the sweetest teacher. Take notes and you'll be grand. Take this class!

This is the second class I have taken with her and it was the same format. There is one group presentation, a research paper, and two exams. She is very kind, but class can get kind of boring. It is all discussion and presentations. She grades fairly easy and I would likely take another class with her.

She's very passionate, but she teaches in a confusing way. Classes were discussion based and exams were based on stuff mentioned by students in lectures. No rubrics were given for anything. You never know what she's looking for, and she mentions out of the box connections in your assignments and takes off points if you didn't make the connections.

analysis.name: Matthew Crawford
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Considering the fact that Math381 is one of the hardest freshman year classes, Crawford made it extremely easy to follow, understand, and do well. First Midterm: 101, Second Midterm, 95. Bonus questions on midterms were understandable and the "pop" quizzes we had were mainly easy 100's. Could not be more happy with Crawford's Math381 course.

Matt was respectful, understanding, and enthusiastic. He was very charismatic in his approach to lecturing, and his office hours greatly helped on the difficult topics. This was by far the most difficult course I've ever taken, and the learning curve was tremendous. However, Matt made the material genuinely intriguing and I'd recommend him for 381.

Matt is awesome. I think he's one of the harder professors for 381 but not completely sure, however he made the lectures super engaging and encouraged us to think critically. Made himself available outside of the classroom as well and is a hilarious and smart guy. Would recommend, course is incredibly hard though. I pass/failed.

Very nice/open to questions. Was his first year teaching though, so pace lagged behind 2 days and a few lectures had to teach self rest of content. Midterm 1 average: 72%, midterm 2 average: 70%, historical final average: 65%. Not easy, but among other options (especially Snoeyink if CS major) is a good choice. Study hard though.

Professor Crawford was O.U.T.S.T.A.N.D.I.N.G. By far the best math professor ever. He is only a graduate student, too! In his class he is animate, enthusiastic, and very encouraging. He truly cares for the success of his students. Timely email responses and very enjoyable classes. If you aren't taking Matthew Crawford, WHAT ARE YOU DOING!!!??

analysis.name: Tim Crothers
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors I have had at UNC. Super engaging and inspirational lectures. You will learn so much in this class and become a much better feature writer and writer in general. Graded on three long-form feature stories and much of the work had to be done outside of class.

Professor Crothers keeps class very interesting and has a lot of experience in journalism, and it shows! He has high expectations, but as long as you put in the work (and double- and triple-check your AP stylebook), you'll do well. 153 has a heavy workload, but he keeps it very reasonable. Ask him about Queen of Katwe sometime!

This is a one of a kind class. It's entirely guest lectures with notable people in the sports media field, with short weekly assignments and two papers at the end of the semester. Prof. Crothers repeated that if you take this class for a grade, that's the wrong reason. He's right, this is networking and insider info galore. Take this class!

(For MEJO 153) Professer Crothers is the most outstanding professor I have taken. His real world experience shines through in a way that makes you feel that you are truly learning. Not only do I feel I have become a much better writer, but I also feel that I am leaving the class a much smarter person, overall. Definitely will take again!

Professor Crothers is the most influential professor I've had at UNC so far. The feedback he gives on papers is also super helpful. The only reason I didn't rank 5/5 is the lack of a Sakai page, canvas site, or even a specific syllabus. This made it difficult to keep up with my grade or what we were doing in class.

analysis.name: Lorraine Cramer
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 74 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
1. She is disorganized--a FACT, not an opinion. She can make things that can be explained in a few sentences into complete chaos and get you more confused.

2. She makes jokes: good ones, offensive ones, and ones that don't even make sense.

3. Get ready to read and watch her lecture recordings. You'll spend tons of time every week on this course.

This class was horrible, even if it's required for your major, take it elsewhere. It's incredibly difficult to memorize the amount of info that Dr. Cramer expects. Her lectures don't help, it's not quite clear what will be on the exams (which are ~70-80% of your grade) bc she's so disorganized in her lectures. Honestly she's not helpful at all

Don't take this class. The grade is based almost entirely on exams,required to write blog 3 page every week he exams require memorizing lectures, the textbook, and Anki material. No study guides.the teaching style made the course overwhelming and hard to understand. I would not recommend this class.

The worst professor at UNC. All she does is talk and ramble. Makes the tests impossible and only has 2 (apart from the final) so that they make up 40% of your grade. When there are only 1 or 2 people making 100's on the tests, that's when you know the prof is the problem. Too bad shes the only one who teaches MCRO at UNC. Avoid her at all costs.

Dr. Cramer is a nice person, but she is not the best professor. Her lectures are quite difficult to follow, and she expects you to know random information from the lectures that likely have no real world application. Tests are extremely difficult, though she curves just a bit. You will need to give all your attention to this class to succeed.

analysis.name: Elyse Crystall
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I never felt unsafe in a learning environment ever in my life until I took a class with this woman. She thinks her opinion is the only one that matters. If you offer a differing point of view or even just ask for clarification about an assignment, she will yell at your in front of the entire class. I once had a panic attack on the way to her class.

As previously stated, this woman does believe that her opinion is the only opinion.  As a very liberal person myself, politically and socially, I find her liberal bias in the classroom unnecessary and limiting to her young students.  She is SOOO politically correct that it makes real debate and dialogue in the classroom impossible.

AVOID taking this class. She is very vague spacey, but manages to get snappy and angry when students make mistakes. I sat next to a slower boy in class, and she ripped into him often (cutting him off sharp tone eye rolling). SO RUDE!!  If you take it, buckle down, do your very best work, and always cover your butt by taking the extra mile.

On one of the last days of class we were put into groups and then asked to write what we liked about the class and what could be done better. When people offered constructive criticism they were shot down with excuses and disrespectful remarks. I have never been more afraid to offer my honest opinion in a class. Consider switching if you get her.
If you have to rearrange your schedule not to take her class, do it.  It's worth it, trust me.  So mean and so stubborn.  A total headache.

analysis.name: Cristiana McFarland
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Cristiana is one of the best WGST professors I have had. She is so caring, and her lectures are very engaging. WGST 224 is an interesting class, and I would totally recommend it. I would also recommend taking good notes during lectures and doing the readings so you do well on the midterm and final. Her exams are fair though if you pay attention.

Cris is really cool and her class was very progressive. She was really nice and there was literally no work. The tests were all multiple choice which sucked but also didn't. Just go to class to get participation points, I never went to class so that's why my participation grade was so bad. Otherwise easiest A.

Cris was very chill and nice! There is not a lot of homework and two exams. Her lectures were interesting for the most part. Make sure you take notes and listen in class to do good on the exams. I recommend her!
She is the sweetest professor and so funny! She cares about her students a lot. We did questions of the day at the beginning of class every day and it was so fun!

analysis.name: Lorraine Cramer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 128 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I am in Dr. Cramer's class right now & I just have to say she is the most hard working & caring professor I've ever had. Yes, the class is difficult & time consuming, but the material is so interesting & applicable to real life it makes studying worthwhile. Her exams are NOT tricky! You have all of the resources you need to be successful.

This is a HARD class, but an A/A- is obtainable. It really is just all memorization, but it is A LOT of information, so keep up with Anki, organism cards, and go to SI sessions! I LOVE Cramer and she really does care about what she's teaching, but honestly, she can be a bit frazzled at times. Still, the resources are there for you to succeed.

Her exams are EXTREMELY memorization based. I love a good application based test and these are not that so they were very difficult for me. ANKI is your best friend. And so is Dr. Cramer. So sweet in office hours, will give you fist bumps for questions you got right on the exam, etc. MCRO is hard, and needs a LOT of time but it is worth it.

I loved this class. people complain the tests are tricky, but they are not tricky. They are rather simple. I think people are overly interpreting the questions. She really cares about her students. you should go to her office hours. at least study 2 weeks ago. recommend the class. go to the class since polleverywhere questions are provided everyday

I have never seen a professor as excited about the subject material or more determined to help her students succeed. The class was the most challenging I've ever taken, but the difficulty is unavoidable, reasonable, and material is interesting. You will succeed by using every resouce and studying every day. Do not underestimate it, and have fun.

analysis.name: Harry Cushman
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cushman if you're reading this I'm so sorry. I almost hit you with my car the other day on campus. I don't want you to know it was me because you're my favorite professor and I don't want you to hate me but I want to say I'm so sorry it was me who almost hit you. I'll be more careful I'm so sorry. I hope you have a great break!

I don't understand why all the comments are good. Dr. Cushman is a nice person and can be flexible, also knowledgeable about his field. But the syllabus is super disorganized and looking back, I learned zero stuff in the class and really thought it was a waste of time. To do the final project you really need background knowledge outside or prior.

i loved this class and really enjoyed the book. it felt like one large book club! if you are even considering this class, take it. in fact, even if you don't enjoy reading, take it. it was so fun getting to hear everyone's different perspectives and takeaways from the novel—that's what reading is all about, after all!
I took this class a year ago and another class with him last semester. He is very kind and knows a lot about the subject matter. Not too much writing, which is nice for a freshman seminar.

I loved this class so much! He is such a great teacher, and he really helped us think about the text deeply. It wasn't very hard at all. I looked forward to the discussions because everyone in the class was so into it. He is a pretty relaxed grader and very nice person.

analysis.name: Mark Crescenzi
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: THE MOST AMAZING PROFESSOR !!! He actually acknowledges that we are in a pandemic right now !! Not only does he want each student to succeed, but he shows that he cares by constant encouragement throughout the semester in emails/Zoom meetings !! He is always available and helpful during office hours, easy to talk to, and has great lectures !!!

Prof Crescenzi is one of the kindest and most empathetic educators I've ever seen and taking his class made this entire online semester that much more enjoyable. He encourage feedback like no prof I've seen before. He's reminds of a skinnier political science genius Santa Clause. If you get the chance to be in one of his classes, go for it!

Prof. Crescenzi is amazing! So understanding of students' needs, good lectures. Super knowledgeable but knows how to teach an intro class in a way that is perceptible and interesting. This class is not hard to get a good grade in if you do the work. It gives you a great toolkit to continue learning about POLI!

Professor Crescenzi is a dedicated instructor who makes a genuine effort to support students. The class has a heavy workload, but his insights and unstuckstudy AI make it manageable. Worth taking if you're interested in the material.

Professor Crescenzi is phenomenal. He truly cares about the wellbeing of his students and has a passion for the material at hand. Overall, the class wasn't too bad with lots of writing assignments, a midterm, and final. Some of the reading was dense, but he was understanding and lectures clarified any confusion. Take any class you can with him!

analysis.name: Tyler Curtain
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 57 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: You will not regret taking this course. He knows what he is talking about and makes class very engaging. Often makes you think outside of the box and dive deeper into hidden meanings of films. Make sure to participate, actually watch the films and memorize the facts he asks of the movies. Not being to check grades was no stress honestly.

Loved this class. Very discussion-based class, that's why participation and attendance matters. Usually a smaller class so he'll notice if you're not in class for a few days. Lots of reading but exams are easy and grading is lax. I enjoyed his class tho! Easy A if you're okay with reading and speaking up at least once a class.

I LOVED THIS CLASS. It was SO interesting, and I would recommend it to basically everyone. If classroom participation really stresses you out, you might find this class to be scary, but he is so interesting to listen to and the seminar is very good.

I audited this class, so grain of salt, but Dr. Curtain is kind and extremely knowledgeable about horror movies. He isn't afraid to call on people out of the blue and challenge their answers, but he's also funny and encourages discussion. Really enjoyed this class.

Genuinely a great class. Professor Curtain really makes you think about the films you watch, I have a whole new perspective of sci-fi film now. All you do is talk about the films/books in class, make sure to watch/read everything because he will cold call. All films except 2 books during the whole semester but easy reads. 1 midterm and 1 final.

analysis.name: Cynthia Current
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 81 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Current's class was almost unnecessarily difficult. She seemed like a nice person but she was very narrow-minded with how she wanted things to be written. When reading through comments on my papers, it felt as if she was marking them simply to have marked them. She rambles in lectures and is very hard on attendance. I don't recommend her class.

Worst professor I have had in all my time at UNC. Beyond unorganized, fails to lay out clear and succinct expectations for assignments and grades like you are supposed to know exactly what she wants when she doesn't tell you. Doesn't bother updating assignment information from previous semesters. Avoid! Find a professor who has their act together.

Dr. Current is super nice and the class is not too hard if you're doing the readings. Class participation is super important, but if you have anxiety about public speaking you can talk to them because they're very understanding.

Take 105 with a different professor. I cannot stress enough how passive aggressive and awful Dr. Current is. She will send you nasty emails ridiculing you if you miss a class or an assignment. She was non-understanding and rude even when I was mentally struggling and when I had COVID. She also rants about her opinions often instead of teaching.

Arbitrary grader. It is clear from her condescending emails/feedback that she thinks extremely highly of herself. She spends most of class on a rant about something random. She is very serious about attendance/doesn't regularly offer zoom. She does give extensions if needed. No one got less than a B, but ENGL 105 is supposed to be an easy A.

analysis.name: Kyle Cunningham
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Choose Kyle as your 105 teacher. 30 mins of work PER WEEK, easiest class you will ever take, 1 assignemnt a week, asnychronus classes, at the end he lets you argue for an A if you somehow dont already have one. He's also super super chill.

kyle was amazing! he is very kind, down to earth, and funny. he cares about his students and is very flexible with due dates and assignments. he also gives very good feedback and grades fairly. very chill and easy class, good for people who don't want much work to do for their 105 class.
Kyle might be the best 105 teacher. Allows late submissions, easy assignments that take 1-2 hours a week max. Also you can call him Kyle and not professor Cunningham
This is genuinely the easiest 105 course you could take. Such an easy grader and there is barely any work

Professor Cunningham is incredibly kind and genuinely cares about his students' success. While the textbook is required, he doesn't use it. His assignments are manageable, effective, and well-structured, and he provides excellent feedback. Though attendance isn't mandatory, attending class occasionally is beneficial.

analysis.name: Graham Culbertson
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Graham is v passionate & the BEST! I didn't know what to expect, but this quickly became my fav class. You read weekly, play board games in class, & write discussion posts. The final is playing a board game that u create. Graham truly cares ab his students & uses a low-pressure grading style that makes u rly want to put in effort. HIGHLY recommend

Great class that provides a broad history of action films in a low-stress environment. Daily film viewing + discussion posts, plus three papers. For all assignments, if you meet the word count, you get an 100. The short video lessons were really informative, and Culbertson gives good feedback on papers. Really fun class, definitely recommend.

Professor Graham was an amazing teacher! We had different units which were all very unique. Definitely not a traditional teacher in his grading contract-- but his system of 100 or fail made it a lot less stressful and allowed us to explore the content more! Provides a worldly view and always opened the class up for group discussion! TAKE HIM!!

The easiest professor I've had at UNC! Doesn't believe in making students stress about grades, so you either get a 100 or a 70 on assignments/projects/papers, no in between! I believe everyone in my class ended with a 100% in the class. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!! Group final project was so fun, you literally played a video game. Love Graham!

I love Dr. Culbertson. He's frank, witty, philosophical, and a lot of fun to talk to. I'm a STEM major, and it made me genuinely sad when I realized I probably wouldn't be taking another class of his.

analysis.name: Paul Cuadros
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Cuadros was an awesome professor! The class was very consistent in work, which was a good schedule to follow, but also not overwhelming in work. Cuadros is very considerate with extended help and is very open to questions. I really enjoyed this as a fun journalism course.

Continually brought in bias in class, he was by no means impartial to anyone who went against his grain of thinking and you paid the price with a poor grade. It was either submit to his ideals, thinking or fail the class. No dissent, independent or critical thinking was allowed.
Paul Cuadros is a tough grader and expects you to turn in quality work, however, he is extremely caring and sees potential in all of his students.

Professor Cuadros is a gem in the J school, and if you aspire to be a journalist or reporter, you have to take a class with him. You have an article due every week but this class teaches you so much and Cuadros is super accommodating, caring & gives excellent feedback. He is a great person to know and he deeply cares about his students doing well.

An amazing, seasoned reporter with a love for teaching and developing his students' crafts. Tough work (one article a week, 3+ interviews, conducted remotely), but accomodating with people not getting back to you and granting extensions. Grading is based both on AP style and how he thinks it reads, so there can sometimes be "hidden traps."

analysis.name: Emily  Curtin
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Climate Change and Health was an incredible class and while topics can be quite heavy, they are relevant and easily applicable to life outside university. Dr. Curtin is very approachable and her knowledge of various fields makes her a great lecturer. 390 is heavily based around discussion. Do the reading + participate and you'll do well.

I cannot recommend professor Curtin enough! I took anth of fitness culture with her and it was so fun! lectures are discussion based and very entertaining. You complete a research project of your choosing during the semester, and the workload is split up well throughout the semester. she is very supportive and wants you to succeed.

Very knowledgeable- all readings are on canvas or accessible through UNC. Gender, sexuality, and health is lecture based with student led discussions some weeks. attendance required but 2 absences no questions asked allowed. HIGHLY recommend to any med anth major/minor or anyone interested in the topic!

One of the best professors at UNC—this was my second class with Dr. Curtin, and I'd take a third! Lectures are engaging, and grading is fair if you put in the effort. The class focuses on understanding and thoughtful discussion over regurgitating forgettable facts. Highly recommend Gender & Sexuality and Bodies Under Capitalism (390 courses).

Dr. Curtin is so easy to talk to during class and office hours. She is slow to grade things, but most of the assignments are really straightforward, easy, and completion. Those that are not are not worth a huge percentage of the grade

analysis.name: Cyrus Sinai
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Cyrus is absolutely the best professor I've ever had! He cares so much about his students and it's clear that he truly loves what he does. I especially like how he takes the time to get to know students and goes above and beyond to make the course relevant and interesting for everyone. Additionally, if you pay attention in class, you'll do well!

Cyrus is the absolute goat. He is willing to work with you on extensions, late work, anything you need. the man would probably donate a kidney if I needed a transplant. homework is extremely light since my class voted to move half the assignments to be optional. extremely easy tests: 1-pagers allowed, hard questions dropped, you can get points back

Nicest professor ever. Cares so much about his students and their success and is very passionate about the topics he teaches. Not a lot of work assigned, 1 assignment and reading reflection per week and only 1 midterm and final which you can use a one pager on each. Would recommend him to anyone. Take his class!!
I haven't finished the class yet, but i dont need to. It was that easy. I already got an A+ and its September.

Cyrus was an amazing teacher. Unfortunately it looks like he won't be back next semester but he made the class so engaging and enjoyable. Everyone I talked to also loved the course. If you ever have an opportunity to take a class with him do it!!!

analysis.name: Anna Curtis
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 202 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I am not joking when I say she is likely the worst professor in the chemistry department. During her lectures, she repeats the same idea numerous times and takes forever to finish simple problems that anyone in the class would understand. If you are taking Chem102, take it with any other professor who doesn't waste their students' time.

If you are a pre-med and thought this course was difficult, you should take a step back and reconsider your long-term goals. This class is by far one of the easiest STEM classes you will take. If you got anything below a B+ and are not 100% sure if becoming a doctor is what you want to do, drop medicine now. It is easier to pivot early on.

Prof Curtis is a great lecturer! She is engaging and kind. When she explains things she shows her thought process so you get a better idea of how to approach the problems. An A is achievable if you put in the effort.
My advice:
1) Read chapters to understand, and put what you're learning in the context of what you already know
2) Go to CHEMPossible

I would say Anna Curtis is one of the best Chem 101 lecturers. She seems to really care about the subject matter and is enthusiastic while teaching, without being too overboard. Although chem 101 is a flipped classroom format which can be somewhat difficult, I feel like she addresses all difficult content and allows time for questions always.

I had her class in Spring 2025. She was a fine chemistry teacher, and she is definitely passionate about her job. I didn't really find her inspiring, and some days she could go from being the sweetest lady to quite snarky. The chemistry department is also just tough. Self study and practice is super necessary, but take with her if you can!

analysis.name: Cynthia Radding
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Required course for LTAM majors. Most of the class agree seems she just leaves us to teach. Discussion based on reading, be sure to give specific examples from text ( what was said on page __, etc). Only grades are attendance/participation, group project, & 20 page final. Very tough grader & dry. Uncomfortable silences. But is for student success.

Very very boring class. The material is extremely interesting but the lectures are very dry and just not fun to go to. They are mandatory and the recitation section is better but still like pulling teeth. The exams are in a nice format and if you study you will do well. Do not know if it is worth it though.

This is a good class if you show up most of the time and take notes. You can download the power points and use them to study along with the study guides that she gives for the midterm and final, which are not too hard and graded very fairly. She wants you to do well and isvery flexible, even let me re-take the midterm so I could get a better grade.

Her lectures are super hard to follow she usually just talks without stopping and has powerpoints with like 4 words per slide so if you dont get it when she says it, you will not get it ever. The good thing is that she gives you everything that's going to be on the test so if you study it you can get a solid grade. She is a very sweet lady

Every class for the entire class, she is talking at us, many times reading directly from a paper she had wrote on the topic in preparation for the class. Thankful for the powerpoint. The lectures were extremely boring. I learned more from doing the readings than from going to class. I would not take this professor again.

analysis.name: Cynthi Schauer
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I really think that Dr. Schauer is a smart woman, but she just has trouble explaining what's going on in her head. She gets tongue-twisted easily and ends up circling everything on the notes, so you really don't know what's important. Tests are too long for the time allotted. Her accent can be pretty amusing - she pronounces anions "EAN-iens."

The first two weeks a class she spent the whole class period trying to figure out how the projector worked, no lie. Bad at explaining things, textbook is useless, other than the useless textbook assigned questions, no other study material is provided. Clicker questions are nothing like the test. Practice exam is way shorter than the real exam.

She explains material in a nice simple holistic fashion in class, but then expects you memorize every single diagram and obscure calculation she ever mentioned for the test. The tests are too long, and though curved they are just too hard compared to the rest of the course material.

Worst teacher I've taken in the chem department. Awful, point blank. Takes forever on the easy concepts and can't explain the more difficult ones. Tests are stupid and it's often unclear what the question is asking. Very unfortunate that they don't find a replacement for her.

Dr. Schauer is not an effective lecturer. Your TAs are your best resource for information. Recitations for this class consist of students working on other classwork or websurfing while Schauer talks in circles. There are poll everywhere questions every lecture, otherwise everyone would skip. Students and TAs alike think she is very disorganized.

analysis.name: Cynthia Demetriou
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is amazing. By far the very best teacher I have ever had. He style of teaching is remarkable. She's clear in everything she says, upbeat, funny, and motivating. Inclusive of all students. Just the absolute best. I highly recommend her.

Among the best teachers I've had. Her style is remarkable. She's able to efficiently guide discussions, keep students interested, and she is clear in her instruction and expectations. She tests and grades fairly as well. I highly recommend her.
Junior Transfer Seminar is a pretty easy A. There is a presentation and 10 page paper at the end of the semester, but it really is not difficult. She is easy to get in contact with and REALLY nice.
Cynthia is a wonderful professor. I took her junior transfer seminar course and enjoyed it.

analysis.name: Cynthia Sturton
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This is the worst COMP Class I have taken to date. Lectures are irrelevant to the LABS and there is little direction and guidance given. LABS are released late and then she doesn't accept late work. The reverse classroom is lazy teaching, Youtube teaches better than this professor. Be prepared to pay the school to teach yourself in this class.

Please do not take this class with her. Every time I step into this class, I fear something terrible might happen. Her lecture slides have less detailing and poor formatting, and it's a matter of whether you know the content or not. The labs are sometimes lengthy; only OH can save you on that. Other than that, please refrain yourself from this.

Cynthia seems like a nice person but is a terrible prof. The way she ran this class was disrespectful and unacceptable imo. She wouldn't accept any late work but would routinely release lecture videos and grades late. The labs (40% of grade) were also such a stretch from the class content and were the bane of my existence. Do not take this class :(

New labs are extremely difficult, time-consuming and the lectures are not very helpful. Sturton is not accommodating: when 50 people requested extension on a lab it wasn't provided. Mandatory videos, which are 40-80 mins long, are uploaded late in evening and you need to know the material for the quiz next morning. This is very bad class, avoid it

Idk what happened to this class but it is absolutely terrible. Irrelevant, harshly graded, and very difficult lab assignments. Everything in this class is graded insanely, including something as small as a project outline. Sturton is disorganized. Seriously don't take this class. My grade is sitting around a B and I've put way too much work in.

analysis.name: Oskar Czendze
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took HIST 153 with Professor Czendze, however, that was not an option to select. He is one of the most genuine professors and often brought candy to class for us :) There is a midterm early in the semester, a final, and a 1-2 page paper due roughly every other week. Take notes, pay attention to lectures, and do the readings - you'll be fine!

I took hist 153 with him but that wasn't an option to select -- great teacher, very knowledgeable and I really learned a lot. Definitely a lot of readings but its easy to get by with just skimming right before class. Pay attention in lecture too. One midterm, final paper, final exam, and ~6 mini papers throughout the semester based on readings.

Prof. Czendze is a very thoughtful and kind professor. I took "Holocaust Remembrance" with him which was fascinating. He encouraged lots of student participation while still guiding the discussion. The readings WERE a bit heavy at times, but they were genuinely interesting. If you at least skim and think about them, you'll be alright.
I took Hist 153, but it wasn't an option! it was a very interesting class, but there was just too much reading. nearly impossible to read before every class

analysis.name: Daniele Meregalli
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He's very encouraging with students in class. He teaches by the book, so as long as you do the readings, participate in class activities, and ask questions, he's a great professor. He encourages students to take advantage of office hours, the Italian conversation table, and the Italian film festival just to get involved in the language community.

***This is for Ital 333. Daniele is a great professor! He is kind, understanding, and wants you to succeed. Participation, a presentation, 2 film reviews, and final paper a exam make up your grade. It was a lot of writing, but you could choose what films to write about. Take this class if you're interested in film/Italian culture, I learned a lot!

He's so kind and wants you to succeed. ITAL401 is an accelerated class designed for students with experience in romance languages. He was accessible and understood that sometimes life happens. Daniele is there to help. Just ask. He's approachable and funny. He'd explain harder grammar concepts with their equivalents in French or Spanish to help.

I had so much fun in this class! The professor is always willing to help and you learn so fast. He can be a tough grader sometimes but if you put in the work you can easily get an A. As in every language class participation is key, and there is a lot of homework because you cover 101 and 102 in one semester–but he made it super enjoyable!

Hated this class so so much. He talks very quickly so half the time I had no clue what was going on and he grades incredibly harshly. He expects us to know words he's never taught. He's a reasonable person in terms of needed extensions though. He picks on people constantly which is horrid when you're clueless as to what he's talking about.

analysis.name: Lightning Czabovsky
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: MEJO341 is a boring class but Lightning made it so much fun! There's no homework, and quizzes and exams are fairly easy, just be prepared to read. Only downside is it's an 8 AM but it lowkey doesn't feel like that sometimes (+ attendance technically isn't mandatory, he does give extra credits if you come though).

Lightning is the best! Goes out of the way to be accessible during office hours and help with assignments as much as you need. Gives great lectures as well and is very engaging. I wish I could take more classes with him, he's one of the best Hussman professors I've had.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER! Media Law is not the easiest class, but Lightning makes it so much better. Three exams + five quizzes + participation. As long as you do your readings, you'll be fine. He also curves the grade and offers extra credit, so don't worry if you didn't do well initially.

I've never rated a professor on here but I MUST rate Lightning. IF I COULD TAKE EVERY CLASS WITH HIM I WOULD. He makes the information so digestible, holds exam review sessions before each exam that basically tell you what to study and genuinely cares about the success of his students so. much. his dog Bert is adorable and he brings him to class.

I had the pleasure of taking Lightning for Mejo-341. He made law material understandable and digestible for someone who has no background knowledge of it. He had great communication, was open to questions, and quickly gave us our grades back. You can tell when someone is meant to be a professor---and Lightning is one of those gems!

analysis.name: David Pfennig
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: David is kind, funny, and passionate in his work and teachings. He is EXTREMELY fair in terms of recognizing fault; he eased up on our second exam after understanding what students didn't like from the first exam and offered extra credit. He's also very helpful outside of lecture to thoroughly explain topics that I didn't understand well in class.

Dr. Pfennig is an amazing professor. The class was amazing and very discussion based. The structure of the course was amazing for learning the material deeply. There was one presentation, a grant proposal, and a few weekly assignments. All were amazing and things I looked forward to completing. 100% recommend.

Great teacher and great class! graded by 4 things (HW, which is a 100, participation, a grant proposal, and a presentation you work on with a group). He gives you great feedback but also grades leniently. Highly reccommend!

Dr. Pfennig was fantastic, and the relaxed nature of this course really worked for me. There was a lot of reading, and everyone had to do multiple group presentations as well as a significant amount of individual/group writing, so the workload is somewhat high, but it seemed like the work was very applicable to what would be done as a scientist.

Great professor who made lectures incredibly enjoyable to attend. He is passionate about the topic and transfers that feeling to the class. Lecture slides contain the exact content you will be tested on. Only difficulty is the tests can be a time crunch, so you have to know your stuff.

analysis.name: Daniel Sands
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Engaging + enjoyable class and Prof. Sands is knowledgeable and impressive. The content was very interesting and useful beyond class. Biggest issue was unclear grading which caused unnecessary stress. Workload felt very heavy for a MOD class, but maybe that's not bad. He's new though so it may improve.

Professor Sands is a very chill professor and a fair grader. Class wasnt filled with busy work or unnecessary assignments. It was graded off a few things, mainly final presentation and report. No final exam either. Would definitely recommend to take 411 with him.
He is a chill guy but grades everything so harsh.

analysis.name: David Hatcher
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Hatch is amazing. He has no exams and very little readings/homework. Still, I learned a ton. His experience working for Duke Energy made his lectures especially interesting. He broke down big concepts in a great way, allowing me to understand concepts that I otherwise definitely wouldn't. Love him! Great guy, great teacher.

Professor Hatcher is the most caring professor you will find and wants you to come to him with questions and will always accommodate your needs. His class is mostly lectures which are sometimes hard to follow as there is not a clear outline of what the class is about. However there is very little work but a few group projects (graded fairly easy).

Highly recommend! Very easy course. Dr. Hatcher cares about his students and wants them to do well. Overall, I am not someone who cares about energy, but I learned a lot. He assigned 4 take-home assignments and 4 group projects + presentations. He definitely goes on tangents in his lectures, but participation matters in this class and was an easy A

Professor Hatcher is probably the most caring professor at UNC. Sweetest dude and really cares about what he is teaching. He is very accessible and is always willing to help! Highly recommend if you want an easy A and to have a professor who is willing to help you; classes are also very interesting.

307 is my first class at UNC that's actually an easy A. I learned a good bit and the class had zero pressure. Hatcher is great person and cares about teaching, the class is a little slow but I think it will continue to get better. He gives great feedback, no busy work and he just wants you to learn.

analysis.name: Dafna Kaufman
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Class is very easy with there being very little work besides the speeches.

Great professor, but an even better person. Made sure to connect to students while also delivering content for the class. Although this content could get a little confusing, the class isn't too tough as long as you show up and participate, would recommend.

Dafna is an amazing professor! I took COMM 140 with her (there's no option for 140 on rmp so i put down 120) & it was the easiest class I've ever taken. All her tests & exams are from her power points/lectures so you don't even need to read the textbook and she gives tons of extra credit opportunities. She's also such a sweetheart! V flexible too!

140. Absolutely loved this class!! If you are a communications major and have to take 140 as one of the three prerecs, Dafna is 100% the best choice! She lectures off of PowerPoints and posts them after every class and the class is split up evenly between PowerPoints , quizzes ( 5 short quizzes throughout the semester) and her midterm and final.

This relates to COMM 350. Dafna is the sweetest professor ever and she really cares about her students. The class is lecture only which can be boring at times-- the only critique I have for Dafna is to maybe make lectures more interactive and interesting. She covers material well, though, and I really enjoyed this class

analysis.name: Janitor Derek
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The original computa. Derek can do whatever you put your mind to. Congrats bud, you've been Derek'd
Every class he encouraged us to get "snug" with our classmates. He would then pretend to be a classmate.
Derek is just a stand up man. His lectures are VERY "hands-on" and I find you learn a lot that way. Highly recommend, but be prepared to "break a sweat" to get good grades in this class.
He really cooked my goose with his stiff grading system. However, his stiff grading system opened my eyes to the world of "responsible" "research".

analysis.name: Desire Kedagni
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The average on the final was a 72. He refuses to curve anything in the class. His actual teaching style was not terrible, and a lot of the exams reused questions from the problem sets, but the fact that he did not curve a single test with the justification of "if 4-5 people get an A, the grades work" was terrible. The average class grade was a C+.

I didn't like Econ 400, but Kedagni made me love econometrics! You have to go to class, since he takes attendance for a grade and includes concepts from lectures on exams. He's a chalkboard lecturer, which isn't everyone's cup of tea. My one gripe is that the midterms are way too long. However, their content isn't difficult. You just have to study.

Desire is a great professor and also a joy to talk to. He made econometrics enjoyable to learn and his problem sets, although somewhat challenging, are great review material. I would highly recommend you study and understand the problem sets and attend each class since he goes through important math proofs.

ECON 470 is very difficult, no matter who you take it with. Kedagni was a really nice guy, but resources were super limited outside of class. Thankfully, I passed/failed this course because the average on the final was a 70 with no curving whatsoever.
I took ECON 470 in fall 2023 and this course covers everything you need to know about linear regression. The pace of the class is very reasonable and Professor Kedagni's notes are easy to understand.

analysis.name: Pedro de Almeida
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took the first version of his FYS, so some disorganization could be expected. His lectures are intriguing, however, and the course taught me a lot even though I am not a language major. He is caring and not a tough grader as long as you participate and make an effort to stay engaged in class.

Was surprised at the one 3-star review. All languages classes are flipped at UNC, and you are not going to find a calmer-paced learning schedule than any of UNC's Portuguese classes.

Pedro is an excellent prof. You NEED to look at the vocab before each class, but it's a very reasonable amount of content. Lots of participation which truly helps.

*PORT 203*
I had Pedro for both 102 and 203, and both semesters he helped a lot with learning. He is very passionate about us learning the language, and grades fairly if you at least attempt to speak and write in  portuguese. He relies a lot on participation in class, but will still take the time to explain confusing concepts.

pedro relies heavily on the flipped format for learning, so if you struggle with learning on your own with the textbook, be sure to visit office hours for questions! however, he is available during class times for you to ask questions, he regularly asks if there are concepts you don't understand, and takes the time to explain in depth.

analysis.name: Katie Deaven
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class has readings, an essay, and presentation projects. Katie clearly cares about making the class interesting and informative. Grading is quite fair but the class still requires work and office hours are helpful. A lot of the work for the class comes later in the semester, so be prepared for the workload at the end.

Participation heavy. Readings are due each class, they tend to get a little long. Deadlines shift around often which may seem good at first glance, but it does get frustrating if you have a job and are calling out for important dates (presentations and such). Set up meetings in advance because office hours fill up!

I really enjoyed her teaching honestly, very enjoyable and the way that she would make the content was engaging. I would say that there was a lot of reading at times even though she tried to get the readings as short as possible. She's very engaged and passionate about the material and wants us to do the best we can in the class.

You can tell she's very passionate about what she teaches and only wants you to succeed. If you put in the work and listen in class then you'll be fine. I will say that it is homework heavy, so a good amount of readings that can be quite difficult to understand.

This is for 102 but there wasn't an option. Katie is very kind, accessible, and fun in class. Heavy emphasis on classroom discussion and participation. Easy to get B+/A-, not an easy A due to lots of reading and high expectations for understanding. I really loved this class and feel like I learned a lot about philosophy and good communication!

analysis.name: Dharini  Bathia
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I don't have any issue with heavy accents but on top of that her PowerPoints don't outline anything. They have just questions without answers, and you have to try to decipher what she is saying with no visual aid. I am a visual learner, and not having the notes in writing on the PowerPoints in class made this class pretty much impossible.

Worst professor I've had. The class is easy, but she is very rude to students. Interrupted student presentations and was passive aggressive when the class expressed concerns about an unfair exam. You can do just fine in the class, but if there are other options for 581, I would absolutely avoid her. She's new to teaching so hopefully she improves.

Worst class I've taken in PLCY dept. Completely unclear grading criteria, awful instructions: 1 Q on midterm was only answered correctly by 1 person in the whole class and she said she "taught it well enough." Very rude, does not treat students with respect. Sure, I did learn something useful, but the environment was not supportive whatsoever.

Definitely the worst professor I have had at UNC. She seems aggravated when students ask questions or give answers (whether their answers are right or wrong). Her instructions for assignments are confusing, with no rubrics and inconsistent deadlines. The exams are graded very harshly and she takes points off even if you are correct.

Don't take this class. Bathia would contradict her own syllabus and get mad when students were confused. Harshest grading I've experienced in the PLCY department; the midterm average was in the 60s. She does not respond well to student questions or feedback. Overall, it's not a very welcoming learning environment.

analysis.name: Diane Kelly
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It was incredibly frustrating. I've never encountered such a ruthless professor at UNC. You can't get a good grade even though u put efforts already. She spent so much time on formalism that I felt like I wasn't learning anything useful. This class is incredibly difficult for an prerequisite, totally disaster
